# Manager, agents and ui split -- Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Replace `cmd/clustarr` and its six per-service processes with one leader-elected `cmd/manager` that runs every reconciler, one `cmd/agent --domain <d>` process per worker domain (autoscaled by HPAs the manager owns, without KEDA), a static `cmd/ui`, and the renamed `cmd/markers` and `cmd/transcode`. Probing, segment decoding, subtitle extraction and par2 repair all run in-process on ffgo and par2go, never as external programs.

**Architecture:** Each service splits into an exported manager-side registration package (`app/<svc>/manager`) and agent-side domain packages (`app/<svc>/agent/...`) over leaf extractions, so per-binary `go list -deps` guards keep the static manager and ui free of worker, client, sqlite, torrent, usenet and FFmpeg code, while the native agent, markers and transcode binaries load FFmpeg 9 through the ffgo fork and par2 through par2go in a re-exec'd child. The manager is the only writer of resource status and the only process that ensures the NATS topology: MediaFile probes become queued work that the import domain answers into a KV record (R3), indexarr splits into a manager half and an index agent with its own client cache and a compare-and-swap session store (R8), and consumers bind, never create, their durables, with per-pod slots under a topology-owned `MaxAckPending` (R5). Two images replace the old set (`clustarr` for manager and ui, the FROM-scratch `native` for everything that loads FFmpeg), the chart and kustomize render one Deployment per agent domain whose HPA the manager's autoscale reconciler owns behind its own External Metrics API, and `cmd/clustarr` and the six `app/<svc>` root packages are deleted.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.27 (module `github.com/mediactl/clustarr`), controller-runtime v0.25.1 on Kubernetes 1.37 (envtest 1.37.0, controller-gen v0.22.0), NATS JetStream (nats.go v1.53.1, nats-server v2.15.0), cobra and pflag, testify, the ffgo fork (`github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo`, fork tag `v0.0.0-clustarr.13`) on FFmpeg 9 through purego v0.11.1, par2go `v0.1.0` (`159eebd`: `1bd94eb`'s Go API, ABI 2; `libpar2shim.so`, par2cmdline-turbo), ONNX Runtime through onnxruntime-purego, `k8s.io/component-helpers` v0.37.0, autoscaling/v2 HPAs with a hand-rolled `external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1` server, Helm and kustomize, Docker BuildKit named build contexts, golangci-lint v2 (gofumpt, goimports, forbidigo).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-manager-agent-split-design.md`. Read §1 and §2 (the request and rulings R1-R14), the header's **Adoption** and **Drift since the review** paragraphs, and each section a wave cites before starting that wave. The spec is about 6,800 lines: read the cited sections in full and `grep -n '^#'` for the rest. Every owner decision in §13 is taken at its recommendation except OD18 and OD23, which stay with the owner; OD19 is resolved (par2go `v0.1.0`, published 2026-10-06; upgrade guide U1), and W0.26 records that in the spec.

## Global Constraints

- **Branch hygiene (R14).** Work only in `/home/appkins/src/mediactl/clustarr-unify`, on branch `unify-manager-agent`. Basis: main `0d3ae234` plus two branch commits, found by subject: the spec commit (`docs(spec): manager, agents and ui …`, `4b103429` before the rebase) and `docs(adr): ADR-0016 -- per-file work is MediaFile status …`. Main's commits since `cdbdd870` that tasks touch are listed under **Rebasing**. ADR-0016 (Accepted) folds SubtitleRequest, TranscodeJob and AudioGraft into MediaFile status. This plan still registers their reconcilers and does not implement that ADR; the owner confirms the order. Because ADR-0016 is taken, this plan's manager/agents ADR is **ADR-0018** (`docs/adr/0018-manager-agents-and-ui.md`, W10.2), and W10.3's "no external media programs" keeps ADR-0017; the spec's §12, R11 and header say the same. Other sessions keep committing to main, so line numbers drift. Every task names its sites by symbol; verify each against the current tree before editing. Only the controlling session rebases onto local main, only between tasks with a clean worktree: before Wave 1 and W0.25, at W0.28 green (see **Rebasing** under Execution order), and again before handing back. Tasks never rebase, merge, fetch, reset or stash.
- **Commits are path-scoped.** Run `git add <new files>`, then `git commit -m '<conventional message>' -- <every path, old and new>`. A `git mv` stages both paths, so the pathspec names both. Never `git add -A`. Never `git stash`: it is process-global and has swept other agents' work. Never `git reset --hard` and never `git push`. Find commits by subject (`git log --grep`), never by a SHA from a report.
- **go.mod.** Exactly three edits, W0.25, W0.26 and W0.27, made serially by the controlling session with `go mod edit`, plus `go mod download <module>@<version>` for one named module. Never `go get`, never `go mod tidy`, and never a persistent `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod`. The only exception is the one-command inline `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go list` that W0.26 and W0.27 each run once to record `go.sum` lines. No other task adds or removes a module. A task that seems to need one stops and reports.
- **The forks.** ffgo changes only in the worktree `/home/appkins/src/mediactl/ffgo-unify`, on branch `clustarr/unify-media` (cut from `v0.0.0-clustarr.12`, which is `a184557`, the tag main's go.mod pins since `ebbb2322`, `build: ffgo v0.0.0-clustarr.12 …`), and is tagged locally as `v0.0.0-clustarr.13`. The spec still names the fork tag `.12` and its base `.11` (§7.4, §7.5, §10.1.6, A35): read `.13` and `.12` there. `../ffgo` is never edited and nothing is fetched into it. par2go is **published** (owner, 2026-10-06; main's `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-06-unify-media-upgrade-guide.md` U1, OD19 resolved): go.mod requires `github.com/mediactl/par2go v0.1.0` (commit `159eebd`: the spec basis `1bd94eb`'s Go API and ABI 2) with **no replace**, and every `libpar2shim.so` (the native image, `make native-assets`) is the `v0.1.0` release asset `libpar2shim-linux-<arch>.so`, checked against `hack/par2go/SHA256SUMS` (W0.24). Nothing exports or builds par2go, and `../par2go` is never edited. go.mod replaces only `github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo => ../ffgo-unify`, until the owner grants OD18.
  - Never push the ffgo branch or tag. A `git push --tags` run anywhere in that repository publishes `.13`.
  - Never report upstream (OD23).
  - ffgo files keep ffgo's conventions: Apache-2.0, no licence header, plain `testing`.
- **No ffmpeg or ffprobe in tests (owner, 2026-10-06; upgrade guide U2).** No test may run the `ffmpeg` or `ffprobe` CLI, directly or through a helper. Clips come from `internal/testmedia` (W6.18), which writes them on ffgo, or are the committed files under `test/data/media-goldens/clips` (W6.23). Every parity check of an R2 step compares with the goldens W6.23 recorded from the exec implementation before it was deleted, never with a live CLI. A task written before this rule whose text runs `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` in a test carries a **U2 amendment** at its top, and the amendment overrides the task's text. `TestNoGoFileRunsFFmpeg` (W10.9) holds the rule over every `.go` file, tests, `test/` and `hack/` included. The `par2` CLI may still create PAR2 test sets (OD26; guide U2.5).
- **Only the FFmpeg libraries ffgo loads (owner; guide U3).** The native image stages exactly `libavutil`, `libavcodec`, `libavformat`, `libavfilter`, `libavdevice`, `libswscale` and `libswresample` (with their soname links) plus `libffshim.so`, and no FFmpeg `bin/` (W6.5, W6.6).
- **Build, don't deploy.** Image builds are expected from Wave 6 on. Never `docker push`, never `kind load` into kind-cluster-plex, and never deploy anywhere without the owner's explicit OK.
- **New files.** Every new clustarr `.go` file starts with `hack/boilerplate.go.txt` verbatim (GPL-3.0), then a blank line, then `package`. The task snippets omit the header. New shell scripts start with `#!/usr/bin/env bash` and `set -euo pipefail`, and are `chmod +x`.
- **Formatting.** After every edit, run `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/gofumpt -w` and `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/goimports -local github.com/mediactl/clustarr -w` on the touched `.go` files. `make lint` runs both.
- **RBAC markers move with the code that needs the grant.** Any task that moves, adds or deletes a `+kubebuilder:rbac` marker or an API type runs `make generate manifests` and syncs the chart's copy of each changed role. Where the roles must not change, it proves that with `git diff --exit-code -- config/rbac charts/clustarr/templates/rbac.yaml`.
- **Test policy.**
  - After every task, `go build ./... && go vet ./...` is green, and so are the tests of every touched package.
  - Envtest packages run with `KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS="$(setup-envtest use 1.37.0 -p path)"`. Check `-v` for `SKIP`: a suite that finishes in milliseconds skipped.
  - Each wave's final gate task runs the full `make test` (envtest, `make pg-assets` and the chart dependency tarballs included) and `make lint`.
  - Run `helm dependency build charts/clustarr` once per worktree before any `cmd/clustarr` or `test/guards` test.
  - From Wave 6 on, `make test` also exports the native environment (`make native-assets`). A native test that reports SKIP under `$NATIVE` or `CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1` is a failure.
- **Guards.** Never weaken or delete a guard without a stated replacement, named in the task and in its commit message.
- **Names that never change (R7).** Field managers, NATS streams, durables, subjects, Msg-Ids, KV buckets, controller names, span names, metric names and label values, unless a task says otherwise and cites the spec.
- **Scratch files** go under the executing session's own scratchpad subdirectory, never into a repository.

## Review Focus

- Field ownership across the new process boundary. Over-claims are silent under forced apply. Assert `metadata.managedFields` by manager name, against an object that is already in its steady state: the session `Drop` CAS (W4.21), MediaFile status under the probe queue (W4.13), and the `DefaultFieldOwner` and the legacy-lease gate (W4.80, W4.81), and the three OD13 compare-and-swaps (W4.83-W4.85).
- Bus semantics change under every consumer:
  - `Subscribe` binds only and waits for a missing durable.
  - Pull is slot-gated, with lapse reclaim under a cap.
  - The topology owns `MaxAckPending`.

  A hung handler must still dead-letter on both buses. A test that hangs usually means a durable nobody bound (W4.42, W4.44, W4.45).
- A file whose bytes changed must never be read through a stale summary. Check the `judgeProbe` table rows (W4.11), the `ProbeCurrent` gates, AudioGraft's Succeeded phase (W4.14), and that a `ProbeVersion` raise re-probes without changing `probeHash`.
- Native media must match the programs it replaces. The probe prints what ffprobe prints, decoding is byte-for-byte equal to the `ffmpeg(1)` commands it replaces, and extraction equals `-c:s srt`, each judged against the goldens W6.23 recorded from those programs (no test runs them, U2). Watch two places in particular:
  - The FFmpeg 7.1 and 9 layout offsets that differ: `r_frame_rate` and `best_effort_timestamp` (Wave 0).
  - Abandoned calls, which must dead-letter rather than redeliver into another stuck call (W7.8, W8.3).
- Deleting `cmd/clustarr` must lose no guard. Check:
  - Every moved test keeps its intent: the exec guard, `TestTheWorkerNeverExecsFFmpeg`'s ban and the registration guards.
  - Each binary's `go list -deps` closure.
  - The generated roles, byte-identical where a task claims so.
  - The External Metrics server's authentication and TLS: 401 or 403 for an unauthenticated caller, and served before the caches sync (W4.68, W4.70).

- **Wave 1.** The `pkg/k8s` owner runs W1.2, then W1.4, then W1.5; W1.4 also waits for W1.3. W1.1, W1.3 and W1.6-W1.10 are independent lanes. W1.11 runs last.
- **Wave 2a.** Serial, W2.1 to W2.12. The tasks share `app/catalog/run.go`, `wiring.go` and `markers/handler.go`.
- **Wave 2b.**
  - The import chain W2.20-W2.24 runs in order, and so does the indexer chain W2.25-W2.28.
  - W2.29 and W2.31 are independent of each other and of both chains.
  - W2.30 runs after W2.23 has committed (and may run beside W2.24 and the indexer chain). It edits
    `app/import/worker/rescan/{keptoutput.go,orphanpart.go,keptoutput_test.go,orphanpart_internal_test.go}`,
    and W2.20, W2.21 and W2.23 commit the whole `app/import/worker/rescan` directory: run beside
    them, one of those commits would take W2.30's uncommitted rescan edits.
  - W2.32 runs last. It may fold into W2.12 when that gate runs after both halves.
- **Wave 3.** W3.1 to W3.5 run in order. Then the catalog chain W3.6, W3.7, W3.8 runs serially on `app/catalog/run.go`. W3.9 to W3.13 own one service each and may run in parallel after W3.5; only W3.11 edits the `Makefile`. W3.14, then W3.15.
- **Wave 4a.**
  - W4.1 (lane A); W4.2, then W4.3, then W4.4 (lane B, `pkg/events`); W4.5 (C); W4.9 (D); W4.10 (E).
  - W4.6 waits for W4.1, W4.4 and W4.5. W4.7 waits for W4.6, and W4.8 for W4.4.

W4.70 re-runs `make manifests` and the chart sync on top of W4.66's commit.

### Cross-wave interface gaps, and how this revision closes them

Found while assembling, then closed by the plan review of 2026-10-06. Where a gap is closed, the closing task or amendment is named; read that task, not this list, for the work.

1. **The writers section (§5.3.4, §5.3.5, §5.8, §5.15).** Closed by Wave 4e and W5.19:
   - `k8s.DefaultFieldOwner` (§5.3.5, OD4): W4.80.
   - `k8s.GatedLeaseLock` / `k8s.NewGatedLeaseLock(cfg, namespace, id) (resourcelock.Interface, error)` and `TestGatedLeaseLockWaitsForLegacyLeases` (§5.8, OD6): W4.81.
   - `PatchOverlay`'s compare-and-swap (§5.3.4): W4.82.
   - `TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome` (§5.15): W5.19, after W5.17, since it needs `cmd/manager`, `cmd/ui`, `cmd/markers`, `cmd/transcode` and the eight domain packages as roots.
2. **`Checks.Merge` is produced twice.** Closed: W3.1 produces `(*k8s.Checks).Merge`; W5.3 produces only `AgentManagerOptions`, and W5.9 consumes `Merge` from W3.1.
3. **Import option names.** Closed: W5.7 builds `importmanager.Options{Options, TraktBaseURL}` (W3.9 defines no `DataPath`), and W5.9 sets `importagent.Options.DataDir`.
4. **The engines' `Client`.** Closed in W5.9: both engine registrations pass `Client: engineClient(o.Engine)` (app/grab's `splitEngineIdentity`, moved there because W5.17 deletes the shim), held by `TestEngineClientSplitsAtTheLastHyphen`; W5.17's `split_test.go` row names it as the successor.
5. **The import probe's Prober injection (§6.6).** Closed by W4.86: `fileimport.NewWorker(c, bus, prober)` and `rescan.NewWorker(c, bus, prober)`, the heartbeat before the audio probe and `TestAnAudioProbeHeartbeatsAndIsBounded`. W8.6 then swaps only the prober's implementation, and W8.1's expectation (only `app/import/agent` names `ffprobeexec`) holds.
6. **`hack/deps` component-helpers entries.** Closed: W4.64 deletes them once `app/autoscale/controller` imports the two packages.
7. **The DLQ projector's `mediafiles` grant.** Closed in W4.3: the projector's marker gains `mediafiles` `patch`, and `TestTheProjectorMayPatchEveryKindAResolverNames` holds every resolvable kind.
8. **Who raises the probe consumers' `MaxAckPending` to 32.** Closed: W4.2 (after W4.40) creates both lanes with `Slots: 4, MaxAckPending: 4`, and W4.63 raises them to `Slots × AutoscaleReplicaCeiling` (32) in `pkg/events/probe.go`, which `TestAutoscaledConsumersSizeMaxAckPendingForTheCeiling` holds. Expect 4 until W4.63.
9. **Per-package deps guards.** Wave 2b's per-package deps guards (and Wave 1's) stay, and stay green; folding them into `test/guards` is listed under **Plan review notes** at the end.

## Wave 0: the ffgo fork, par2go and go.mod (W0.1 to W0.30)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-manager-agent-split-design.md` §7.5
(the unified F1-F17 table and the F10 internals), §6.4 (the probe's fields and
its three ffgo tests), §7.3 (what F10 serves), §7.6 (consuming the fork and
par2go before their tags are pushed), §8.3, §8.10, §8.11 (par2go), §9.5
(`k8s.io/component-helpers v0.37.0`), §11.1 steps 0a-0c, §13 OD18/OD19.
Verified on 2026-10-06 against the worktree at `4b103429` (local main
`cdbdd870` plus the spec commit), ffgo master `a184557`
(= `v0.0.0-clustarr.12`, a lightweight tag that main's MP4-standard work
published after this plan was first written; `.11` is `9f7a3a4`, and `.12`
adds only Go code to it: `NewPacketFromData`, `Packet.Data` and the
codec_id/extradata setters, no shim change), and par2go, whose `main` is now
`159eebd`, one commit past the basis `1bd94eb`.

### What this wave does

1. **ffgo (W0.1 to W0.23).** A new git worktree of
   `/home/appkins/src/mediactl/ffgo` at `/home/appkins/src/mediactl/ffgo-unify`
   on a new branch `clustarr/unify-media`, from tag `v0.0.0-clustarr.12`. One
   commit per addition, F12 first (it sets `FFSHIM_API_VERSION 1`, which
   covers every later shim change in this tag), then the table's order. At
   the end W0.23 rebuilds and checks the prebuilt shim (F14), runs ffgo's
   whole suite, and creates the **local** annotated tag `v0.0.0-clustarr.13`.
   Nothing is pushed (OD18). `../ffgo` itself is never edited: other sessions
   work there.
2. **par2go (W0.24).** par2go is published (owner, 2026-10-06; upgrade guide
   U1, OD19 resolved): tag `v0.1.0` (`159eebd`, the basis `1bd94eb`'s Go API,
   ABI 2 and patches) with release assets `libpar2shim-linux-{amd64,arm64}.so`
   and `SHA256SUMS`. W0.24 checks the release against the owner's two digests
   and commits them as `hack/par2go/SHA256SUMS`. Nothing exports or builds
   par2go, and `/home/appkins/src/mediactl/par2go` is never edited.
3. **go.mod (W0.25 to W0.27)**, serially, by the controlling session only:
   the ffgo replace, the par2go `v0.1.0` require (no replace), and
   `k8s.io/component-helpers v0.37.0`. W0.28 is the wave gate (`make test`).
4. **testmedia's ffgo needs (W0.29, W0.30, upgrade guide U2.2)**, after W0.22
   and before W0.23 tags: subtitle-stream muxing, and a round-trip test of the
   lavfi sources, HDR10 side data, AC-3 options, chapters and tags that
   `internal/testmedia` (W6.18) writes clips with instead of the ffmpeg CLI.

### Deviations from the spec's paths (later waves must follow them)

- go.mod says `replace github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo => ../ffgo-unify`, not
  `../ffgo` (§7.6 item 1). Inside a Docker build stage whose WORKDIR is `/src`,
  that resolves to `/ffgo-unify`. So the images wave must write
  `COPY --from=ffgo / /ffgo-unify/` (§7.6 item 2 says `/ffgo/`), the Makefile's
  `FFGO_DIR ?= ../ffgo-unify`, and `LOCAL_CONTEXTS`' `grep -qE` pattern must
  match `=> \.\./ffgo-unify$` (§10.1.6).
- **par2go has no replace, no named context and no local build** (U1): §7.6
  item 1's par2go replace, items 2-3's `par2go` stage, context and `PAR2GO_REF`
  export, and §10.1.3/§10.1.6's builds of `shim/build.sh` are replaced by the
  `v0.1.0` module and its release assets, checked against
  `hack/par2go/SHA256SUMS`. The tasks that would have built them carry **U1
  amendments**.

### Rules for this wave (beside the plan's global rules)

- **ffgo conventions.** Files in ffgo keep ffgo's own conventions: the first
  line is `//go:build !ios && !android && (amd64 || arm64)`, there is no
  licence header (ffgo is Apache-2.0), tests use plain `testing` (ffgo's
  go.mod has no testify and must not gain one), and commit subjects are
  `feat:`/`fix:` with a `--` explanation. ffgo's go.mod is not edited. The GPL
  header rule applies only to clustarr files. The one clustarr Go file this
  wave edits, `hack/deps/deps.go`, already carries the header.
- **Every ffgo test command sets `FFGO_SHIM_DIR`** to the worktree's
  `shim/prebuilt/linux-amd64`, so the shim under test is the one just
  rebuilt, never a stale copy in a system directory.
- **Every task that changes `shim/ffshim.c` or `shim/ffshim.h` rebuilds** with
  `/home/appkins/src/mediactl/ffgo-unify/shim/build.sh prebuilt` (pkg-config
  resolves the host's FFmpeg 9.0.1 headers). It commits
  `shim/prebuilt/linux-amd64/libffshim.so` in the same commit, as `9c292f0`
  did. Only linux-amd64 is rebuilt. The other prebuilt shims stay at the base tag's
  (`.12`'s, which are `.11`'s: `.12` changed no shim).
  They lack every new symbol, so `ShimAPIVersion()` reports 0 for them, and
  the native image compiles its own shim from the fork's `shim/ffshim.c`
  (§7.6 item 2).
- **`FFSHIM_API_VERSION` stays 1** for the whole branch. Every function and
  layout field this wave adds ships in the first versioned shim (§7.5:
  "`MinShimAPI` stays 1").
- **New layout entries.** Each new struct read is an `FFSHIM_FIELD` entry with
  a `layout.Offset` Go fallback. The Go value is FFmpeg 7.1's, as §7.5 asks.
  The values below were derived from the 7.1 headers' field order and checked
  on this host: the AVCodecParameters, AVStream prefix and AVInputFormat
  values equal FFmpeg 9's, compiled with `offsetof` against `/usr/include`.
  The two exceptions are `AVStream.r_frame_rate` (7.1: 216, 9: 204) and
  `AVFrame.best_effort_timestamp` (7.1: 320, 9: 304). For those two,
  `TestEveryOffsetIsKnownToTheHeaders` logs a difference and does not fail.
  The shim's value is always the one used on FFmpeg 9.
- **Baseline.** W0.1 records ffgo's suite result before any change. No task
  may add a failing or newly skipped test to it.
- **go.mod.** Only the controlling session edits go.mod, one task at a time.
  The commands are `go mod edit`, plus `go mod download <module>@<version>`
  for one named module. `go get` and `go mod tidy` are forbidden. Missing
  `go.sum` lines are recorded by one inline
  `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go list ... >/dev/null` in the task that needs them, and
  the task then diffs go.mod. **Never** set `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod` persistently
  (`go env -w`, a shell profile, a Makefile) or in a parallel agent: under it
  any `go build` may rewrite go.mod.
- **Commits** are path-scoped (`git -C <repo> commit -m … -- <paths>`). Never
  `git stash`, never push, never `git fetch` into `../ffgo` (it rewrites
  shared refs). `git ls-remote` is the only network read of a remote.
- `SCRATCH` below is the executing session's scratchpad directory. Scratch
  files go under `$SCRATCH/w0/`, never into a repository.

### Order and parallelism

| Tasks | Depends on | Runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W0.1 | — | first |
| W0.2 to W0.22, then W0.29, W0.30, then W0.23 | W0.1, each on the previous | serially, one owner (they share `ffgo.go`, `decoder.go`, `muxer.go`, `filter_graph.go`, `shim/ffshim.c` and the prebuilt `.so`) |

| W0.26 | W0.24, W0.25 | controlling session, after W0.25 |
| W0.27 | W0.26 | controlling session, network once |
| W0.28 | W0.25 to W0.27 | gate |

**First consumers.** These tasks land in Wave 0. Each changes no linked code
until a later task imports it:

```c
/* Raised whenever the shim gains a function or a layout-table field, so Go
```

```go
// APIVersion is the loaded shim's FFSHIM_API_VERSION: 0 without a shim, or
// with one built before ffshim_api_version existed.
func APIVersion() int {
	if !loaded || shimAPIVersion == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return int(shimAPIVersion())
}
```

In `ffgo.go`, after `Version`:

```go
// ShimAPIVersion is the loaded ffshim's FFSHIM_API_VERSION: 0 without a shim
// or with one older than v0.0.0-clustarr.13. Code that reads FFmpeg 9 structs
// through the shim refuses a version below the one it was written for.
func ShimAPIVersion() int {
	_ = shim.Load()
	return shim.APIVersion()
}
```

### Task W0.3: F13: the log callback drops lines above `av_log_get_level()`

**Spec:** §7.5 F13, §7.1 fact 7, §7.4 (logging)
**Files:**
- Modify: `/home/appkins/src/mediactl/ffgo-unify/shim/ffshim.c` (`internal_log_callback`), `shim/prebuilt/linux-amd64/libffshim.so`
- Create: `log_level_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: W0.2's shim.
- Produces: behaviour only. A callback set with `ffgo.SetLogCallback` now
  receives only lines at or below the level set with `ffgo.SetLogLevel` (the
  default is INFO). clustarr's `pkg/transcode/engine/logtail.go` already drops
  lines above WARNING itself, so its tails (graft runs included) do not change.
  `ffruntime.Load` calls `SetLogLevel(LogWarning)`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test.**

`log_level_test.go`:

```go
//go:build !ios && !android && (amd64 || arm64)

package ffgo

import (
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/internal/shim"
)

// av_log hands every line to a custom callback whatever its level (only
// av_log_default_callback filters), so before the shim filtered, every debug
// line cost a vsnprintf and a purego call.
func TestTheLogCallbackGetsOnlyLinesAtOrBelowTheLogLevel(t *testing.T) {
	requireShim(t)
	var mu sync.Mutex
	var got []string
	if err := SetLogCallback(func(_ LogLevel, msg string) {
		if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "ffgo-level-test ") {
			return
		}
		mu.Lock()
		got = append(got, msg)
		mu.Unlock()
	}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = SetLogCallback(nil)
		_ = SetLogLevel(LogInfo)
	})
	if err := SetLogLevel(LogWarning); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, l := range []LogLevel{LogDebug, LogVerbose, LogInfo, LogWarning, LogError} {
		if err := shim.Log(nil, int32(l), "ffgo-level-test "+l.String()); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	mu.Lock()
	defer mu.Unlock()
	if want := "ffgo-level-test warning,ffgo-level-test error"; strings.Join(got, ",") != want {
		t.Fatalf("callback got %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
```

`fork_helpers_test.go`:

```go
//go:build !ios && !android && (amd64 || arm64)

package ffgo

import (
	"errors"
	"io"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// gopClip is a 3 s, 25 fps H.264 clip (75 frames, an IDR every 25 frames
// and no other keyframe, B-frames, BT.709 limited range) with a 48 kHz AAC
// track, in a container of extension ext ("mkv" or "mp4").
func gopClip(t *testing.T, ext string) string {
	t.Helper()
	ffmpegOrSkip(t)
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "gop."+ext)
	run(t, "ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y",
		"-f", "lavfi", "-i", "testsrc2=size=160x90:rate=25:duration=3",
		"-f", "lavfi", "-i", "sine=frequency=440:duration=3:sample_rate=48000",
		"-map", "0", "-map", "1",
		"-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-bf", "3",
		"-x264-params", "keyint=25:min-keyint=25:scenecut=0", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
		"-colorspace", "bt709", "-color_primaries", "bt709", "-color_trc", "bt709", "-color_range", "tv",
		"-c:a", "aac", path)
	return path
}

// decodeStream feeds sd every packet of its stream from d, calls each for
// every decoded frame (borrowed: valid until each returns), and drains the
// decoder at end of file.
func decodeStream(t *testing.T, d *Decoder, sd *StreamDecoder, each func(Frame)) {
	t.Helper()
	drain := func() {
		for {
			f, err := sd.Receive()
			if errors.Is(err, ErrAgain) || errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
				return
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("receive: %v", err)
			}
			each(f)
		}
	}
	send := func(p *Packet) {
		for {
			err := sd.Send(p)
			if errors.Is(err, ErrAgain) {
				drain()
				continue
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("send: %v", err)
			}
			return
		}
	}
	for {
		p, err := d.ReadPacket()
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read: %v", err)
		}
		if p == nil {
			break
		}
		if p.StreamIndex() != sd.StreamIndex() {
			continue
		}
		send(p)
		drain()
	}
	send(nil)
	drain()
}
```

```go
// AVFMT_SEEK_TO_PTS: the demuxer seeks by presentation time.
const AVFMT_SEEK_TO_PTS = 0x4000000

// GetInputFormatFlags is an AVInputFormat's flags (AVFMT_*).
func GetInputFormatFlags(f InputFormat) int32 {
	if f == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return *(*int32)(unsafe.Pointer(uintptr(f) + offsetInputFormatFlags))
}
```

`decoder.go`, after `StartTime`:

```go
// SeekToPTS reports whether the input's demuxer seeks by presentation
// timestamps (AVFMT_SEEK_TO_PTS: mov/mp4 yes, Matroska no). ffmpeg(1) moves
// an -ss seek back by 3/23 s when it is false and a stream has a VideoDelay.
func (d *Decoder) SeekToPTS() bool {
	d.mu.Lock()
	defer d.mu.Unlock()
	if d.closed || d.formatCtx == nil {
		return false
	}
	return avformat.GetInputFormatFlags(avformat.GetInputFormat(d.formatCtx))&avformat.AVFMT_SEEK_TO_PTS != 0
}
```

```go
// AVDiscardAll is AVDISCARD_ALL: the demuxer drops every packet of the stream.
const AVDiscardAll int32 = 48

// GetStreamDiscard is an AVStream's discard level (AVDISCARD_*).
func GetStreamDiscard(stream Stream) int32 {
	if stream == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return *(*int32)(unsafe.Pointer(uintptr(stream) + offsetStreamDiscard))
}

// SetStreamDiscard sets an AVStream's discard level.
func SetStreamDiscard(stream Stream, v int32) {
	if stream == nil {
		return
	}
```

- `decoder.go`, after `SeekToPTS` (add `"fmt"` to the imports):

```go
// Discard makes the demuxer drop every stream's packets except keep's
// (AVStream.discard = AVDISCARD_ALL), as ffmpeg(1) does for the streams no
// output reads. ffmpeg(1) discards only after its -ss seek, so the seek's
// default-stream choice sees every stream: call Discard after seeking.
func (d *Decoder) Discard(keep ...int) error {
	d.mu.Lock()
	defer d.mu.Unlock()
	if d.closed || d.formatCtx == nil {
		return ErrClosed
	}
	n := avformat.GetNumStreams(d.formatCtx)
	kept := make(map[int]bool, len(keep))
	for _, k := range keep {
		if k < 0 || k >= n {
			return fmt.Errorf("ffgo: no stream %d", k)
		}
		kept[k] = true
	}
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		if !kept[i] {
			avformat.SetStreamDiscard(avformat.GetStream(d.formatCtx, i), avformat.AVDiscardAll)
		}
	}
	return nil
}
```

```go
var unspecifiedLayout = regexp.MustCompile(`^([0-9]+) channels$`)

// audioBufferArgs is abuffer's argument string, as fftools/ffmpeg_filter.c
// configure_input_audio_filter writes it: time_base when known, then the
// rate and format, then the layout -- channel_layout=<describe> for a known
// order, channels=N for an unspecified one.
func audioBufferArgs(cfg FilterGraphConfig) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	if cfg.TimeBase.Num != 0 && cfg.TimeBase.Den != 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "time_base=%d/%d:", cfg.TimeBase.Num, cfg.TimeBase.Den)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "sample_rate=%d:sample_fmt=%s:", cfg.SampleRate, getSampleFormatName(cfg.SampleFmt))
	switch m := unspecifiedLayout.FindStringSubmatch(cfg.Layout); {
	case m != nil:
		b.WriteString("channels=" + m[1])
	case cfg.Layout != "":
		b.WriteString("channel_layout=" + cfg.Layout)
	default:
		b.WriteString("channel_layout=" + layoutForChannels(cfg.Channels))
	}
	return b.String()
}

// layoutForChannels is the layout ffgo always gave a bare channel count.
func layoutForChannels(n int) string {
	switch n {
	case 1:
		return "mono"
	case 6:
		return "5.1"
	case 8:
		return "7.1"
	default:
		return "stereo"
	}
}
```

```go
// videoBufferArgs is the buffer source's argument string.
func videoBufferArgs(cfg FilterGraphConfig) string {
	tb := cfg.TimeBase
	if tb.Num == 0 {
		tb = Rational{Num: 1, Den: 90000}
	}
	sar := cfg.SAR
	if sar.Num == 0 {
		sar = Rational{Num: 1, Den: 1}
	}
	args := fmt.Sprintf("video_size=%dx%d:pix_fmt=%d:time_base=%d/%d:pixel_aspect=%d/%d",
		cfg.Width, cfg.Height, int(cfg.PixelFmt), tb.Num, tb.Den, sar.Num, sar.Den)
	if cfg.ColorSpace != 0 || cfg.ColorRange != 0 {
		args += fmt.Sprintf(":colorspace=%d:range=%d", int(cfg.ColorSpace), int(cfg.ColorRange))
	}
	return args
}
```

```go
		{1000, 48000},

			t.Fatalf("frame %d: pts %d ms rescaled to %d, want %d", i, tc.in, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
	if last != 49024 {
		t.Errorf("last = %d after the jump, want 49024", last)
	}
	last = 0
	if got := RescaleDelta(sr, 1024, sr, 1024, &last, sr); got != 1024 || last != 2048 {
		t.Errorf("same time base: got %d, last %d; want 1024, 2048", got, last)
	}
```

`rescale.go`:

```go
//go:build !ios && !android && (amd64 || arm64)

package ffgo

import "github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/avutil"

// Rounding is FFmpeg's AVRounding.
type Rounding int32

const (
	RoundDown       Rounding = 2    // AV_ROUND_DOWN: toward -infinity
	RoundUp         Rounding = 3    // AV_ROUND_UP: toward +infinity
	RoundNearInf    Rounding = 5    // AV_ROUND_NEAR_INF: to nearest, halfway away from zero
	RoundPassMinMax Rounding = 8192 // AV_ROUND_PASS_MINMAX: INT64_MIN and INT64_MAX pass through unchanged
)

// RescaleQRnd is av_rescale_q_rnd: a in time base bq expressed in cq, through
// av_rescale_rnd (av_rescale_q_rnd takes AVRationals by value, which purego
// cannot pass on every platform).
func RescaleQRnd(a int64, bq, cq Rational, rnd Rounding) int64 {
	return avutil.RescaleRnd(a, int64(bq.Num)*int64(cq.Den), int64(cq.Num)*int64(bq.Den), int32(rnd))
}

// RescaleQ is av_rescale_q: RescaleQRnd with RoundNearInf.
func RescaleQ(a int64, bq, cq Rational) int64 { return RescaleQRnd(a, bq, cq, RoundNearInf) }

// RescaleDelta is av_rescale_delta (libavutil/mathematics.c), ported because
// it takes AVRationals by value: it rescales inTS from inTB to outTB keeping
// consecutive frames of duration samples (in fsTB) contiguous while the
// rounding allows, tracking the next expected timestamp in *last
// (avutil.NoPTSValue to start). ffmpeg(1)'s audio_ts_process uses it.
func RescaleDelta(inTB Rational, inTS int64, fsTB Rational, duration int, last *int64, outTB Rational) int64 {
	simple := func() int64 {
		*last = RescaleQ(inTS, inTB, fsTB) + int64(duration)
		return RescaleQ(inTS, inTB, outTB)
	}
	if *last == avutil.NoPTSValue || duration == 0 ||
		int64(inTB.Num)*int64(outTB.Den) <= int64(outTB.Num)*int64(inTB.Den) {
		return simple()
	}
	a := RescaleQRnd(2*inTS-1, inTB, fsTB, RoundDown) >> 1
	b := (RescaleQRnd(2*inTS+1, inTB, fsTB, RoundUp) + 1) >> 1
	if *last < 2*a-b || *last > 2*b-a {
		return simple()
	}
	this := min(max(*last, a), b) // av_clip64
	*last = this + int64(duration)
	return RescaleQ(this, fsTB, outTB)
}
```

```go
// srtFrame frames events as libavformat/srtenc.c writes them, with packet
// times in milliseconds (the srt muxer's time base): what

func srtFrame(evs []SubtitleEvent) []byte {
	var b bytes.Buffer
	us, ms := NewRational(1, 1000000), NewRational(1, 1000)
	n := 1
	for _, ev := range evs {
```

```c
/* Copies a decoder's subtitle_header (the ASS script header every FFmpeg
   text decoder emits) to an encoder, NUL-terminated as the ASS code needs
   (fftools/ffmpeg_enc.c enc_open). */
int ffshim_codecctx_copy_subtitle_header(void *dst, const void *src);
```

```c
int ffshim_codecctx_copy_subtitle_header(void *dst, const void *src) {
    AVCodecContext *d = dst;
    const AVCodecContext *s = src;
    av_freep(&d->subtitle_header);
    d->subtitle_header_size = 0;
    if (!s->subtitle_header)
        return 0;
    d->subtitle_header = av_mallocz(s->subtitle_header_size + 1);
    if (!d->subtitle_header)
        return AVERROR(ENOMEM);
    memcpy(d->subtitle_header, s->subtitle_header, s->subtitle_header_size);
    d->subtitle_header_size = s->subtitle_header_size;
    return 0;
}
```

```go
// CodecCtxCopySubtitleHeader copies a decoder's subtitle_header to an
// encoder; it returns the AVERROR code, ENOSYS without the shim.
func CodecCtxCopySubtitleHeader(dst, src unsafe.Pointer) int32 {
	if !loaded || shimCodecCtxCopySubtitleHeader == nil {

	}
```

`subtitle_transcoder.go`:

```go
//go:build !ios && !android && (amd64 || arm64)

package ffgo

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"sync"
	"unsafe"

	"github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/avcodec"
	"github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/avformat"
	"github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/avutil"
	"github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/internal/shim"
)

var (
	// ErrSubtitleDecode wraps a packet the subtitle decoder refused; ffmpeg(1)
	// logs it and goes on (ffmpeg_dec.c), so a caller can skip the packet.
	ErrSubtitleDecode = errors.New("ffgo: subtitle decode failed")
	// ErrSubtitleEncode wraps an encoder failure, which ffmpeg(1) treats as fatal.
	ErrSubtitleEncode = errors.New("ffgo: subtitle encode failed")
)

// SubtitleEvent is one encoded subtitle: PTS and Duration in microseconds
// (AV_TIME_BASE), Data the encoder's output.
type SubtitleEvent struct {
	PTS      int64
	Duration int64
	Data     []byte
}

const (
	subtitleOutMax     = 1 << 20 // fftools/ffmpeg_enc.c subtitle_out_max_size
	subtitleStructSize = 32      // sizeof(AVSubtitle), FFmpeg 4 through 9
)

// SubtitleTranscoder decodes one subtitle stream and re-encodes each event
// with another subtitle encoder, as `ffmpeg -map 0:N -c:s <encoder>` does.
type SubtitleTranscoder struct {
	mu     sync.Mutex
	dec    avcodec.Context
	enc    avcodec.Context
	sub    unsafe.Pointer // AVSubtitle
	out    unsafe.Pointer // subtitleOutMax bytes
	flush  avcodec.Packet // an empty packet: the decoder flush
	index  int
	closed bool
}

// NewSubtitleTranscoder opens a decoder for subtitle stream index (with
// pkt_timebase, so event times are filled) and the named encoder ("srt") in
// AV_TIME_BASE, given the decoder's subtitle_header as ffmpeg(1) gives it.
func (d *Decoder) NewSubtitleTranscoder(index int, encoder string) (*SubtitleTranscoder, error) {
	d.mu.Lock()
	defer d.mu.Unlock()
	if d.closed || d.formatCtx == nil {
		return nil, ErrClosed
	}
	if index < 0 || index >= avformat.GetNumStreams(d.formatCtx) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("ffgo: no stream %d", index)
	}
	stream := avformat.GetStream(d.formatCtx, index)
	par := avformat.GetStreamCodecPar(stream)
	if avformat.GetCodecParType(par) != avutil.MediaTypeSubtitle {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("ffgo: stream %d is not a subtitle stream", index)
	}
	t := &SubtitleTranscoder{index: index}
	fail := func(err error) (*SubtitleTranscoder, error) { t.free(); return nil, err }
	dc := avcodec.FindDecoder(avformat.GetCodecParCodecID(par))
	if dc == nil {
		return fail(fmt.Errorf("ffgo: no decoder for stream %d", index))
	}
	if t.dec = avcodec.AllocContext3(dc); t.dec == nil {
		return fail(ErrOutOfMemory)
	}
	if err := avcodec.ParametersToContext(t.dec, par); err != nil {
		return fail(err)
	}
	num, den := avformat.GetStreamTimeBase(stream)
	if err := avutil.OptSet(unsafe.Pointer(t.dec), "pkt_timebase", fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d", num, den), 0); err != nil {
		return fail(fmt.Errorf("ffgo: pkt_timebase: %w", err))
	}
	if err := avcodec.Open2(t.dec, dc, nil); err != nil {
		return fail(err)
	}
	ec := avcodec.FindEncoderByName(encoder)
	if ec == nil {
		return fail(fmt.Errorf("ffgo: no subtitle encoder %q", encoder))
	}
	if t.enc = avcodec.AllocContext3(ec); t.enc == nil {
		return fail(ErrOutOfMemory)
	}
	avcodec.SetCtxTimeBase(t.enc, 1, 1000000)
	if ret := shim.CodecCtxCopySubtitleHeader(unsafe.Pointer(t.enc), unsafe.Pointer(t.dec)); ret < 0 {
		if ret == -38 {
			return fail(fmt.Errorf("ffgo: subtitle header copy: %w", ErrShimRequired))
		}
		return fail(avutil.NewError(ret, "subtitle_header"))
	}
	if err := avcodec.Open2(t.enc, ec, nil); err != nil {
		return fail(err)
	}
	if t.sub = avutil.Malloc(subtitleStructSize); t.sub == nil {
		return fail(ErrOutOfMemory)
	}
	clearSubtitle(t.sub)
	if t.out = avutil.Malloc(subtitleOutMax); t.out == nil {
		return fail(ErrOutOfMemory)
	}
	if t.flush = avcodec.PacketAlloc(); t.flush == nil {
		return fail(ErrOutOfMemory)
	}
	return t, nil
}

// Transcode decodes p (a packet of the transcoder's stream; nil flushes the
// decoder at end of file) and encodes the event. ok is false when there is
// no output: no event, an event without pts, or an empty encode. The event's
// PTS and Duration are the decoded ones; the encoder sees start_display_time
// folded into pts, as fftools/ffmpeg_enc.c do_subtitle_out folds it.
func (t *SubtitleTranscoder) Transcode(p *Packet) (SubtitleEvent, bool, error) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	if t.closed {
		return SubtitleEvent{}, false, ErrClosed
	}
	pkt := t.flush
	if p != nil {
		if p.StreamIndex() != t.index {
			return SubtitleEvent{}, false, nil
		}
		pkt = p.ptr
	}
	clearSubtitle(t.sub)
	got, err := avcodec.DecodeSubtitle2(t.dec, t.sub, unsafe.Pointer(pkt))
	if err != nil {
		return SubtitleEvent{}, false, fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", ErrSubtitleDecode, err)
	}
	if !got {
		return SubtitleEvent{}, false, nil
	}
	defer avcodec.SubtitleFree(t.sub)
	pts := *(*int64)(unsafe.Add(t.sub, offsetSubPTS))
	if pts == avutil.NoPTSValue {
		return SubtitleEvent{}, false, nil
	}
	start := *(*uint32)(unsafe.Add(t.sub, offsetSubStartDisplayTime))
	end := *(*uint32)(unsafe.Add(t.sub, offsetSubEndDisplayTime))
	*(*int64)(unsafe.Add(t.sub, offsetSubPTS)) = pts + int64(start)*1000
	*(*uint32)(unsafe.Add(t.sub, offsetSubEndDisplayTime)) = end - start
	*(*uint32)(unsafe.Add(t.sub, offsetSubStartDisplayTime)) = 0
	n := avcodec.EncodeSubtitle(t.enc, t.out, subtitleOutMax, t.sub)
	if n < 0 {
		return SubtitleEvent{}, false, fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", ErrSubtitleEncode, avutil.NewError(n, "avcodec_encode_subtitle"))
	}
	if n == 0 {
		return SubtitleEvent{}, false, nil
	}
	data := make([]byte, n)
	copy(data, unsafe.Slice((*byte)(t.out), n))
	return SubtitleEvent{PTS: pts, Duration: int64(end) * 1000, Data: data}, true, nil
}

// Close frees the transcoder; the Decoder it reads from is not affected.
func (t *SubtitleTranscoder) Close() error {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	if !t.closed {
		t.closed = true
		t.free()
	}
	return nil
}

func (t *SubtitleTranscoder) free() {
	if t.flush != nil {
		avcodec.PacketFree(&t.flush)
	}
	if t.out != nil {
		avutil.Free(t.out)
		t.out = nil
	}
	if t.sub != nil {
		avutil.Free(t.sub)
		t.sub = nil
	}
	if t.enc != nil {
		avcodec.FreeContext(&t.enc)
	}
	if t.dec != nil {
		avcodec.FreeContext(&t.dec)
	}
}
```

```go
package ffgo

// ffprobeStream is one entry of `ffprobe -show_streams -of json`.
type ffprobeStream map[string]any

// str is ffprobe's value for key as text, and whether ffprobe printed it:
// JSON output leaves out the fields ffprobe prints as "unknown" or N/A.
func (s ffprobeStream) str(key string) (string, bool) {
	v, ok := s[key]
	if !ok {
		return "", false
	}
	switch v := v.(type) {
	case string:
		return v, true
	case float64:
		return strconv.FormatInt(int64(v), 10), true
	default:
		return fmt.Sprint(v), true
	}
}

func ffprobeStreams(t *testing.T, path string) []ffprobeStream {
	t.Helper()
	var doc struct {
		Streams []ffprobeStream `json:"streams"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(run(t, "ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_streams", "-of", "json", path)), &doc); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ffprobe %s: %v", path, err)
	}
	return doc.Streams
}

func probeFixtures(t *testing.T) map[string]string {

	ff := func(name string, args ...string) {

		"-f", "lavfi", "-i", "anullsrc=channel_layout=3c:sample_rate=48000",
		"-map", "0", "-map", "1", "-map", "2", "-t", "1",
		"-c:v", "libx265", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p10le", "-x265-params", "log-level=error",
		"-color_primaries", "bt2020", "-color_trc", "smpte2084", "-colorspace", "bt2020nc", "-color_range", "tv",
		"-c:a:0", "flac", "-sample_fmt:a:0", "s32", "-bits_per_raw_sample:a:0", "24",

// streamInfoCheck compares one StreamInfo field with what ffprobe prints;
// got and want both "" means the field does not apply to the stream.
type streamInfoCheck struct {
	name  string
	check func(si *StreamInfo, ff ffprobeStream) (got, want string)
}

var streamInfoChecks = []streamInfoCheck{
	{"profile", func(si *StreamInfo, ff ffprobeStream) (string, string) {
		want, _ := ff.str("profile")
		got := ProfileName(si.CodecID, si.Profile)
		if got == "" && si.Profile != ProfileUnknown {
			got = strconv.Itoa(si.Profile) // ffprobe prints a nameless profile's number
		}
		return got, want
	}},
	{"level", func(si *StreamInfo, ff ffprobeStream) (string, string) {
		if si.Type != MediaTypeVideo {
			return "", ""
		}
		want, _ := ff.str("level")
		return strconv.Itoa(si.Level), want
	}},
}

// fixtureFacts pin that the fixtures give each compared field a real value,
// since a comparison of two zeros passes whatever ffgo read. want "" means
// ffprobe must print the field, "-" that it must leave it out.
var fixtureFacts = []struct {
	file   string
	stream int
	key    string
	want   string
}{
	{"hdr.mkv", 0, "profile", "Main 10"},
	{"avc.mp4", 1, "profile", "LC"},
	{"avc.mp4", 0, "level", ""},
}

func TestStreamInfoReadsWhatFFprobePrints(t *testing.T) {
	requireShim(t)
	paths := probeFixtures(t)
	probed := map[string][]ffprobeStream{}
	for name, path := range paths {
		probed[name] = ffprobeStreams(t, path)
	}
	for _, f := range fixtureFacts {
		got, ok := probed[f.file][f.stream].str(f.key)
		switch {
		case f.want == "-" && ok:
			t.Errorf("fixture %s stream %d: ffprobe prints %s=%q; the fixture must leave it unknown", f.file, f.stream, f.key, got)
		case f.want != "-" && !ok:
			t.Errorf("fixture %s stream %d: ffprobe prints no %s", f.file, f.stream, f.key)
		case f.want != "" && f.want != "-" && got != f.want:
			t.Errorf("fixture %s stream %d: ffprobe %s=%q, want %q", f.file, f.stream, f.key, got, f.want)
		}
	}
	for name, path := range paths {
		d, err := NewDecoder(path)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		streams := d.Streams()
		ff := probed[name]
		if len(streams) != len(ff) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: ffgo sees %d streams, ffprobe %d", name, len(streams), len(ff))
		}
		for i, si := range streams {
			for _, c := range streamInfoChecks {
				if got, want := c.check(si, ff[i]); got != want {
					t.Errorf("%s stream %d (%s) %s: ffgo %q, ffprobe %q", name, i, si.Codec, c.name, got, want)
				}
			}
		}
		_ = d.Close()
	}
}

func TestProfileUnknownMatchesTheHeaders(t *testing.T) {
	requireShim(t)
	if v, ok := shim.EnumValue("AV_PROFILE_UNKNOWN"); !ok || v != ProfileUnknown {
		t.Fatalf("AV_PROFILE_UNKNOWN: headers %d (known %v), ffgo %d", v, ok, ProfileUnknown)
	}
}
```

```go
// GetCodecParProfile is codecpar's profile (AV_PROFILE_UNKNOWN, -99, when unknown).
func GetCodecParProfile(par avcodec.Parameters) int32 {
	if par == nil {
		return -99
	}
	return *(*int32)(unsafe.Pointer(uintptr(par) + offsetCodecParProfile))
}

// GetCodecParLevel is codecpar's level (-99 when unknown).
func GetCodecParLevel(par avcodec.Parameters) int32 {
	if par == nil {
		return -99
	}
	return *(*int32)(unsafe.Pointer(uintptr(par) + offsetCodecParLevel))
}
```

```go
// ProfileName is avcodec_profile_name: FFmpeg's name for profile p of codec
// id, numbered as the loaded library numbers it; "" when FFmpeg has none.
func ProfileName(id CodecID, p int32) string {
	if avcodecProfileName == nil {
		return ""
	}
	name := avcodecProfileName(int32(id), p)
	if name == nil {
		return ""
	}
	return goString(name)
}
```

```go
//go:build !ios && !android && (amd64 || arm64)

package ffgo

import "github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/avcodec"

// ProfileUnknown is AV_PROFILE_UNKNOWN: a stream whose profile is not known.
const ProfileUnknown = -99

// ProfileName is FFmpeg's name for profile p of codec id ("Main 10", "LC",
// "DTS-HD MA"); id is numbered as the loaded release numbers it, as
// StreamInfo.CodecID holds it. It is "" when FFmpeg names none; ffprobe then
// prints the number, unless p is ProfileUnknown.
func ProfileName(id CodecID, p int) string { return avcodec.ProfileName(id, int32(p)) }
```

```go
// FieldOrder is a video stream's AVFieldOrder.
type FieldOrder int32

const (
	FieldOrderUnknown     FieldOrder = iota // AV_FIELD_UNKNOWN
	FieldOrderProgressive                   // AV_FIELD_PROGRESSIVE
	FieldOrderTT                            // AV_FIELD_TT: top coded first, top displayed first
	FieldOrderBB                            // AV_FIELD_BB
	FieldOrderTB                            // AV_FIELD_TB: top coded first, bottom displayed first
	FieldOrderBT                            // AV_FIELD_BT
)

// String is ffprobe's name for the field order; "" when unknown, which
// ffprobe prints as "unknown" and its JSON leaves out.
func (f FieldOrder) String() string {
	switch f {
	case FieldOrderProgressive:
		return "progressive"
	case FieldOrderTT:
		return "tt"
	case FieldOrderBB:
		return "bb"
	case FieldOrderTB:
		return "tb"
	case FieldOrderBT:
		return "bt"
	}
	return ""
}
```

- `decoder.go` `getStreamInfo`, video branch: `info.FieldOrder = FieldOrder(avformat.GetCodecParFieldOrder(codecPar))`.

```go
// GetStreamRFrameRate is the stream's r_frame_rate: the lowest frame rate
// that represents every timestamp exactly (ffprobe's r_frame_rate); 0/0
// when unknown.
func GetStreamRFrameRate(stream Stream) (num, den int32) {
	if stream == nil {
		return 0, 0
	}
	num = *(*int32)(unsafe.Pointer(uintptr(stream) + offsetStreamRFrameRate))
	den = *(*int32)(unsafe.Pointer(uintptr(stream) + offsetStreamRFrameRate + 4))
	return
}

// GetStreamStartTime is the stream's first timestamp in its time base, or
// AV_NOPTS_VALUE.
func GetStreamStartTime(stream Stream) int64 {
	if stream == nil {
		return avutil.NoPTSValue
	}
	return *(*int64)(unsafe.Pointer(uintptr(stream) + offsetStreamStartTime))
}

// GetStreamDuration is the stream's duration in its time base, or
// AV_NOPTS_VALUE when the container records none (Matroska).
func GetStreamDuration(stream Stream) int64 {
	if stream == nil {
		return avutil.NoPTSValue
	}
	return *(*int64)(unsafe.Pointer(uintptr(stream) + offsetStreamDuration))
}
```

A Matroska chapter (time base 1/1000000000) past 2h33m43s no longer overflows `ts*num*1e6`. `SetChapters` and clustarr's `m.SetChapters(d.GetChapters())` (`pkg/transcode/engine/engine.go`) use only `Start` and `End`, so they are unchanged.

```go
package ffgo

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// Matroska stores chapter times in nanoseconds (time base 1/1000000000), so
// ts*num*1000000 overflows int64 past 9.22e12 ns: 2h33m43s.
func TestChapterTimesPastTheInt64MicrosecondRange(t *testing.T) {
	requireShim(t)
	ffmpegOrSkip(t)
	dir := t.TempDir()
	meta := filepath.Join(dir, "chapters.txt")
	if err := os.WriteFile(meta, []byte(";FFMETADATA1\n"+
		"[CHAPTER]\nTIMEBASE=1/1000000000\nSTART=0\nEND=600000000\ntitle=Opening\n"+
		"[CHAPTER]\nTIMEBASE=1/1000000000\nSTART=600000000\nEND=10800000000000\ntitle=Long\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	path := filepath.Join(dir, "long.mkv")
	run(t, "ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y",
		"-f", "lavfi", "-i", "testsrc2=size=64x36:rate=5:duration=1", "-i", meta,
		"-map", "0", "-map_chapters", "1", "-c:v", "libx264", path)
	d, err := NewDecoder(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer d.Close()
	ch := d.GetChapters()
	if len(ch) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("got %d chapters, want 2", len(ch))
	}
	c := ch[1]
	if c.Title != "Long" || c.Start != 600*time.Millisecond || c.End != 3*time.Hour {
		t.Errorf("chapter 2 = %q %v-%v, want Long 600ms-3h0m0s", c.Title, c.Start, c.End)
	}
	if c.TimeBase != NewRational(1, 1000000000) || c.StartTS != 600000000 || c.EndTS != 10800000000000 {
		t.Errorf("chapter 2 timestamps = %d-%d in %d/%d, want 600000000-10800000000000 in 1/1000000000",
			c.StartTS, c.EndTS, c.TimeBase.Num, c.TimeBase.Den)
	}
}
```

and add:

```go
// tsDuration is ts in time base tb as a Duration, truncated to the
// microsecond as GetChapters always did. It is computed in big integers:
// ts*num*1000000 overflows int64 for a Matroska chapter past 2h33m43s.
func tsDuration(ts int64, tb Rational) time.Duration {
	us := new(big.Int).Mul(big.NewInt(ts), big.NewInt(int64(tb.Num)*1000000))
	us.Quo(us, big.NewInt(int64(tb.Den)))
	ns := us.Mul(us, big.NewInt(int64(time.Microsecond)))
	switch {
	case ns.IsInt64():
		return time.Duration(ns.Int64())
	case ns.Sign() < 0:
		return math.MinInt64
	default:
		return math.MaxInt64
	}
}
```

The existing `if tbDen == 0 { tbDen = 1 }` stays before `tb` is built.

### Task W0.21: F16: `WithInterrupt`

**Spec:** §7.5 F16, §6.4 (`TestWithInterruptAbortsAnOpenOnAStalledReader`), §7.2.8 (decode does not use it)
**Files:**
- Modify: `/home/appkins/src/mediactl/ffgo-unify/shim/ffshim.h`, `shim/ffshim.c` (`ffshim_formatctx_set_interrupt`), `shim/prebuilt/linux-amd64/libffshim.so`, `internal/shim/shim.go`, `decoder.go` (`DecoderOptions.Interrupt`, `Decoder.interruptID`, `NewDecoderWithOptions`, `Close`), `probe.go` (`openInputWithRetries`, `openInputOnce`)
- Create: `interrupt.go`, `interrupt_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: none.
- Produces: `func WithInterrupt(done <-chan struct{}) DecoderOption` and `DecoderOptions.Interrupt <-chan struct{}`. Once `done` is closed, FFmpeg's I/O wait loops abort the open, stream-info read or packet read with `AVERROR_EXIT` ("Immediate exit requested"). The callback is process-wide: one `purego.NewCallback`, with `opaque` keyed in a registry. Also C `void ffshim_formatctx_set_interrupt(void *ctx, void *cb, void *opaque)` and Go `shim.FormatCtxSetInterrupt`. **Limit:** FFmpeg polls the callback only between I/O attempts (EAGAIN, network protocols, the file protocol's `follow`). A `read(2)` blocked in the kernel, such as a hard NFS mount or a FIFO with no writer, is never interrupted. The probe's 45 s bound therefore still rests on `ffruntime.Do`'s abandonment (§7.4).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test.**

```go
import (

	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

// An empty file opened with the file protocol's follow=1 never reaches
// EOF: every read answers EAGAIN, and FFmpeg's I/O loop
// (retry_transfer_wrapper) polls the interrupt callback between retries --
// a stalled reader. A FIFO nobody writes would block inside open(2) instead,
// where FFmpeg never polls the callback.
func TestWithInterruptAbortsAnOpenOnAStalledReader(t *testing.T) {
	requireShim(t)
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "stalled.mkv")

		if !strings.Contains(r.err.Error(), "Immediate exit requested") {
			t.Errorf("err = %v, want AVERROR_EXIT (Immediate exit requested)", r.err)
```

`interrupt.go`:

```go
//go:build !ios && !android && (amd64 || arm64)

package ffgo

import (
	"sync"

	"github.com/ebitengine/purego"
)

// One process-wide purego callback (purego never frees one, so never one per
// open) looks its opaque id up in this registry.
var (
	interruptMu     sync.Mutex
	interruptNext   uintptr
	interrupts      = map[uintptr]<-chan struct{}{}
	interruptCBOnce sync.Once
	interruptCB     uintptr
)

func interruptCallback() uintptr {
	interruptCBOnce.Do(func() { interruptCB = purego.NewCallback(interruptTrampoline) })
	return interruptCB
}

// interruptTrampoline is FFmpeg's int (*)(void *opaque): 1 aborts the I/O.
func interruptTrampoline(opaque uintptr) uintptr {
	interruptMu.Lock()
	done := interrupts[opaque]
	interruptMu.Unlock()
	if done == nil {
		return 0
	}
	select {
	case <-done:
		return 1
	default:
		return 0
	}
}

func registerInterrupt(done <-chan struct{}) uintptr {
	interruptMu.Lock()
	defer interruptMu.Unlock()
	interruptNext++
	interrupts[interruptNext] = done
	return interruptNext
}

func unregisterInterrupt(id uintptr) {
	if id == 0 {
		return
	}
	interruptMu.Lock()
	delete(interrupts, id)
	interruptMu.Unlock()
}

func interruptsRegistered() int {
	interruptMu.Lock()
	defer interruptMu.Unlock()
	return len(interrupts)
}

// WithInterrupt makes FFmpeg abort the decoder's I/O with AVERROR_EXIT once
// done is closed: the open, the stream-info read and every packet read. It
// acts where FFmpeg's I/O loops poll (EAGAIN retries, network protocols), not
// inside a read(2) blocked in the kernel. It needs the shim.
func WithInterrupt(done <-chan struct{}) DecoderOption {
	return func(o *DecoderOptions) { o.Interrupt = done }
}
```

**Spec:** §7.5 F17, §7.2.2 step 8, §7.2.3 (why the downmix info matters), §7.2.10 (the non-default `-center_mixlev` fixture)
**Files:**
- Modify: `/home/appkins/src/mediactl/ffgo-unify/shim/ffshim.h`, `shim/ffshim.c` (`ffshim_buffersrc_set_side_data`), `shim/prebuilt/linux-amd64/libffshim.so`, `internal/shim/shim.go`, `filter_graph.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `decodeStream` (W0.4); `FilterGraphConfig.Layout` (W0.9).
- Produces: `FilterGraphConfig.InputSideData *Frame`. Before the graph is configured, the buffer source (audio or video) gets the frame's side data the way `ffmpeg(1)` forwards it: every entry whose descriptor has `AV_SIDE_DATA_PROP_GLOBAL`, plus `AV_FRAME_DATA_DOWNMIX_INFO`. If the shim cannot forward it, `NewFilterGraph` returns an error rather than silently producing different output. Also C `int ffshim_buffersrc_set_side_data(void *src_ctx, const void *frame)` and Go `shim.BufferSrcSetSideData(src, frame unsafe.Pointer) error`.

`filter_graph_sidedata_test.go`:

```go
//go:build !ios && !android && (amd64 || arm64)

package ffgo

import (
	"bytes"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// The AC-3 decoder attaches the bitstream's downmix levels to every frame
// (AV_FRAME_DATA_DOWNMIX_INFO); aresample reads them from the buffer source
// at init, so ffmpeg(1) hands the first frame's side data to abuffer.
// Without it the mono downmix uses swresample's -3 dB defaults.
func TestInputSideDataReachesAresampleAsInFFmpeg(t *testing.T) {
	requireShim(t)
	ffmpegOrSkip(t)
	dir := t.TempDir()
	path := filepath.Join(dir, "mix.mka")
	run(t, "ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y", "-f", "lavfi",
		"-i", "sine=frequency=440:duration=2:sample_rate=48000,aformat=channel_layouts=5.1(side)",
		"-c:a", "ac3", "-center_mixlev", "0.5", "-surround_mixlev", "0.5", path)
	ref := filepath.Join(dir, "ref.pcm")
	run(t, "ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y", "-i", path, "-map", "0:a:0",
		"-ac", "1", "-ar", "11025", "-f", "s16le", ref)
	want, err := os.ReadFile(ref)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := downmixPCM(t, path, true); !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("with the first frame's side data: %d bytes, ffmpeg %d, contents differ", len(got), len(want))
	}
	if got := downmixPCM(t, path, false); bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatal("without side data the downmix still equals ffmpeg's: the fixture does not exercise the downmix levels")
	}
}

// downmixPCM decodes path's audio through the chain `ffmpeg -ac 1 -ar 11025
// -f s16le` builds, giving the buffer source the first frame's side data
// when withSideData.
func downmixPCM(t *testing.T, path string, withSideData bool) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	d, err := NewDecoder(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer d.Close()
	sd, err := d.NewStreamDecoder(d.AudioStream().Index, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer sd.Close()
	var g *FilterGraph
	var pcm []byte
	take := func(out []*Frame) {
		for _, o := range out {
			w := WrapFrame(*o, MediaTypeAudio)
			pcm = append(pcm, w.Data(0)[:2*w.NumSamples()]...)
			_ = o.Free()
		}
	}
	decodeStream(t, d, sd, func(f Frame) {
		if g == nil {
			rate := WrapFrame(f, MediaTypeAudio).SampleRate()
			cfg := FilterGraphConfig{
				SampleRate: rate, SampleFmt: SampleFormat(f.Format()), Layout: f.ChannelLayout(),
				TimeBase: NewRational(1, int32(rate)),
				Filters:  "aformat=sample_fmts=s16:sample_rates=11025:channel_layouts=mono",
			}
			if withSideData {
				cfg.InputSideData = &f
			}
			var err error
			if g, err = NewFilterGraph(cfg); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}
		out, err := g.Filter(&f)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		take(out)
	})
	out, err := g.Flush()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	take(out)
	_ = g.Close()
	return pcm
}
```

`shim/ffshim.h`, after `ffshim_buffersrc_set_hw_frames`:

```c
/* Gives a buffer source the side data ffmpeg(1) forwards from an input's
   frame: every entry whose descriptor is AV_SIDE_DATA_PROP_GLOBAL, plus
   AV_FRAME_DATA_DOWNMIX_INFO (fftools/ffmpeg_filter.c ifilter_parameters_from_frame).
   ENOSYS where AVBufferSrcParameters has no side data (before libavfilter 11). */
int ffshim_buffersrc_set_side_data(void *src_ctx, const void *frame);
```

`shim/ffshim.c`, inside the `#ifdef FFSHIM_HAVE_AVFILTER` block after `ffshim_buffersrc_set_hw_frames`:

```c
int ffshim_buffersrc_set_side_data(void *src_ctx, const void *frame) {
#if LIBAVFILTER_VERSION_MAJOR >= 11
    const AVFrame *f = frame;
    AVFrameSideData **sd = NULL;
    int nb = 0, ret = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < f->nb_side_data; i++) {
        const AVFrameSideData *e = f->side_data[i];
        const AVSideDataDescriptor *desc = av_frame_side_data_desc(e->type);
        if (e->type != AV_FRAME_DATA_DOWNMIX_INFO && !(desc && (desc->props & AV_SIDE_DATA_PROP_GLOBAL)))
            continue;
        if ((ret = av_frame_side_data_clone(&sd, &nb, e, 0)) < 0)
            goto end;
    }
    if (nb > 0) {
        AVBufferSrcParameters *p = av_buffersrc_parameters_alloc();
        if (!p) {
            ret = AVERROR(ENOMEM);
            goto end;
        }
        p->side_data = sd;
        p->nb_side_data = nb;
        ret = av_buffersrc_parameters_set((AVFilterContext *)src_ctx, p); /* clones them */
        av_free(p);
    }
end:
    av_frame_side_data_free(&sd, &nb);
    return ret;
#else
    (void)src_ctx;
    (void)frame;
    return AVERROR(ENOSYS);
#endif
}
```

`internal/shim/shim.go`: add `shimBufferSrcSetSideData func(src, frame uintptr) int32` and register it optionally as `"ffshim_buffersrc_set_side_data"`. Then add:

```go
// BufferSrcSetSideData gives a buffer source the side data ffmpeg(1)
// forwards from an input frame (global entries plus the downmix info).
func BufferSrcSetSideData(src, frame unsafe.Pointer) error {
	if !loaded {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: side data on a buffer source requires the shim", ErrShimNotLoaded)
	}
	if shimBufferSrcSetSideData == nil {
		return errors.New("ffgo: this shim was built without ffshim_buffersrc_set_side_data")
	}
	if ret := shimBufferSrcSetSideData(uintptr(src), uintptr(frame)); ret < 0 {
		if ret == averrorENOSYS {
			return fmt.Errorf("ffgo: buffer source side data: %w", ErrENOSYS)
		}
		return fmt.Errorf("ffgo: av_buffersrc_parameters_set (side data): %d", ret)
	}
	return nil
}
```

```go
			}
		})
	}
```

```go
// NewPacketData gives pkt a buffer of len(data) bytes (av_new_packet) and
// copies data into it. pkt must be empty.
func NewPacketData(pkt Packet, data []byte) error {
	if ret := av_new_packet(pkt, int32(len(data))); ret < 0 {
		return avutilError(ret) // the package's existing error conversion
	}
	if len(data) > 0 {
		copy(unsafe.Slice((*byte)(GetPacketData(pkt)), len(data)), data)
	}
	return nil
}
```

  In `muxer.go`:

```go
// SubtitleStreamConfig is a text subtitle stream written from pre-made
// events, with no encoder: SubRip ("subrip") or ASS ("ass").
type SubtitleStreamConfig struct {
	Codec   string
	Header  []byte // the stream's extradata; for "ass", DefaultASSHeader when empty
	Options StreamOptions
}

// DefaultASSHeader is the script header FFmpeg's ass encoder writes.
const DefaultASSHeader = "[Script Info]\r\n; Script generated by FFmpeg/Lavc\r\nScriptType: v4.00+\r\nPlayResX: 384\r\nPlayResY: 288\r\nScaledBorderAndShadow: yes\r\nYCbCr Matrix: None\r\n\r\n[V4+ Styles]\r\nFormat: Name, Fontname, Fontsize, PrimaryColour, SecondaryColour, OutlineColour, BackColour, Bold, Italic, Underline, StrikeOut, ScaleX, ScaleY, Spacing, Angle, BorderStyle, Outline, Shadow, Alignment, MarginL, MarginR, MarginV, Encoding\r\nStyle: Default,Arial,16,&Hffffff,&Hffffff,&H0,&H0,0,0,0,0,100,100,0,0,1,1,0,2,10,10,10,0\r\n\r\n[Events]\r\nFormat: Layer, Start, End, Style, Name, MarginL, MarginR, MarginV, Effect, Text\r\n"

// AddSubtitleStream adds a stream WriteSubtitle fills. Its time base is
// 1/1000, the one the text subtitle muxers write.
func (m *Muxer) AddSubtitleStream(cfg *SubtitleStreamConfig) (*MuxerStream, error) {
	if cfg == nil || (cfg.Codec != "subrip" && cfg.Codec != "ass") {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("ffgo: subtitle stream codec must be subrip or ass")
	}
	id := avcodec.CodecIDByName(cfg.Codec)
	par := avcodec.ParametersAlloc()
	defer avcodec.ParametersFree(&par)
	avformat.SetCodecParType(par, avutil.MediaTypeSubtitle)
	avformat.SetCodecParCodecID(par, id)
	header := cfg.Header
	if cfg.Codec == "ass" && len(header) == 0 {
		header = []byte(DefaultASSHeader)
	}
	if len(header) > 0 {
		avformat.SetCodecParExtradata(par, header)
	}
	return m.AddCopyStream(&CopyStreamConfig{CodecParameters: par, TimeBase: NewRational(1, 1000), Options: cfg.Options})
}

// WriteSubtitle writes one event: PTS and Duration in microseconds, as
// SubtitleEvent carries them, and Data as the codec stores a packet
// (SubRip text, or an ASS event line "ReadOrder,Layer,Style,...,Text").
func (m *Muxer) WriteSubtitle(ms *MuxerStream, ev SubtitleEvent) error {
	pkt := avcodec.PacketAlloc()
	defer avcodec.PacketFree(&pkt)
	if err := avcodec.NewPacketData(pkt, ev.Data); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("ffgo: subtitle packet: %w", err)
	}
	us := NewRational(1, 1_000_000)
	avcodec.SetPacketPTS(pkt, RescaleQ(ev.PTS, us, ms.timeBase))
	avcodec.SetPacketDTS(pkt, RescaleQ(ev.PTS, us, ms.timeBase))
	avcodec.SetPacketDuration(pkt, RescaleQ(ev.Duration, us, ms.timeBase))
	avcodec.SetPacketFlags(pkt, avcodec.PktFlagKey)
	return m.WritePacket(ms, &Packet{ptr: pkt}) // the package's Packet wrapper; WritePacket rescales to the muxer's stream time base
}
```

  (`ms.timeBase` is the stream's time base as `AddCopyStream` set it. Use the package's existing names for `PacketFree`, `PktFlagKey`, the `Packet` wrapper and the error conversion; the shapes above are the contract.)

```go
//go:build linux && amd64

package shim

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"runtime"
	"testing"

	"github.com/ebitengine/purego"

	"github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/internal/bindings"
)

// The committed prebuilt shim must define every function ffshim.h declares.
// A C change committed without `./shim/build.sh prebuilt` leaves Go calling
// a symbol the shipped library lacks, which the optional bindings would
// silently read as "no shim" (and ShimAPIVersion as 0).
func TestPrebuiltShimDefinesEveryDeclaredFunction(t *testing.T) {
	if err := bindings.Load(); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("FFmpeg not loaded: %v", err)
	}
	_, file, _, _ := runtime.Caller(0)
	root := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(file), "..", "..")
	hdr, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, "shim", "ffshim.h"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	so := filepath.Join(root, "shim", "prebuilt", "linux-amd64", "libffshim.so")
	lib, err := purego.Dlopen(so, purego.RTLD_NOW|purego.RTLD_LOCAL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("the prebuilt shim does not load on this host (built for another FFmpeg?): %v", err)
	}
	defer purego.Dlclose(lib)
	decls := regexp.MustCompile(`\b(ffshim_[a-z0-9_]+)\s*\(`).FindAllSubmatch(hdr, -1)
	if len(decls) < 95 {
		t.Fatalf("found %d declarations in ffshim.h, want at least 95 (91 at .11 plus this tag's four)", len(decls))
	}
	for _, m := range decls {
		if _, err := purego.Dlsym(lib, string(m[1])); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s is declared in ffshim.h but missing from %s: run ./shim/build.sh prebuilt", m[1], so)
		}
	}
}
```

```bash
39364599a57f6b7bb36b4532200ab5741213fbab0476c2399d0a3e091a38de2c  libpar2shim-linux-amd64.so
```

## Wave 1: pkg leaves (W1.1 to W1.11)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-manager-agent-split-design.md` §4.3
"Wave 1: pkg leaves" (steps 1.1 to 1.9), §3.1 (`pkg/binpath`), §3.5.2 step 7
(`AwaitTopology`), §5.9, §7.3.1, §9.2 (`StreamAdmin.Missing`). Verified against
the worktree at `4b103429` (local main `cdbdd870` plus the spec commit).

Wave 1 extracts leaf packages and moves code without changing behaviour. Callers
keep compiling through wrappers where the spec says so (pkg/k8s), and move to the
new import path everywhere else. Nothing here touches the AudioGraft work that
landed after the spec (`app/squash/grafttask`, the AudioGraft controller,
`--graft-concurrency`). The only squasharr files Wave 1 edits are tests that call
the ffprobe probe, plus `app/squash/exec_guard_test.go`, whose ban list W1.8
extends so the guard keeps its meaning once the probe moves.

### Spec step to task

| Spec §4.3 step | Task | Owner lane |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.1 pkg/obs | W1.1 | A |
| 1.2 pkg/k8s/conditions | W1.2 | B (pkg/k8s, serial) |
| prerequisite of 1.3: `events.StreamAdmin.Missing` (§3.5.2, §9.2) | W1.3 | C (pkg/events) |
| 1.3 pkg/busconn + `AwaitTopology` | W1.4 | B (after W1.2, W1.3) |
| 1.6 pkg/k8s/dataready.go | W1.5 | B (after W1.4) |
| 1.4 pkg/overlay/render | W1.6 | D |
| 1.5 pkg/subtitles/postprocess | W1.7 | E |
| 1.7 pkg/mediainfo/ffprobeexec | W1.8 | F |
| 1.8 embedded `Extract` + execextract | W1.9 | G |
| 1.9 pkg/binpath | W1.10 | H |
| wave gate | W1.11 | last, after all lanes |

The lanes touch disjoint files. pkg/k8s has one owner, who runs W1.2, then W1.4,
then W1.5. W1.4 also needs W1.3 to have landed. Every other lane may run in
parallel with lane B and with each other.

### Wave-specific rules

- **Envtest.** Packages with `*_envtest_test.go` files run with
  `KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS="$($(go env GOPATH)/bin/setup-envtest use 1.37.0 -i -p path)"`
  (`-i` uses the installed assets; this host has them under
  `~/.local/share/kubebuilder-envtest/k8s/1.37.0-linux-amd64`). Below,
  `$ENVTEST` stands for that assignment.
- **Formatting.** After every edit, run
  `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/gofumpt -w <touched .go files>` and
  `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/goimports -local github.com/mediactl/clustarr -w <touched .go files>`
  (`make lint` runs both formatters).
- **No go.mod edit.** Every import Wave 1 adds is already a requirement
  (nats.go, controller-runtime `pkg/log` and `pkg/healthz`, x/image, go-astisub,
  go-ffprobe, regexp2). No `go get`, no `go mod tidy`.
- **No RBAC marker moves.** None of the moved files carries a
  `+kubebuilder:rbac` marker, so `make manifests` must leave `config/` and
  `charts/` byte-identical. W1.11 checks this.
- **Real ffprobe and ffmpeg.** This host has `/usr/bin/ffprobe` and
  `/usr/bin/ffmpeg` (n9.0.1). The probe and extraction tests that W1.8 and W1.9
  move must **run** after the move, not skip. Check with `-v`.
- **Commits** are path-scoped (`git commit -m … -- <paths>`). Run `git add` on
  new files first. Never `git stash`, never push. A `git mv` stages the rename,
  so include both the old and the new path in the commit pathspec.

```go
// Package conditions reads metav1.Conditions. It is the read half of pkg/k8s's
// condition helpers, split out so that a reader which never writes status
// (pkg/pipeline, and through it cmd/ui) links neither pkg/k8s nor
// controller-runtime (spec §4.3 step 1.2). pkg/k8s keeps a one-line wrapper
// for each name, so its callers are unchanged.
package conditions

import (
	"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/meta"
	metav1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1"
)

// ConditionReady is the one condition type every Clustarr kind reports.
const ConditionReady = "Ready"

// FindCondition returns the condition of type condType, or nil.
func FindCondition(conds []metav1.Condition, condType string) *metav1.Condition {
	return meta.FindStatusCondition(conds, condType)
}

// IsConditionTrue reports whether condType is present and True.
func IsConditionTrue(conds []metav1.Condition, condType string) bool {
	return meta.IsStatusConditionTrue(conds, condType)
}

// IsConditionFalse reports whether condType is present and False.
func IsConditionFalse(conds []metav1.Condition, condType string) bool {
	return meta.IsStatusConditionFalse(conds, condType)
}

// IsReady reports whether Ready is present and True.
func IsReady(conds []metav1.Condition) bool { return IsConditionTrue(conds, ConditionReady) }

// ObservedGeneration returns the ObservedGeneration of condType, or 0.
func ObservedGeneration(conds []metav1.Condition, condType string) int64 {
	if c := FindCondition(conds, condType); c != nil {
		return c.ObservedGeneration
	}
	return 0
}

// StatusUpToDate reports whether condType was last set for obj's current
// generation. A controller that returns early on an unchanged spec, and a test
// that waits for a reconcile to land, both ask exactly this question.
func StatusUpToDate(obj metav1.Object, conds []metav1.Condition, condType string) bool {
	if obj == nil {
		return false
	}
	c := FindCondition(conds, condType)
	return c != nil && c.ObservedGeneration == obj.GetGeneration()
}
```

```go
// testMissing holds StreamAdmin.Missing to its contract (spec §3.5.2). On a bus
// nothing has ensured, it names every object of the topology in
// Topology.Objects order. Once the streams, buckets and object stores exist,
// it names only the consumer still absent. Once Ensure has created that too,
// it names nothing. A deleted durable is missing again.
func testMissing(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), Timeout)
	t.Cleanup(cancel)
	bus := newBus()
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		if err := bus.Close(); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("Close: %v", err)
		}
	})
	sa, ok := bus.(events.StreamAdmin)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("%T does not implement events.StreamAdmin", bus)
	}

	grab, ok := events.Default().ForSingleNode().Consumer(events.ConsumerCatalogGrab)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("the default topology has no %s", events.ConsumerCatalogGrab)
	}
	bare := Topology()
	full := Topology()
	full.Consumers = []events.ConsumerSpec{grab}

	var all []string
	for _, o := range full.Objects() {
		all = append(all, o.String())
	}
	if got, err := sa.Missing(ctx, full); err != nil || !slices.Equal(got, all) {
		t.Fatalf("Missing before Ensure = %v, %v; want every object %v", got, err, all)
	}

	if err := bus.Ensure(ctx, bare); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Ensure without consumers: %v", err)
	}
	consumer := events.TopologyObject{Kind: events.TopologyConsumer, Stream: grab.Stream, Name: grab.Name}.String()
	if got, err := sa.Missing(ctx, full); err != nil || !slices.Equal(got, []string{consumer}) {
		t.Fatalf("Missing with only the consumer absent = %v, %v; want [%s]", got, err, consumer)
	}

	if err := bus.Ensure(ctx, full); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Ensure: %v", err)
	}
	if got, err := sa.Missing(ctx, full); err != nil || len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Missing after Ensure = %v, %v; want nothing", got, err)
	}

	if err := sa.DeleteSubscription(ctx, grab.Stream, grab.Name); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("DeleteSubscription: %v", err)
	}
	if got, err := sa.Missing(ctx, full); err != nil || !slices.Equal(got, []string{consumer}) {
		t.Fatalf("Missing after deleting the durable = %v, %v; want [%s]", got, err, consumer)
	}
}
```

```go
// TopologyKind is the kind of JetStream object a TopologyObject is.
type TopologyKind string

const (
	TopologyStream      TopologyKind = "stream"
	TopologyConsumer    TopologyKind = "consumer"
	TopologyBucket      TopologyKind = "kv"
	TopologyObjectStore TopologyKind = "object store"
)

// TopologyObject is one stream, consumer, KV bucket or object store that a
// Topology declares.
type TopologyObject struct {
	Kind TopologyKind
	// Stream is a consumer's stream; empty for every other kind.
	Stream string
	Name   string
}

// String names o as StreamAdmin.Missing reports it: "stream CLUSTARR_EVENTS",
// "consumer CLUSTARR_WORK_CATALOGARR/catalogarr-grab", "kv <bucket>",
// "object store clustarr-artwork".
func (o TopologyObject) String() string {
	if o.Kind == TopologyConsumer {
		return string(o.Kind) + " " + o.Stream + "/" + o.Name
	}
	return string(o.Kind) + " " + o.Name
}

// Objects lists every object t declares: its streams, then its consumers, then
// its KV buckets, then its object stores, each in declaration order.
func (t Topology) Objects() []TopologyObject {
	out := make([]TopologyObject, 0, len(t.Streams)+len(t.Consumers)+len(t.Buckets)+len(t.ObjectStores))
	for _, s := range t.Streams {
		out = append(out, TopologyObject{Kind: TopologyStream, Name: s.Name})
	}
	for _, c := range t.Consumers {
		out = append(out, TopologyObject{Kind: TopologyConsumer, Stream: c.Stream, Name: c.Name})
	}
	for _, b := range t.Buckets {
		out = append(out, TopologyObject{Kind: TopologyBucket, Name: b.Name})
	}
	for _, o := range t.ObjectStores {
		out = append(out, TopologyObject{Kind: TopologyObjectStore, Name: o.Name})
	}
	return out
}
```

```go
// Missing implements events.StreamAdmin. Each object is looked up afresh by
// name: the bus's bound KV and object-store handles are not consulted, because
// a NATS restart can delete a memory-backed bucket under a live handle.
func (b *Bus) Missing(ctx context.Context, t events.Topology) ([]string, error) {
	var out []string
	for _, o := range t.Objects() {
		var err error
		switch o.Kind {
		case events.TopologyStream:
			_, err = b.js.Stream(ctx, o.Name)
		case events.TopologyConsumer:
			_, err = b.js.Consumer(ctx, o.Stream, o.Name)
		case events.TopologyBucket:
			_, err = b.js.KeyValue(ctx, o.Name)
		case events.TopologyObjectStore:
			_, err = b.js.ObjectStore(ctx, o.Name)
		}
		switch {
		case err == nil:
		case errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound),
			errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrConsumerNotFound),
			errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrBucketNotFound):
			out = append(out, o.String())
		default:
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("natsbus: look up %s: %w", o, err)
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}
```

     `js.KeyValue` and `js.ObjectStore` map a missing backing stream to
     `jetstream.ErrBucketNotFound` (nats.go v1.53.1 `jetstream/kv.go:509`,
     `object.go:598`). `js.Consumer` on a missing stream returns
     `ErrStreamNotFound`.

```go
// hasDurable reports whether durable exists on this stream: bound by Ensure,
// Subscribe or Pull, and not forgotten since.
func (s *stream) hasDurable(durable string) bool {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	_, ok := s.durables[durable]
	return ok
}
```

```go
// Missing implements events.StreamAdmin.
func (b *Bus) Missing(_ context.Context, t events.Topology) ([]string, error) {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.closed {
		return nil, events.ErrClosed
	}
	var out []string
	for _, o := range t.Objects() {
		var ok bool
		switch o.Kind {
		case events.TopologyStream:
			_, ok = b.streams[o.Name]
		case events.TopologyConsumer:
			st := b.streams[o.Stream]
			ok = st != nil && st.hasDurable(o.Name)
		case events.TopologyBucket:
			_, ok = b.buckets[o.Name]
		case events.TopologyObjectStore:
			_, ok = b.objectStores[o.Name]
		}
		if !ok {
			out = append(out, o.String())
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}
```

```go
package busconn

import (
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events/contracttest"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events/membus"
)

func fastPoll(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	old := awaitPoll
	awaitPoll = 10 * time.Millisecond
	t.Cleanup(func() { awaitPoll = old })
}

// An agent that starts before the manager waits, then proceeds once the
// manager has ensured the topology (spec §3.5.2 step 7).
func TestAwaitTopologyReturnsOnceTheManagerHasEnsuredIt(t *testing.T) {
	fastPoll(t)
	ctx := t.Context()
	bus := membus.New(nil)
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = bus.Close() })
	topo := contracttest.Topology()

	go func() {
		time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
		_ = bus.Ensure(ctx, topo)
	}()
	require.NoError(t, AwaitTopology(ctx, bus, topo, 5*time.Second))
}

// On timeout the error names exactly what is still missing, so a crash-looping
// agent's log says which object the manager has not made.
func TestAwaitTopologyNamesWhatIsStillMissingWhenItGivesUp(t *testing.T) {
	fastPoll(t)
	ctx := t.Context()
	bus := membus.New(nil)
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = bus.Close() })
	topo := contracttest.Topology()
	require.NotEmpty(t, topo.Buckets)
	partial := topo
	partial.Buckets = nil
	require.NoError(t, bus.Ensure(ctx, partial))

	err := AwaitTopology(ctx, bus, topo, 100*time.Millisecond)
	require.ErrorContains(t, err, "waiting for the manager to create ")
	for _, b := range topo.Buckets {
		require.ErrorContains(t, err, "kv "+b.Name)
	}
	for _, s := range topo.Streams {
		require.NotContains(t, err.Error(), "stream "+s.Name, "the streams exist")
	}
}

type adminless struct{ events.Bus }

func TestAwaitTopologyNeedsABusThatCanReportWhatIsMissing(t *testing.T) {
	err := AwaitTopology(t.Context(), adminless{}, contracttest.Topology(), time.Second)
	require.ErrorContains(t, err, "cannot report")
}
```
