```go
// Controller names are process-global; only the manager registers them
// in bulk, so uniqueness is held across what cmd/manager links.
func TestControllerNamesAreUniqueAcrossTheBinary(t *testing.T) {
	linked := moduleDirs(depguard.Load(t, mod+"cmd/manager", linuxStatic...))
	files := map[string]*ast.File{}
	for path, f := range productionFiles(t) {
		if linked[filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(path))] {
			files[path] = f
		}
	}
	// body of runnable_registration_test.go:702-774 over files, the replay
	// controllers' "replay-" prefix included; floor: >= 30 chains.

// Among module packages cmd/agent links, only the two engines build a
// controller; markers, transcode and ui link none (§10.3.2).
func TestOnlyTheManagerRegistersControllers(t *testing.T) {
	builds := func(f *ast.File) bool {
		found := false
		ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
			call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr)
			if !ok {
				return true
			}
			if sel, ok := call.Fun.(*ast.SelectorExpr); ok {
				switch sel.Sel.Name {
				case "NewControllerManagedBy", "ControllerManagedBy", "NewTypedControllerManagedBy":
					found = true
				case "New", "NewTyped", "NewUnmanaged", "NewTypedUnmanaged":
					if x, ok := sel.X.(*ast.Ident); ok && importAlias(f, "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/controller", "controller") == x.Name {
						found = true
					}
				}
			}
			return true
		})
		return found
	}
	files := productionFiles(t)
	for bin, allowed := range map[string][]string{
		"cmd/agent":     {"app/grab/engine/torrent", "app/grab/engine/usenet"},
		"cmd/markers":   nil,
		"cmd/transcode": nil,
		"cmd/ui":        nil,
	} {
		env := linuxStatic
		if bin == "cmd/agent" {
			env = linuxCgo
		}
		linked := moduleDirs(depguard.Load(t, mod+bin, env...))
		builders := map[string]bool{}
		for path, f := range files {
			if dir := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(path)); linked[dir] && builds(f) {
				builders[dir] = true
			}
		}
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, allowed, slices.Collect(maps.Keys(builders)), "%s links controller builders", bin)
	}
}

// R9: a leader-only runnable (a type whose NeedLeaderElection returns true,
// or a k8s.LeaderOnly wrapper) is wired only where cmd/manager links and no
// other binary does.
func TestLeaderOnlyRunnablesLiveInTheManager(t *testing.T) {
	managerOnly := moduleDirs(depguard.Load(t, mod+"cmd/manager", linuxStatic...))
	for _, bin := range []struct{ pkg string; env []string }{
		{"cmd/agent", linuxCgo}, {"cmd/markers", []string{"CGO_ENABLED=0"}}, {"cmd/transcode", []string{"CGO_ENABLED=0"}}, {"cmd/ui", linuxStatic},
	} {
		for dir := range moduleDirs(depguard.Load(t, mod+bin.pkg, bin.env...)) {
			delete(managerOnly, dir)
		}
	}
	files := productionFiles(t)
	leaderTypes := map[string]bool{} // "<import path>.<Type>"
	for path, f := range files {
		for _, d := range f.Decls {
			fn, ok := d.(*ast.FuncDecl)
			if !ok || fn.Recv == nil || fn.Name.Name != "NeedLeaderElection" || fn.Body == nil || len(fn.Body.List) != 1 {
				continue
			}
			if ret, ok := fn.Body.List[0].(*ast.ReturnStmt); ok && len(ret.Results) == 1 && isIdent(ret.Results[0], "true") {
				leaderTypes[mod+filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(path))+"."+receiverTypeName(fn.Recv.List[0].Type)] = true
			}
		}
	}
	var sites int
	for path, f := range files {
		dir := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(path))
		if dir == "pkg/k8s" {
			continue // declares LeaderOnly
		}
		ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
			sel, ok := n.(*ast.SelectorExpr)
			if !ok {
				return true
			}
			x, ok := sel.X.(*ast.Ident)
			if !ok {
				return true
			}
			ip := importPathOf(f, x.Name)
			if (ip == mod+"pkg/k8s" && sel.Sel.Name == "LeaderOnly") || leaderTypes[ip+"."+sel.Sel.Name] {
				sites++
				assert.True(t, managerOnly[dir], "%s wires the leader-only %s.%s, but %s is linked by a binary that never elects (R9)",
					path, x.Name, sel.Sel.Name, dir)
			}
			return true
		})
	}
	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, sites, 4, "found %d leader-only wiring sites; this guard is not looking where it thinks it is", sites)
}
```

  (`importPathOf(f, name)` resolves a file's import by its local name; it lives in `astutil_test.go`.)
  `leaderTypes` also gets, for each leader type, the exported functions of its declaring package
  whose first result is the type or a pointer to it (the `ctors` computation of
  `serviceComponents`), so a runnable wired through `artwork.NewReaper(...)` is a site too.

```go
// Every ctrl.NewManager / manager.New in production code wraps its options in
// k8s.WithBaseContext, discovered rather than listed (§10.3.3).
func TestEveryManagerGetsTheBaseContext(t *testing.T) {
	var calls int
	for path, f := range productionFiles(t) {
		ctrlAlias := importAlias(f, "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime", "controllerruntime")
		mgrAlias := importAlias(f, "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/manager", "manager")
		k8sAlias := importAlias(f, mod+"pkg/k8s", "k8s")
		ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
			call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr)
			if !ok || !(isSelector(call.Fun, ctrlAlias, "NewManager") || isSelector(call.Fun, mgrAlias, "New")) {
				return true
			}
			calls++
			wrapped := slices.ContainsFunc(call.Args, func(a ast.Expr) bool {
				inner, ok := a.(*ast.CallExpr)
				return ok && isSelector(inner.Fun, k8sAlias, "WithBaseContext")
			})
			assert.True(t, wrapped, "%s: a manager built without k8s.WithBaseContext runs every runnable under the discard logger", path)
			return true
		})
	}
	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, calls, 2, "the manager and the agent each build one")
}
```

```go
// Every bus connection carries the trace hooks: busconn.Connect with
// busconn.WithHooks(obs.BusHooks()), and natsbus.New (markers, transcode,
// which must not link pkg/obs) with the inline tracing hooks. pkg/busconn's own
// natsbus.New is the implementation of Connect and is exempt.
func TestEveryBusConnectionCarriesTraceHooks(t *testing.T) {
	var connects, news int
	for path, f := range productionFiles(t) {
		busconnAlias := importAlias(f, mod+"pkg/busconn", "busconn")
		obsAlias := importAlias(f, mod+"pkg/obs", "obs")
		natsbusAlias := importAlias(f, mod+"pkg/events/natsbus", "natsbus")
		tracingAlias := importAlias(f, mod+"pkg/obs/tracing", "tracing")
		ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
			call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr)
			if !ok {
				return true
			}
			switch {
			case isSelector(call.Fun, busconnAlias, "Connect"):
				connects++
				assert.True(t, hasCall(call.Args, busconnAlias, "WithHooks", func(c *ast.CallExpr) bool {
					return hasCall(c.Args, obsAlias, "BusHooks", nil)
				}), "%s: busconn.Connect without busconn.WithHooks(obs.BusHooks())", path)
			case isSelector(call.Fun, natsbusAlias, "New") && !strings.HasPrefix(path, "pkg/busconn/"):
				news++
				assert.True(t, hasCall(call.Args, natsbusAlias, "WithHooks", func(c *ast.CallExpr) bool {
					return inlineHooks(c, tracingAlias)
				}), "%s: natsbus.New without the tracing hooks", path)
			}
			return true
		})
	}
	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, connects, 3, "manager, agent and ui connect through busconn")
	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, news, 2, "markers and transcode build their bus by hand")
}
```

  `hasCall(args, pkg, name, inner)` reports whether an argument is a call `pkg.name(...)` for which
  `inner` (nil: always) holds; `inlineHooks` holds when the call's argument is an
  `events.Hooks{...}` composite literal with `BeforePublish: tracing.Inject` and
  `AfterReceive: tracing.Extract`. Both live in `astutil_test.go`.

```go
// nats_test.go. Every clustarr Deployment dials NATS (manager, agents, ui,
// markers alike), so every one must carry NATS_URL, and one installer names one
// endpoint. Keyed on the installers' own labels until the installers wave keys
// it on binpath commands (§10.3.3).
func TestEveryClustarrDeploymentCarriesNATSURL(t *testing.T) {
	check := func(t *testing.T, installer string, deps []appsv1.Deployment) {
		urls := map[string]string{}
		for _, d := range deps {
			var url string
			for _, e := range d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0].Env {
				if e.Name == "NATS_URL" {
					url = e.Value
				}
			}
			require.NotEmptyf(t, url, "%s: Deployment %q sets no NATS_URL; it would dial %q, which no installer creates",
				installer, d.Name, "nats://clustarr-nats:4222")
			urls[d.Name] = url
		}
		require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(urls), 7, "%s: too few clustarr Deployments checked", installer)
		var ui string
		for name := range urls {
			if strings.HasSuffix(name, "ui") {
				ui = name
			}
		}
		require.NotEmpty(t, ui, "%s: the ui Deployment was not checked", installer)
		for name, url := range urls {
			require.Equalf(t, urls[ui], url, "%s: Deployment %q dials a different NATS from the ui", installer, name)
		}
	}
	t.Run("kustomize", func(t *testing.T) {
		paths, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(installtest.RepoRoot(t), "config/manager/*.yaml"))
		require.NoError(t, err)
		var all []appsv1.Deployment
		for _, p := range paths {
			all = append(all, installtest.DeploymentsIn(t, p)...)
		}
		check(t, "config/manager", all)
	})
	t.Run("chart", func(t *testing.T) {
		var ours []appsv1.Deployment
		for _, d := range installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.RenderChart(t)).Deployments {
			if d.Spec.Template.Labels["app.kubernetes.io/name"] == "clustarr" {
				ours = append(ours, d)
			}
		}
		check(t, "charts/clustarr", ours)
	})
}
```

```go
// engine_identity_test.go. The Deployment that renders engines is the one
// carrying the engine image variable (today grabarr's CLUSTARR_ENGINE_IMAGE,
// after the installers wave the manager's CLUSTARR_NATIVE_IMAGE).
func engineRenderer(t *testing.T, r installtest.Rendered) (appsv1.Deployment, map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, d := range r.Deployments {
		env := map[string]string{}
		for _, e := range d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0].Env {
			if e.ValueFrom == nil {
				env[e.Name] = e.Value
			}
		}
		if _, ok := env["CLUSTARR_ENGINE_IMAGE"]; ok {
			return d, env
		}
		if _, ok := env["CLUSTARR_NATIVE_IMAGE"]; ok {
			return d, env
		}
	}
	t.Fatal("no Deployment carries the engine image")
	return appsv1.Deployment{}, nil
}

func renders(t *testing.T) map[string]installtest.Rendered {
	return map[string]installtest.Rendered{
		"helm template clustarr":   installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.RenderChart(t)),
		"helm template media":      installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.Run(t, installtest.RepoRoot(t), installtest.FindTool(t, "helm"), "template", "media", "charts/clustarr")),
		"kustomize config/default": installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.BuildKustomize(t, "config/default")),
	}
}

func TestManagerStampsAClaimTheInstallerCreates(t *testing.T) {
	for name, r := range renders(t) {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			dep, env := engineRenderer(t, r)
			claim := cmp.Or(env["CLUSTARR_DATA_CLAIM"], downloadclient.DefaultDataClaimName)
			require.True(t, r.Claims[claim], "engines would mount PVC %q, which %s does not create", claim, name)
			var mounted string
			for _, v := range dep.Spec.Template.Spec.Volumes {
				if v.Name == "data" && v.PersistentVolumeClaim != nil {
					mounted = v.PersistentVolumeClaim.ClaimName
				}
			}
			require.Equal(t, mounted, claim, "the engines would mount a different /data than the controller that sizes it")
		})
	}
}

func TestEnginesRunAsAnAccountTheInstallerBinds(t *testing.T) {
	want := installtest.SortedGrants(installtest.GrantsOf(installtest.ReadRole(t, installtest.RepoRoot(t), "grabarr_engine_role.yaml").Rules))
	for name, r := range renders(t) {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			_, env := engineRenderer(t, r)
			account := cmp.Or(env["CLUSTARR_ENGINE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT"], downloadclient.DefaultEngineServiceAccount)
			require.True(t, r.ServiceAccounts[account],
				"engine pods would run as ServiceAccount %q, which %s does not create", account, name)
			var boundTo []string
			for _, b := range r.Bindings {
				for _, s := range b.Subjects {
					if s.Kind == "ServiceAccount" && s.Name == account {
						boundTo = append(boundTo, b.RoleRef.Name)
					}
				}
			}
			require.Len(t, boundTo, 1, "engine ServiceAccount %q is bound to %v, not exactly the engine ClusterRole", account, boundTo)
			role, ok := r.Roles[boundTo[0]]
			require.True(t, ok, "ClusterRole %q is not rendered by %s", boundTo[0], name)
			require.Equal(t, want, installtest.SortedGrants(installtest.GrantsOf(role.Rules)),
				"the ClusterRole engine pods run under is not the generated engine role")
		})
	}
}
```

```go
// manager_values_test.go. The pools' renderer is the Deployment carrying the
// pool image variable (today squasharr's CLUSTARR_WORKER_IMAGE, later the
// manager's CLUSTARR_NATIVE_IMAGE); the chart key is today's
// squasharr.intelRenderGroups until the installers wave moves it to the manager.
func TestIntelRenderGroupsReachTheManager(t *testing.T) {
	for name, tc := range map[string]struct {
		args []string
		want []int64
	}{
		"set":   {args: []string{"--set", "squasharr.intelRenderGroups={44,109}"}, want: []int64{44, 109}},
		"unset": {},
	} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			var got []int64
			var found bool
			for _, d := range installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.RenderChart(t, tc.args...)).Deployments {
				env := map[string]string{}
				for _, e := range d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0].Env {
					env[e.Name] = e.Value
				}
				_, worker := env["CLUSTARR_WORKER_IMAGE"]
				_, native := env["CLUSTARR_NATIVE_IMAGE"]
				if !worker && !native {
					continue
				}
				found = true
				var err error
				got, err = ctrlflags.ParseGIDs(env["CLUSTARR_INTEL_RENDER_GROUPS"])
				require.NoError(t, err)
			}
			require.True(t, found, "no Deployment renders the transcode pools")
			require.Equal(t, tc.want, got)
		})
	}
}
```

```go
// Only the manager creates or updates topology (§5.9): busconn.EnsureTopology,
// busconn.KeepTopology and busconn.WatchDeadLetters are called, package-
// qualified, only from internal/cli/manager. pkg/busconn's own KeepTopology
// calls EnsureTopology unqualified, inside the package, which is the one
// other caller §5.15 allows.
func TestOnlyTheManagerEnsuresTopology(t *testing.T) {
	var managerCalls int
	for path, f := range productionFiles(t) {
		busconnAlias := importAlias(f, mod+"pkg/busconn", "busconn")
		k8sAlias := importAlias(f, mod+"pkg/k8s", "k8s")
		ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
			call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr)
			if !ok {
				return true
			}
			for _, name := range []string{"EnsureTopology", "KeepTopology", "WatchDeadLetters"} {
				if !isSelector(call.Fun, busconnAlias, name) && !isSelector(call.Fun, k8sAlias, name) {
					continue
				}
				if strings.HasPrefix(path, "internal/cli/manager/") {
					managerCalls++
					continue
				}
				t.Errorf("%s calls %s: only the manager writes topology, so an older agent can never revert a newer one (§5.9)", path, name)
			}
			return true
		})
	}
	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, managerCalls, 3, "internal/cli/manager ensures, keeps and watches")
}
```

```go
// Declared indexes are registered once, by the agent (§3.5.2 step 9), never by
// a worker: among the packages only the agent links, IndexField appears only here.
func TestTheAgentIsTheOnlyIndexRegistrar(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	agentDirs := moduleDirs(depguard.Load(t, "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/cmd/agent", "CGO_ENABLED=1", "GOOS=linux", "GOARCH=amd64"))
	for dir := range moduleDirs(depguard.Load(t, "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/cmd/manager", "CGO_ENABLED=0", "GOOS=linux", "GOARCH=amd64")) {
		delete(agentDirs, dir) // shared packages (app/caption/itemindex) register for the manager's controllers
	}
	var here int
	for dir := range agentDirs {
		for _, file := range goFiles(t, filepath.Join(root, dir)) {
			f, err := parser.ParseFile(token.NewFileSet(), file, nil, parser.SkipObjectResolution)
			require.NoError(t, err)
			ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
				if sel, ok := n.(*ast.SelectorExpr); ok && sel.Sel.Name == "IndexField" {
					if dir == "internal/cli/agent" {
						here++
					} else {
						t.Errorf("%s registers a field index itself; declare it in the domain's Registration (§3.5.2)", file)
					}
				}
				return true
			})
		}
	}
	require.Positive(t, here, "internal/cli/agent registers the declared indexes")
}
```

`test/starttest/indexes.go`:

```go
// RegisterIndexes registers each declared index on idx once, as
// internal/cli/agent does, for a test that builds its manager by hand. It
// lives here, under test/, because only internal/cli/agent may call
// IndexField in code a binary links (TestTheAgentIsTheOnlyIndexRegistrar).
// A (kind, name) declared by two slices is registered once.
func RegisterIndexes(ctx context.Context, idx client.FieldIndexer, ix ...[]k8s.FieldIndex) error {
	type key struct {
		kind reflect.Type
		name string
	}
	seen := map[key]bool{}
	for _, set := range ix {
		for _, fi := range set {
			k := key{reflect.TypeOf(fi.Object), fi.Name}
			if seen[k] {
				continue
			}
			seen[k] = true
			if err := idx.IndexField(ctx, fi.Object, fi.Name, fi.Extract); err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("starttest: field index %q on %T: %w", fi.Name, fi.Object, err)
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}
```

### Task W5.19: `TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome`

> Runs after W5.17 and before the gate W5.18: it needs the five binaries and the eight domain packages as roots, and no `cmd/clustarr` or `app/<svc>` root left to link everything.

**Spec:** §5.15 (`TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome`, R7), §5.2 (the "After" column), §5.3.2 (the session store's `s.Manager`, attributed to its constructor's caller), §5.3.6 (`clustarr-autoscale`)
**Files:**
- Create: `test/guards/fieldmanager_test.go`
**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: W5.14's `depguard.Load(t, pkg, env...) Graph` with `Has` and `Chain`; W5.15's `productionFiles(t, dirs...) map[string]*ast.File` and `isSelector`/`importAlias` (`test/guards/astutil_test.go`); W4.20's `clients.NewSessionStore(c, bus, mgr)`; every `k8s.Manager*` constant (`k8s.FieldManagers()`), including Wave 4d's `k8s.ManagerAutoscale`.
- Produces: the guard only.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the test.** `test/guards/fieldmanager_test.go` (package `guards`):

```go
// homeRoots are §5.15's home roots, package-granular on purpose: each agent
// domain has its own registration package so a writer's home is the domain
// that links it, not the one agent binary that links every domain.
var homeRoots = map[string]string{
	"manager": mod + "cmd/manager", "ui": mod + "cmd/ui", "markers": mod + "cmd/markers", "transcode": mod + "cmd/transcode",
	"catalog": mod + "app/catalog/agent/catalog", "events": mod + "app/catalog/agent/events",
	"metadata": mod + "app/catalog/agent/metadata", "import": mod + "app/import/agent", "index": mod + "app/indexer/agent",
	"caption": mod + "app/caption/agent", "torrent-engine": mod + "app/grab/agent/torrent", "usenet-engine": mod + "app/grab/agent/usenet",
}

// wantHomes is §5.2's "After" column.
var wantHomes = map[k8s.FieldManager][]string{
	k8s.ManagerCatalogarr: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerCatalogarrSeries: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerCatalogarrFanout: {"manager"},
	k8s.ManagerCatalogarrClassify: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerCatalogarrWorker: {"catalog"}, k8s.ManagerCatalogarrGrab: {"catalog", "events"},
	k8s.ManagerCatalogarrMetadata: {"metadata"}, k8s.ManagerCatalogarrArtwork: {"catalog"}, k8s.ManagerCatalogarrMarkers: {"metadata"},
	k8s.ManagerImportarr: {"import", "manager"}, k8s.ManagerImportarrWorker: {"import", "manager"},
	k8s.ManagerIndexarr: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerIndexarrWorker: {"index"},
	k8s.ManagerGrabarr: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerGrabarrEngine: {"torrent-engine", "usenet-engine"},
	k8s.ManagerSquasharr: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerSquasharrPool: {"manager"},
	k8s.ManagerCaptionarr: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerCaptionarrWorker: {"caption"},
	k8s.ManagerDLQProjector: {"events"}, k8s.ManagerUI: {"ui"}, k8s.ManagerAutoscale: {"manager"},
}

// multiHome are the names §5.15 allows in more than one home.
var multiHome = map[k8s.FieldManager]bool{
	k8s.ManagerCatalogarrGrab: true, k8s.ManagerImportarr: true, k8s.ManagerImportarrWorker: true, k8s.ManagerGrabarrEngine: true,
}

// linkedNotWritten lists a home that links a writer package it never calls
// (the package-level graph over-approximates), with the reason. Empty until
// the scan shows a case; each entry needs a sentence a reviewer can check.
var linkedNotWritten = map[k8s.FieldManager]map[string]string{}

// aliases are the non-pkg/k8s names for a manager (§5.15's list).
var aliases = map[string]k8s.FieldManager{
	"rescan.FieldManager": k8s.ManagerImportarrWorker, "fileimport.FieldManager": k8s.ManagerImportarrWorker,
	"importlist.FieldManager": k8s.ManagerImportarrWorker, "mediafilespec.FieldManager": k8s.ManagerImportarrWorker,
	"fetch.FieldManager": k8s.ManagerCaptionarrWorker, "catalogstatus.GatewayManager": k8s.ManagerCatalogarrMetadata,
	"catalogstatus.RendererManager": k8s.ManagerCatalogarrArtwork, "actions.FieldManager": k8s.ManagerUI,
}

// fixedManagerWrappers are status-package writers that take no manager
// argument because they always write one.
var fixedManagerWrappers = map[string]k8s.FieldManager{
	mod + "app/squash/status.PatchCAS": k8s.ManagerSquasharr,
}

// writeFuncs are the calls whose arguments name the writing manager.
var writeFuncs = map[string]bool{
	"PatchStatus": true, "PatchStatusCAS": true, "Apply": true, "FieldOwner": true,
	"Patch": true, "PatchCAS": true, "PatchOverlay": true, "PatchRequest": true, "PatchProfile": true, "PatchProvider": true,
	"NewSessionStore": true, // §5.3.2: the store writes as the manager its constructor's caller names
}

func TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome(t *testing.T) {
	byName := map[string]k8s.FieldManager{}
	for _, m := range k8s.FieldManagers() {
		byName["k8s.Manager"+managerSuffix(m)] = m
	}
	// writers: manager -> the packages holding a write naming it.
	writers := map[k8s.FieldManager]map[string]bool{}
	for path, f := range productionFiles(t) {
		dir := filepath.Dir(path)
		if dir == "pkg/k8s" || regexp.MustCompile(`^app/[a-z]+/status$`).MatchString(dir) {
			continue // declaration-only (§5.15)
		}
		pkg := mod + dir
		imports := importsOf(f) // alias -> import path
		ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
			call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr)
			if !ok {
				return true
			}
			name, qual := calleeName(call.Fun)
			if !writeFuncs[name] {
				return true
			}
			found := false
			for _, arg := range call.Args {
				if m, ok := managerOf(arg, byName, aliases); ok {
					addWriter(writers, m, pkg)
					found = true
				}
			}
			if !found {
				if m, ok := fixedManagerWrappers[imports[qual]+"."+name]; ok {
					addWriter(writers, m, pkg)
				}
			}
			return true
		})
	}

	graphs := map[string]depguard.Graph{}
	for home, root := range homeRoots {
		env := []string{"GOOS=linux", "GOARCH=amd64", "CGO_ENABLED=0"}
		if strings.HasPrefix(root, mod+"app/") && home != "ui" {
			env[2] = "CGO_ENABLED=1" // the agent's build mode (§3.9)
		}
		graphs[home] = depguard.Load(t, root, env...)
	}
	for _, m := range k8s.FieldManagers() {
		want, ok := wantHomes[m]
		require.True(t, ok, "%s has no row in §5.2's After column: add it to wantHomes", m)
		got := map[string]bool{}
		for pkg := range writers[m] {
			for home, g := range graphs {
				if g.Has(pkg) && linkedNotWritten[m][home] == "" {
					got[home] = true
				}
			}
		}
		homes := slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(got))
		assert.Equal(t, want, homes, "%s is written from %v (writer packages %v); §5.2 says %v", m, homes, slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(writers[m])), want)
		if !multiHome[m] {
			assert.LessOrEqual(t, len(homes), 1, "%s is reachable from two homes: one field manager per process (R7)", m)
		}
	}
}
```

  plus four small helpers in the same file: `managerSuffix(m k8s.FieldManager) string` (the constant's
  identifier suffix, from a table built by parsing `pkg/k8s/fieldmanager.go`'s `ManagerX FieldManager = "…"`
  lines, so the guard never restates the names); `calleeName(fun ast.Expr) (name, qualifier string)` (a
  selector's `Sel` and its `X` identifier, or a bare identifier); `managerOf(arg ast.Expr, byName, aliases)
  (k8s.FieldManager, bool)` (a `k8s.ManagerX` selector, a known alias selector or bare `FieldManager` in the
  alias's own package, and the same wrapped in `string(…)` or followed by `.String()`); `importsOf(f)`
  (alias → import path, the default alias being the path's last element); and `addWriter`.

```bash
git commit -m "test(guards): TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome -- every write's field manager is reachable only from the homes spec §5.2 gives it, by package-granular roots (the five binaries and the eight domain packages) (spec 2026-10-06 §5.15, R7)" -- test/guards/fieldmanager_test.go
```

## Wave 6: images, installers, RBAC, KEDA removal, e2e renames (W6.1 to W6.17)

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-manager-agent-split-design.md` §10.0-§10.4,
§4.6 (RBAC paths), §3.9 (build modes), §3.10 (`make run-dev`), §9.7, §11.1 step 9,
§13 OD33, OD34, OD37-OD45. Verified against the worktree at `4b103429` (local main
`cdbdd870` plus the spec commit) and, for the drift, local `main` at `e8134264`.

This is the wave the other waves call "the installers wave"
(§11.1 step 9). It runs after Wave 5 (W5.18 green).

**Goal.** Two images replace four: `ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr` (static, `manager` and
`ui`) and `ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr/native` (FROM scratch, `agent`, `markers`,
`transcode`, plus `native-debug`). Both installers render the §10.2.1 topology
(`manager`, six `agent-<domain>` Deployments, `markers`, `ui`) with one generated
ClusterRole per identity, the External Metrics `APIService`, and no KEDA. The
Makefile, `hack/`, the GitHub workflows, `config/e2e` and `test/e2e` follow, and
every installer guard W5.16 left transitional takes its final form.

### Deviations from the spec this wave must follow

- **go.mod paths (from Wave 0).** go.mod says
  `replace github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo => ../ffgo-unify`, not `../ffgo`
  (§7.6 item 1), and requires `github.com/mediactl/par2go v0.1.0` with **no
  replace** (upgrade guide U1, OD19 resolved). Inside a build stage with
  `WORKDIR /src` the ffgo directory is `/ffgo-unify`, so every Dockerfile writes
  `COPY --from=ffgo / /ffgo-unify/` (§10.1.2 and §10.1.5 say `/ffgo/`), and no
  Dockerfile declares a `par2go` stage or context. The Makefile derives the
  directory names from go.mod rather than restating them, and a guard
  (`TestEveryGoBuildingDockerfileCarriesTheReplaceStages`, W6.4) holds every
  Dockerfile to go.mod.
- **par2go is a published module, not a build context** (U1): `make contexts` exports
  only ffgo (the spec's strict check: a clean `../ffgo-unify` at `v0.0.0-clustarr.13`),
  and every `libpar2shim.so` is the `v0.1.0` release asset checked against
  `hack/par2go/SHA256SUMS` (W0.24). The tasks below whose text still builds or exports
  par2go carry a **U1 amendment**, which overrides that text.
- **The native image stages only the seven FFmpeg libraries ffgo loads** (U3): W6.5 and
  W6.6 carry **U3 amendments**.
- **The native image is per-architecture** (main `142d0d4b`, after the spec): §10.1.3's
  single `native` stage sets `LIBVA_*` on both architectures, the bug `142d0d4b` fixed in
  `Dockerfile.transcoder`. `native` is `FROM native-${TARGETARCH}` over a shared
  FROM-scratch `native-base`, and only `native-amd64` sets `LIBVA_*` (W6.5).
- **§11.1 step 9's rule.** The native image lands without the par2 stage, the
  `libpar2shim.so` trace entry, `ENV PAR2GO_LIB`, the par2 notices, `self-check:par2-child`
  and the ffgo/par2go parts of `agent --self-check`. `self-check:markers` also waits:
  `cmd/markers --self-check` arrives with markers decode (§11.1 step 10; W5.12 keeps
  `--ffmpeg`). Each lands with the step that makes it exist (hand-off table below).
- **The AudioGraft drift** (spec header, "Drift since the review"). The graft Job is rendered by the
  manager's AudioGraft controller on `CLUSTARR_NATIVE_IMAGE` with `Command: [/usr/bin/transcode]`
  (W5.6), so the native image's `transcode` serves it and `TestEveryContainerNamesItsBinary` covers its
  binary through `pool.Template`'s; its RBAC (`audiografts`, `audiografts/status`, `batch/jobs`) rides
  `RBAC_PATHS_manager`'s `./app/squash/controller/...` (W6.9); `--graft-concurrency` keeps its binary
  default and no installer sets it, as today.
- **`agentdomain.Domains()` also lists `torrent-engine` and `usenet-engine`** (W4.63),
  which no installer renders. Every guard below maps a domain to a Deployment only for
  domains that have consumers.

### Wave-specific rules

- **Starts from W5.18 green.** W6.1 checks every symbol this wave consumes.
- **Installer guards change with the installers, in one task.** The parity, topology and
  RBAC-split guards read both installers at once, so a task that changes one installer
  changes the other and the guards together (W6.11 is large for that reason). Every task
  ends with `go test ./test/guards/...` green.

  tests and helpers. "Delete `TestX`" means delete that function and any file-local helper
  only it used (`go vet ./test/guards` names a helper left unused or defined twice).

  Never `docker push`, never `kind load` into kind-cluster-plex, never deploy.

- Commits are path-scoped (`git commit -m '...' -- <paths>`); `git rm`/`git mv` stage

```go
// managerConsumers are the two static durables the manager drains itself
// (spec §9.1.1): the transcode results its TranscodeJob status writer shares
// one compare-and-swap path with, and the segment planner.
var managerConsumers = []string{events.ConsumerSquasharrResults, events.ConsumerCatalogSegmentsPlan}

// deploymentOf names the Deployment that runs a domain: agent-<domain>,
// except markers, which is its own binary and Deployment.
func deploymentOf(d agentdomain.Domain) string {
	if d.Name == agentdomain.Markers {
		return "markers"
	}
	return "agent-" + d.Name
}

// consumerHomes maps each static durable to every Deployment that binds it.
func consumerHomes() map[string][]string {
	homes := map[string][]string{}
	for _, c := range managerConsumers {
		homes[c] = append(homes[c], "manager")
	}
	for _, d := range agentdomain.Domains() {
		for _, c := range d.Consumers {
			homes[c] = append(homes[c], deploymentOf(d))
		}
	}
	return homes
}

func readRepoFile(t *testing.T, root, rel string) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, rel))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	return b
}

// TestEveryConsumerHasExactlyOneHome is what remains of KEDA's
// TestCaptionarrScaledObjectCountsTheRealFetchConsumers: the autoscaler and
// the processes must count the consumers that really exist. Every static
// durable of events.Default() is bound by exactly one Deployment -- the
// manager, one agent domain or markers -- so a durable nothing drains (its
// queue only grows) or two processes drain (the manager's HPA would count
// one home's lag for both) fails here. The transcode pools' durables are
// dynamic (events.TranscodeTaskConsumerName) and not in Default(). Every
// durable has exactly one dead-letter watcher on StreamAdvisories (§5.9),
// homed with it.
func TestEveryConsumerHasExactlyOneHome(t *testing.T) {
	top := events.Default()
	homes := consumerHomes()
	fixed := agentdomain.Fixed()
	durables := map[string]events.ConsumerSpec{}
	for _, c := range top.Consumers {
		if c.Stream == events.StreamAdvisories {
			continue
		}
		durables[c.Name] = c
		switch h := homes[c.Name]; len(h) {
		case 0:
			t.Errorf("durable %s on %s has no home: no Deployment binds it, so its stream only grows", c.Name, c.Stream)
		case 1:
		default:
			t.Errorf("durable %s is bound by %v: exactly one Deployment may drain a durable", c.Name, h)
		}
		_, isFixed := fixed[c.Name]
		inAgent := len(homes[c.Name]) == 1 && homes[c.Name][0] != "manager"
		assert.NotEqual(t, isFixed, inAgent,
			"durable %s must be in exactly one of agentdomain.Domains() and agentdomain.Fixed()", c.Name)
	}
	require.NotEmpty(t, durables, "events.Default() declares no durable; this guard is not reading the topology")
	for name, h := range homes {
		_, ok := durables[name]
		assert.True(t, ok, "%v binds %s, which events.Default() does not declare", h, name)
	}
	for _, c := range top.Consumers {
		if c.Stream != events.StreamAdvisories {
			continue
		}
		var watched []string
		for _, d := range durables {
			if events.DeadLetterWatcherName(d.Stream, d.Name) == c.Name {
				watched = append(watched, d.Name)
			}
		}
		assert.Len(t, watched, 1, "dead-letter watcher %s must watch exactly one durable of the topology", c.Name)
	}
	for _, d := range durables {
		w := events.DeadLetterWatcherName(d.Stream, d.Name)
		_, ok := top.Consumer(w)
		assert.True(t, ok, "durable %s has no dead-letter watcher %s in the topology (§5.9)", d.Name, w)
	}
}

// TestNoInstallerRendersAnHPAOrKEDA: the manager's autoscale reconciler owns
// every HorizontalPodAutoscaler (R5) -- Helm's server-side apply would fight
// it over maxReplicas -- and KEDA is gone (§10.2.7): no keda.sh object in any
// render, no keda value, schema key or chart dependency, no config/keda.
func TestNoInstallerRendersAnHPAOrKEDA(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	for name, out := range map[string][]byte{
		"helm template":                  installtest.RenderChart(t),
		"helm template, servicemonitors": installtest.RenderChart(t, "--set", "metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled=true"),
		"kustomize config/default":       installtest.BuildKustomize(t, "config/default"),
		"kustomize config/e2e":           installtest.BuildKustomize(t, "config/e2e"),
	} {
		objs := installtest.Objects(t, out)
		require.NotEmpty(t, objs, name)
		for _, o := range objs {
			gvk := o.GroupVersionKind()
			assert.NotEqual(t, "keda.sh", gvk.Group, "%s renders %s %q: KEDA is removed", name, gvk.Kind, o.GetName())
			assert.NotEqual(t, "HorizontalPodAutoscaler", gvk.Kind,
				"%s renders HorizontalPodAutoscaler %q: the manager's autoscale reconciler owns every HPA", name, o.GetName())
		}
	}

	var values map[string]any
	require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(readRepoFile(t, root, "charts/clustarr/values.yaml"), &values))
	assert.NotContains(t, values, "keda", "values.yaml")
	var schema struct {
		Properties map[string]any `json:"properties"`
	}
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(readRepoFile(t, root, "charts/clustarr/values.schema.json"), &schema))
	assert.NotContains(t, schema.Properties, "keda", "values.schema.json")
	for _, f := range []string{"charts/clustarr/Chart.yaml", "charts/clustarr/Chart.lock"} {
		var c struct {
			Dependencies []struct {
				Name string `json:"name"`
			} `json:"dependencies"`
		}
		require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(readRepoFile(t, root, f), &c), f)
		require.NotEmpty(t, c.Dependencies, f)
		for _, d := range c.Dependencies {
			assert.NotEqual(t, "keda", d.Name, "%s still depends on keda", f)
		}
	}
	_, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(root, "config", "keda"))
	assert.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "config/keda is deleted with KEDA")
	tpls, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(root, "charts", "clustarr", "templates", "*"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	for _, f := range tpls {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(f)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.NotContains(t, string(b), ".Values.keda", "%s reads .Values.keda", filepath.Base(f))
	}
}
```

```go
import (
	"os"
	"os/exec"

// gitIn runs git in dir with a fixed identity, failing the test on error.
func gitIn(t *testing.T, git, dir string, args ...string) string {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := exec.Command(git, append([]string{"-c", "user.name=t", "-c", "user.email=t@example.com", "-C", dir}, args...)...)
	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
	require.NoError(t, err, "git %v: %s", args, out)
	return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
}

// newRepo makes a one-commit repository holding files.
func newRepo(t *testing.T, git, dir string, files map[string]string) string {
	t.Helper()
	for name, body := range files {
		require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(filepath.Join(dir, name)), 0o755))
		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, name), []byte(body), 0o644))
	}
	gitIn(t, git, dir, "init", "-q")
	gitIn(t, git, dir, "add", "-A")
	gitIn(t, git, dir, "commit", "-qm", "init")
	return dir
}

// TestContextsExportsPinnedCleanTrees: the image build contexts are git
// archives of the pinned refs, never the working trees other sessions edit
// (spec §7.6 item 3). ffgo must be a clean checkout of its tag, because
// go.mod builds against that working tree and the image must be the same
// code; par2go needs only the ref, because go.mod points at an export of
// it, not at ../par2go (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-06-manager-agent-split.md, Wave 0).
func TestContextsExportsPinnedCleanTrees(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	git := installtest.FindTool(t, "git")
	tmp := t.TempDir()
	ffgo := newRepo(t, git, filepath.Join(tmp, "ffgo-unify"), map[string]string{
		"go.mod": "module github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo\n", "shim/ffshim.c": "/* shim */\n"})
	gitIn(t, git, ffgo, "tag", "-a", "v0.0.0-clustarr.13", "-m", "fork")
	par2go := newRepo(t, git, filepath.Join(tmp, "par2go"), map[string]string{"go.mod": "module github.com/mediactl/par2go\n"})
	pin := gitIn(t, git, par2go, "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD")
	dest := filepath.Join(tmp, "contexts")
	contexts := func() (string, error) {
		out, err := exec.Command("bash", filepath.Join(root, "hack", "contexts.sh"),
			dest, ffgo, "v0.0.0-clustarr.13", par2go, pin).CombinedOutput()
		return string(out), err
	}

	out, err := contexts()
	require.NoError(t, err, out)
	assert.FileExists(t, filepath.Join(dest, "ffgo", "shim", "ffshim.c"))
	assert.FileExists(t, filepath.Join(dest, "par2go", "go.mod"))
	assert.NoDirExists(t, filepath.Join(dest, "ffgo", ".git"), "an export, not a clone")

	// par2go may move past its pin: the export is the pin, not HEAD.
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(par2go, "later.txt"), []byte("later\n"), 0o644))
	gitIn(t, git, par2go, "add", "later.txt")
	gitIn(t, git, par2go, "commit", "-qm", "later")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(par2go, "untracked"), nil, 0o644))
	out, err = contexts()
	require.NoError(t, err, out)
	assert.NoFileExists(t, filepath.Join(dest, "par2go", "later.txt"), "the export is the pinned commit")
	assert.NoFileExists(t, filepath.Join(dest, "par2go", "untracked"))

	// A dirty fork is refused.
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(ffgo, "shim", "ffshim.c"), []byte("/* edited */\n"), 0o644))
	out, err = contexts()
	require.Error(t, err)
	assert.Contains(t, out, "not a clean v0.0.0-clustarr.13")
	gitIn(t, git, ffgo, "checkout", "--", ".")

	// A pin the repository does not hold is refused.
	out, err = exec.Command("bash", filepath.Join(root, "hack", "contexts.sh"),
		dest, ffgo, "v0.0.0-clustarr.13", par2go, "0123456789abcdef").CombinedOutput()
	require.Error(t, err)
	assert.Contains(t, string(out), "has no commit 0123456789abcdef")
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** `hack/contexts.sh` (`chmod +x`):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# hack/contexts.sh DEST FFGO_DIR FFGO_REF PAR2GO_DIR PAR2GO_REF
#
# Exports clean trees of the ffgo fork and par2go at their pinned refs into
# DEST/ffgo and DEST/par2go: the --build-context directories every image
# build gets while go.mod replaces either module with a local directory
# (spec 2026-10-06 §7.6 item 3, §10.1.5). A build context ships whatever is
# in its directory, and the working trees are edited by other sessions (and
# par2go's holds a CMake build directory recorded at host paths), so a working
# tree is never passed: each ref is `git archive`d.
#
# ffgo must be a clean checkout of FFGO_REF, because go.mod builds against
# that working tree and the image must be the same code. par2go needs only
# the ref: go.mod points at an export of it (../par2go-1bd94eb), and
# par2go's own HEAD moves on (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-06-manager-agent-split.md, Wave 0).
set -euo pipefail
usage="usage: hack/contexts.sh DEST FFGO_DIR FFGO_REF PAR2GO_DIR PAR2GO_REF"
dest=${1:?$usage} ffgo_dir=${2:?$usage} ffgo_ref=${3:?$usage} par2go_dir=${4:?$usage} par2go_ref=${5:?$usage}
die() { printf 'contexts: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

got=$(git -C "${ffgo_dir}" describe --tags --exact-match --dirty 2>/dev/null || true)
[[ "${got}" == "${ffgo_ref}" ]] ||
  die "${ffgo_dir} is at '${got:-no tag}', not a clean ${ffgo_ref}: check out the tag and commit or drop local edits before building images"
ffgo_commit=$(git -C "${ffgo_dir}" rev-parse "${ffgo_ref}^{commit}")
par2go_commit=$(git -C "${par2go_dir}" rev-parse -q --verify "${par2go_ref}^{commit}") ||
  die "${par2go_dir} has no commit ${par2go_ref}"

mkdir -p "${dest}"
# export NAME DIR COMMIT: unpack beside the destination, then swap it in.
export_tree() {
  local tmp
  tmp=$(mktemp -d "${dest}/.$1.XXXXXX")
  git -C "$2" archive "$3" | tar -x -C "${tmp}"
  rm -rf "${dest}/.$1.old"
  if [[ -e "${dest}/$1" ]]; then mv "${dest}/$1" "${dest}/.$1.old"; fi
  mv "${tmp}" "${dest}/$1"
  rm -rf "${dest}/.$1.old"
}
export_tree ffgo "${ffgo_dir}" "${ffgo_commit}"
export_tree par2go "${par2go_dir}" "${par2go_commit}"
printf '%s\n' "${dest}/ffgo ${ffgo_ref} (${ffgo_commit})" "${dest}/par2go ${par2go_ref} (${par2go_commit})"
```

  `Makefile`: below `TRANSCODER_IMG ?= …` (`:17`) insert:

```make
# The ffgo fork and par2go, which go.mod replaces with local directories until
# their tags are published (spec §7.6, R12; Wave 0 of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-06-manager-agent-split.md names the directories).
# Image builds never read those working trees: `make contexts` exports
# $(FFGO_REF) and $(PAR2GO_REF) with git archive, and every docker build
# passes them as the named contexts the Dockerfiles' empty ffgo and par2go
# stages stand in for. FFGO_LOCAL/PAR2GO_LOCAL are the directories go.mod
# names (empty once go.mod replaces with a published version).
FFGO_LOCAL := $(shell sed -nE 's#^replace github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo => \.\./(.+)$$#\1#p' go.mod)
PAR2GO_LOCAL := $(shell sed -nE 's#^replace github.com/mediactl/par2go => \.\./(.+)$$#\1#p' go.mod)
FFGO_DIR ?= ../$(or $(FFGO_LOCAL),ffgo)
PAR2GO_DIR ?= ../par2go
FFGO_REF ?= v0.0.0-clustarr.13
PAR2GO_REF ?= 1bd94eb
CONTEXTS ?= $(or $(TMPDIR),/tmp)/clustarr-contexts-$(USER)
LOCAL_CONTEXTS := $(if $(FFGO_LOCAL)$(PAR2GO_LOCAL),--build-context ffgo=$(CONTEXTS)/ffgo --build-context par2go=$(CONTEXTS)/par2go --build-arg FFGO_COMMIT=$(shell git -C $(FFGO_DIR) rev-parse $(FFGO_REF)^{commit} 2>/dev/null) --build-arg PAR2GO_COMMIT=$(shell git -C $(PAR2GO_DIR) rev-parse $(PAR2GO_REF)^{commit} 2>/dev/null))
```

```make
.PHONY: contexts
contexts: ## Export clean trees of $(FFGO_REF) and $(PAR2GO_REF) for the image builds (spec §7.6); refuses a dirty or moved ffgo.
	@if [ -n "$(FFGO_LOCAL)$(PAR2GO_LOCAL)" ]; then hack/contexts.sh $(CONTEXTS) $(FFGO_DIR) $(FFGO_REF) $(PAR2GO_DIR) $(PAR2GO_REF); fi

# make build and make test read the forks' working trees through go.mod;
# developing the fork additions needs a dirty tree, so this only warns.
.PHONY: fork-status
fork-status:
	@if [ -n "$(FFGO_LOCAL)" ] && [ "$$(git -C $(FFGO_DIR) describe --tags --exact-match --dirty 2>/dev/null)" != "$(FFGO_REF)" ]; then \
	  echo "WARNING: $(FFGO_DIR) is not a clean $(FFGO_REF); go.mod builds against it as it is" >&2; fi
	@if [ -n "$(PAR2GO_LOCAL)" ] && ! git -C $(PAR2GO_DIR) rev-parse -q --verify $(PAR2GO_REF)^{commit} >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  echo "WARNING: $(PAR2GO_DIR) has no commit $(PAR2GO_REF)" >&2; fi
```

```go
// stageIn finds the stage named name in Dockerfile df: the image it is built
// FROM and its instructions up to the next FROM.
func stageIn(df, name string) (from, body string, ok bool) {
	re := regexp.MustCompile(`(?im)^FROM\s+(?:--platform=\S+\s+)?(\S+)\s+AS\s+` + regexp.QuoteMeta(name) + `\s*$`)
	loc := re.FindStringSubmatchIndex(df)
	if loc == nil {
		return "", "", false
	}
	body = df[loc[1]:]
	if next := regexp.MustCompile(`(?im)^FROM\s`).FindStringIndex(body); next != nil {
		body = body[:next[0]]
	}
	return df[loc[2]:loc[3]], body, true
}

// replaceDirs maps every module go.mod replaces with a local directory to
// that directory as a build stage with WORKDIR /src sees it: "/<dir>/".
func replaceDirs(t *testing.T, root string) map[string]string {
	t.Helper()
	out := map[string]string{}
	re := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^replace (\S+) => \.\./(\S+)$`)
	for _, m := range re.FindAllStringSubmatch(string(readRepoFile(t, root, "go.mod")), -1) {
		out[m[1]] = "/" + m[2] + "/"
	}
	return out
}

// goBuildingDockerfiles are the Dockerfiles whose build stage resolves this
// module. W6.5 widens it to every images/Dockerfile*.
func goBuildingDockerfiles(t *testing.T, root string) []string {
	return []string{"images/Dockerfile.clustarr", "images/Dockerfile.e2e-fixtures"}
}

// TestEveryGoBuildingDockerfileCarriesTheReplaceStages: a directory replace
// needs the replacement's go.mod for `go mod download`, even for binaries
// that never link it (spec §7.6 item 2). So every Dockerfile that resolves
// this module declares empty ffgo and par2go stages, which `make contexts`'
// named contexts replace, and copies them, before `go mod download`, to the
// directories go.mod names.
func TestEveryGoBuildingDockerfileCarriesTheReplaceStages(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	dirs := replaceDirs(t, root)
	stageOf := map[string]string{"github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo": "ffgo", "github.com/mediactl/par2go": "par2go"}
	for mod := range dirs {
		_, ok := stageOf[mod]
		assert.True(t, ok, "go.mod replaces %s with a local directory, and no image stage stands in for it", mod)
	}
	files := goBuildingDockerfiles(t, root)
	require.NotEmpty(t, files)
	for _, f := range files {
		df := string(readRepoFile(t, root, f))
		download := strings.Index(df, "go mod download")
		require.GreaterOrEqual(t, download, 0, "%s runs no go mod download; this guard's premise changed", f)
		assert.Contains(t, df, "WORKDIR /src", "%s: the COPY targets assume /src/.. is /", f)
		for mod, stage := range stageOf {
			from, _, ok := stageIn(df, stage)
			require.True(t, ok, "%s declares no %s stage", f, stage)
			assert.Equal(t, "scratch", from, "%s: the %s stage is empty unless a build context replaces it", f, stage)
			re := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^COPY --from=` + stage + ` / (\S+)$`)
			m := re.FindStringSubmatchIndex(df)
			require.NotNil(t, m, "%s never copies the %s stage", f, stage)
			assert.Less(t, m[0], download, "%s copies the %s stage after go mod download", f, stage)
			if want, local := dirs[mod]; local {
				assert.Equal(t, want, df[m[2]:m[3]], "%s copies %s where go.mod's replace does not look", f, stage)
			}
		}
	}
}

// TestTheClustarrImageIsStatic: manager and ui are static, loader-free
// binaries (the deps guards hold that), so their image is distroless static,
// cross-compiled with cgo off, and names no ENTRYPOINT because it holds two.
func TestTheClustarrImageIsStatic(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	df := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "images/Dockerfile.clustarr"))
	from, body, ok := stageIn(df, "clustarr")
	require.True(t, ok, "Dockerfile.clustarr has no clustarr target")
	assert.Equal(t, "gcr.io/distroless/static:nonroot", from)
	assert.Contains(t, body, "COPY --from=build /out/manager /out/ui /usr/bin/")
	_, build, ok := stageIn(df, "build")
	require.True(t, ok, "Dockerfile.clustarr has no build stage")
	assert.Contains(t, build, "CGO_ENABLED=0")
	assert.Contains(t, build, "-o /out/manager ./cmd/manager")
	assert.Contains(t, build, "-o /out/ui ./cmd/ui")
	assert.NotRegexp(t, `(?m)^ENTRYPOINT`, df, "the image holds two binaries; every container names its own")
	_, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(root, "images", "Dockerfile.controller"))
	assert.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "Dockerfile.controller became Dockerfile.clustarr")
}
```

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
#
# ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr -- the manager and ui binaries, static and
# cgo-free, on distroless (spec 2026-10-06 §10.1.2, R1). Everything that
# loads FFmpeg, ONNX Runtime or par2 runs from images/Dockerfile.native. The
# deps guards (test/guards/deps_test.go) keep both binaries free of a dynamic
# loader, so they cross-compile from $BUILDPLATFORM.
#
# No ENTRYPOINT: the image holds two binaries, so every container names its
# own (pkg/binpath; TestEveryContainerNamesItsBinary).
#
#   make docker-build     # this image and the native one, with the pinned contexts

ARG GO_VERSION=1.27

# Empty unless `--build-context ffgo=<dir>` / `par2go=<dir>` replaces them.
# go.mod replaces both modules with local directories until their tags are
# published, and `go mod download` needs their go.mod files even for
# binaries that never link them (spec §7.6, §10.1.5). The COPY targets are
# go.mod's directories as /src/.. sees them;
# TestEveryGoBuildingDockerfileCarriesTheReplaceStages holds them to go.mod.
FROM scratch AS ffgo
FROM scratch AS par2go

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# build: cmd/manager and cmd/ui, CGO_ENABLED=0
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM golang:${GO_VERSION} AS build
ARG TARGETOS
ARG TARGETARCH
ARG VERSION=dev
WORKDIR /src
ENV CGO_ENABLED=0 \
    GOFLAGS=-trimpath
COPY --from=ffgo / /ffgo-unify/
COPY --from=par2go / /par2go-1bd94eb/
# Warm the module cache separately so source edits do not re-download.
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    go mod download
COPY . .
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    GOOS=${TARGETOS} GOARCH=${TARGETARCH} go build \
      -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/version.Version=${VERSION}" \
      -o /out/manager ./cmd/manager \
 && GOOS=${TARGETOS} GOARCH=${TARGETARCH} go build \
      -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/version.Version=${VERSION}" \
      -o /out/ui ./cmd/ui

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# clustarr: distroless static, non-root
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM gcr.io/distroless/static:nonroot AS clustarr
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/mediactl/clustarr" \
      org.opencontainers.image.licenses="GPL-3.0-only" \
      org.opencontainers.image.title="clustarr"
COPY --from=build /out/manager /out/ui /usr/bin/
USER 65532:65532
```

```go
// goBuildingDockerfiles are the Dockerfiles whose build stage resolves this
// module: every images/Dockerfile* that runs `go mod download`.
func goBuildingDockerfiles(t *testing.T, root string) []string {
	t.Helper()
	all, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(root, "images", "Dockerfile*"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	var out []string
	for _, f := range all {
		rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, f)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		if strings.Contains(string(readRepoFile(t, root, rel)), "go mod download") {
			out = append(out, rel)
		}
	}
	return out
}
```

```go
// TestTheNativeImageCarriesNoMediaExecutable: every binary in the native
// image runs FFmpeg and par2 as libraries (R2), so neither the Dockerfile nor
// stage.sh may put an ffmpeg, ffprobe or par2 executable in it, and stage.sh's
// last step refuses one that arrives some other way (a package the Intel
// runtime pulls in, say). The images that carried them stay gone.
func TestTheNativeImageCarriesNoMediaExecutable(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	installs := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^[^#\n]*(/usr/(local/)?bin/(ffmpeg|ffprobe|par2)\b|bin/(ffmpeg|ffprobe|par2)\s+\S*/usr/(local/)?bin)`)
	for _, f := range []string{"images/Dockerfile.native", "images/distroless/stage.sh"} {
		if m := installs.Find(readRepoFile(t, root, f)); m != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s puts a media executable in the native image: %q", f, m)
		}
	}
	stage := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "images/distroless/stage.sh"))
	assert.Regexp(t, `(?s)for f in ffmpeg ffprobe par2; do.*exit 1`, stage, "stage.sh refuses a staged ffmpeg, ffprobe or par2")
	df := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "images/Dockerfile.native"))
	from, _, ok := stageIn(df, "native-base")
	require.True(t, ok, "the native-base stage")
	assert.Equal(t, "scratch", from, "the native image is FROM scratch")
	from, _, ok = stageIn(df, "native")
	require.True(t, ok, "the native target")
	assert.Equal(t, "native-${TARGETARCH}", from, "native is its architecture's stage")
	for _, gone := range []string{"Dockerfile.media", "Dockerfile.transcoder", "Dockerfile.controller", "Dockerfile.transcoder-distroless"} {
		_, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(root, "images", gone))
		assert.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "images/%s stays gone", gone)
	}
}

// Every pool, Intel's included, and every agent run the one native image
// (ADR 0015, OD43), so it carries the Intel media runtime -- the iHD VAAPI
// driver and both QSV runtimes, which nothing injects at run time the way the
// NVIDIA runtime injects NVIDIA's. The runtime is amd64's alone, and so is the
// environment pointing libva at it (main 142d0d4b): native picks its
// architecture's stage, and arm64's, which stages no libva, sets none.
func TestTheNativeImageCarriesTheIntelStack(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	df := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "images/Dockerfile.native"))
	assert.NotRegexp(t, `(?im)^FROM\s+\S+\s+AS\s+\S*intel`, df, "no Intel-only target")
	for _, arch := range []string{"amd64", "arm64"} {
		from, _, ok := stageIn(df, "native-"+arch)
		require.True(t, ok, "the native-%s stage", arch)
		assert.Equal(t, "native-base", from, "native-%s builds on native-base", arch)
	}
	_, amd64, _ := stageIn(df, "native-amd64")
	assert.Contains(t, amd64, "LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/dri")
	assert.Contains(t, amd64, "LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD")
	_, arm64, _ := stageIn(df, "native-arm64")
	assert.NotContains(t, arm64, "LIBVA_", "arm64 stages no libva")
	_, base, _ := stageIn(df, "native-base")
	assert.NotContains(t, base, "LIBVA_", "libva's environment is amd64's alone")
	staging := regexp.MustCompile(`COPY --from=(\S+) /staging/ /`).FindStringSubmatch(base)
	require.NotNil(t, staging, "native-base copies a staging tree")
	_, st, ok := stageIn(df, staging[1])
	require.True(t, ok, "the %s stage", staging[1])
	for _, pkg := range []string{"intel-media-va-driver-non-free", "libmfx-gen1.2", "libmfx1/bookworm"} {
		assert.Contains(t, st, pkg, "the native image's staging installs %s", pkg)
	}
}

// TestTheNativeImageStagesEveryBinaryItBuilds: the three binaries are built
// as §3.9 says (the agent with cgo, R13: sqlite piece completion and
// go-libutp; markers and transcode purego), copied into the staging tree,
// and traced by stage.sh, whose trace fails on a missing file, so a binary
// the build drops fails the image. ONNX Runtime is traced too: markers'
// text detector loads it.
func TestTheNativeImageStagesEveryBinaryItBuilds(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	df := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "images/Dockerfile.native"))
	_, build, ok := stageIn(df, "build")
	require.True(t, ok, "the build stage")
	assert.Regexp(t, `CGO_ENABLED=1 go build [^\n]*-o /out/agent \./cmd/agent`, build)
	assert.Regexp(t, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build [^\n]*-o /out/markers \./cmd/markers`, build)
	assert.Regexp(t, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build [^\n]*-o /out/transcode \./cmd/transcode`, build)
	assert.Contains(t, df, "COPY --from=build /out/agent /out/markers /out/transcode /usr/bin/")
	trace := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^trace (/usr/bin/.+)$`).FindStringSubmatch(string(readRepoFile(t, root, "images/distroless/stage.sh")))
	require.NotNil(t, trace, "stage.sh's trace line")
	traced := strings.Fields(trace[1])
	for _, f := range []string{"/usr/bin/agent", "/usr/bin/markers", "/usr/bin/transcode", "/usr/lib/libffshim.so", "/usr/lib/libonnxruntime.so"} {
		assert.Contains(t, traced, f, "stage.sh traces %s", f)
	}
	assert.NotRegexp(t, `(?m)^ENTRYPOINT`, df, "the image holds three binaries; every container names its own")
}
```

  1. `git mv images/Dockerfile.transcoder images/Dockerfile.native` and `git rm images/Dockerfile.media`
     (its ORT stage moves into `native`; its ffmpeg, ffprobe and par2 fetches go, R2).
  2. Replace `images/Dockerfile.native`'s content with:

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
#
# ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr/native -- the agent, markers and transcode
# binaries on FFmpeg 9's libraries, FROM scratch (spec 2026-10-06 §10.1.3,
# R1, R2). Targets:
#
#   native        every agent domain (the download engines included), markers,
#                 every transcode pool (cpu, nvidia, intel) and the AudioGraft
#                 Jobs; amd64 and arm64 (Intel's VAAPI driver and QSV runtimes
#                 on amd64 only)
#   native-debug  the same plus a static busybox, for kubectl exec
#
#   make docker-build-native     # both, with the pinned build contexts
#
# No ENTRYPOINT: the image holds three binaries, so every container names its
# own (pkg/binpath; TestEveryContainerNamesItsBinary), and one that names none
# fails at once instead of starting the wrong program.
#
# There is no CUDA target (docs/adr/0015-no-cuda-image.md). An nvidia pool
# runs `native`: the NVIDIA container runtime injects the driver's libraries
# (libcuda, libnvidia-encode, libnvcuvid) into a pod that asks for them with
# runtimeClassName, an nvidia.com/gpu request and
# NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=video,compute,utility
# (app/squash/controller/pool.applyHardware).
#
# There is no ffmpeg, ffprobe or par2 executable in the image: every binary
# runs FFmpeg through ffgo in-process, and (from §11.1 step 12) par2 through
# par2go. stage.sh refuses all three, so a copy cannot creep back in.
#
# FFmpeg is BtbN's 9.0 shared GPL build (FFMPEG_RELEASE/FFMPEG_VERSION pin
# one, checked by its SHA-256): NVENC/NVDEC and the CUDA filters, VAAPI
# through libva (dlopen'ed), and the libvpl dispatcher. Its libraries, the
# ffgo shim compiled against the same tarball's headers from the fork's own
# shim/ffshim.c, and ONNX Runtime live in /usr/lib, which the dynamic linker
# searches without an ld.so.cache. hack/native-assets.sh reads the FFmpeg and
# ONNX Runtime pins from this file's ARG defaults, so tests load what ships.

ARG GO_VERSION=1.27
ARG FFMPEG_BRANCH=9.0

# Empty unless `--build-context ffgo=<dir>` / `par2go=<dir>` replaces them
# (spec §7.6, §10.1.5): go.mod replaces both modules with local directories
# until their tags are published. The COPY targets are go.mod's directories
# as /src/.. sees them.
FROM scratch AS ffgo
FROM scratch AS par2go

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# build: agent (cgo, R13), markers and transcode (purego), and the ffgo
# shim's source. Built on the target platform: the agent needs cgo.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM golang:${GO_VERSION}-bookworm AS build
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG FFGO_COMMIT=""
WORKDIR /src
ENV GOFLAGS=-trimpath
COPY --from=ffgo / /ffgo-unify/
COPY --from=par2go / /par2go-1bd94eb/
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod go mod download
COPY . .
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    set -eux; \
    ld="-s -w -X github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/version.Version=${VERSION}"; \
    CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -ldflags "${ld}" -o /out/agent ./cmd/agent; \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags "${ld}" -o /out/markers ./cmd/markers; \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags "${ld}" -o /out/transcode ./cmd/transcode; \
    mkdir -p /out/ffgo /out/licenses/clustarr /out/licenses/ffgo; \
    ffgo="$(go list -m -f '{{.Dir}}' github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo)"; \
    cp -r "${ffgo}/shim" /out/ffgo/; \
    cp "${ffgo}/LICENSE" /out/licenses/ffgo/LICENSE; \
    printf 'ffgo %s\nSource: https://github.com/mediactl/ffgo (a fork of https://github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo)\n' \
      "${FFGO_COMMIT:-$(go list -m -f '{{if .Replace}}{{.Replace.Path}} {{.Replace.Version}}{{else}}{{.Version}}{{end}}' github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo)}" \
      > /out/licenses/ffgo/SOURCE; \
    cp LICENSE /out/licenses/clustarr/LICENSE

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ffmpeg: BtbN's shared build into /usr, and the shim against its headers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM debian:bookworm-slim AS ffmpeg
ARG TARGETARCH
ARG FFMPEG_BRANCH
# One dated BtbN build, checked by its published SHA-256, so CI, the release
# and hack/native-assets.sh use the same FFmpeg. FFMPEG_URL (with
# FFMPEG_SHA256) overrides.
ARG FFMPEG_RELEASE=autobuild-2026-09-30-13-08
ARG FFMPEG_VERSION=n9.0.2-17-g2a571b6068
ARG FFMPEG_SHA256_AMD64=01a9764d0b5364b66cfeb4617557c64321b0e232e172ec73f0a701c5f7694326
ARG FFMPEG_SHA256_ARM64=706ccdbc8b0537646345532713a9b6750c0a6258cc001ec1c0379754f0ae730a
ARG FFMPEG_URL=""
ARG FFMPEG_SHA256=""
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl xz-utils gcc libc6-dev \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY --from=build /out/ffgo/shim /src/shim
RUN set -eux; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
      amd64) a=linux64; sum="${FFMPEG_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
      arm64) a=linuxarm64; sum="${FFMPEG_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
      *) echo "unsupported TARGETARCH=${TARGETARCH}" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
    esac; \
    url="https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases/download/${FFMPEG_RELEASE}/ffmpeg-${FFMPEG_VERSION}-${a}-gpl-shared-${FFMPEG_BRANCH}.tar.xz"; \
    if [ -n "${FFMPEG_URL}" ]; then url="${FFMPEG_URL}"; sum="${FFMPEG_SHA256}"; fi; \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/ff.tar.xz "${url}"; \
    if [ -n "${sum}" ]; then echo "${sum}  /tmp/ff.tar.xz" | sha256sum -c -; fi; \
    mkdir -p /opt/ffmpeg; \
    tar -xJf /tmp/ff.tar.xz --strip-components=1 -C /opt/ffmpeg; \
    mkdir -p /out/usr/lib /out/usr/share/licenses/ffmpeg; \
    cp -a /opt/ffmpeg/lib/lib*.so* /out/usr/lib/; \
    cp /opt/ffmpeg/LICENSE.txt /out/usr/share/licenses/ffmpeg/LICENSE.txt; \
    printf 'FFmpeg %s, built by BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds (GPL, shared): %s\nSource: https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg (the commit after the last "g" in the version)\nBuild scripts: https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds\n' \
      "$(LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/ffmpeg/lib /opt/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg -hide_banner -version 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || echo "${FFMPEG_VERSION}")" "${url}" \
      > /out/usr/share/licenses/ffmpeg/SOURCE; \
    gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -DFFSHIM_HAVE_AVDEVICE=1 -DFFSHIM_HAVE_AVFILTER=1 \
      -I/opt/ffmpeg/include -o /out/usr/lib/libffshim.so /src/shim/ffshim.c \
      -L/opt/ffmpeg/lib -lavutil -lavcodec -lavformat -lavdevice -lavfilter

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ort: ONNX Runtime's shared library, for markers' text detector
# (pkg/segments/textdet through onnxruntime-purego, C API 23 = ORT 1.23)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM debian:bookworm-slim AS ort
ARG TARGETARCH
ARG ORT_VERSION=1.23.2
ARG ORT_SHA256_AMD64=1fa4dcaef22f6f7d5cd81b28c2800414350c10116f5fdd46a2160082551c5f9b
ARG ORT_SHA256_ARM64=7c63c73560ed76b1fac6cff8204ffe34fe180e70d6582b5332ec094810241e5c
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN set -eux; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
      amd64) a=x64; sum="${ORT_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
      arm64) a=aarch64; sum="${ORT_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
      *) echo "unsupported TARGETARCH=${TARGETARCH}" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
    esac; \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/ort.tgz "https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/releases/download/v${ORT_VERSION}/onnxruntime-linux-${a}-${ORT_VERSION}.tgz"; \
    echo "${sum}  /tmp/ort.tgz" | sha256sum -c -; \
    mkdir -p /tmp/ort /out/usr/lib /out/usr/share/licenses/onnxruntime; \
    tar -xzf /tmp/ort.tgz --strip-components=1 -C /tmp/ort; \
    install -m 0644 "/tmp/ort/lib/libonnxruntime.so.${ORT_VERSION}" /out/usr/lib/libonnxruntime.so; \
    install -m 0644 /tmp/ort/LICENSE /tmp/ort/ThirdPartyNotices.txt /out/usr/share/licenses/onnxruntime/

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# staging: lddtree everything the binaries load into /staging
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Staged from Debian 13: BtbN's FFmpeg 9 calls libva 2.21's vaMapBuffer2, and
# Debian 12's libva 2.17 lacks it. glibc and libstdc++ run binaries built
# against older versions, as the agent (bookworm, cgo) and BtbN's are.
FROM debian:trixie-slim AS staging-base
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends pax-utils ca-certificates gcc binutils \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY --from=ffmpeg /out/ /
COPY --from=ort /out/ /
COPY --from=build /out/agent /out/markers /out/transcode /usr/bin/
COPY --from=build /out/licenses/ /usr/share/licenses/
COPY images/distroless/stage.sh /stage.sh

# Intel (amd64 only): Debian 13's VAAPI driver (the non-free iHD build: the
# free one has no HEVC 10-bit encode on Kaby Lake through Comet Lake) and
# libva 2.22, and both QSV runtimes -- libmfx-gen for Gen12 and newer, and
# Media SDK's libmfxhw64 for Broadwell..Ice Lake, which Debian 13 dropped, so
# it alone comes from Debian 12. All of it is dlopen'ed, so it is named for
# lddtree. On arm64 there is no Intel GPU to drive.
#
# Then the C++-symbol check (spec §7.6 item 2): ONNX Runtime is C++, and
# FFmpeg's libraries must never export a C++ symbol beside it.
FROM staging-base AS staging
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    if [ "${TARGETARCH}" = amd64 ]; then \
      sed -i 's/^Components: main$/Components: main non-free/' /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian.sources; \
      grep -q '^Components: main non-free$' /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian.sources; \
      printf 'Types: deb\nURIs: http://deb.debian.org/debian\nSuites: bookworm\nComponents: main\nSigned-By: /usr/share/keyrings/debian-archive-keyring.gpg\n' \
        > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/bookworm.sources; \
      printf 'Package: *\nPin: release n=bookworm\nPin-Priority: 100\n' > /etc/apt/preferences.d/bookworm; \
      apt-get update; \
      apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends intel-media-va-driver-non-free libmfx-gen1.2 libva2 libva-drm2 libmfx1/bookworm; \
      rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
      d=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu; \
      export EXTRA_DLOPEN="$d/dri/iHD_drv_video.so $d/libva.so.2 $d/libva-drm.so.2 $d/libmfx-gen.so.1.2 $(ls $d/libmfx-gen/*.so) $d/libmfxhw64.so.1 $(ls $d/mfx/*.so)"; \
    fi; \
    /stage.sh /staging; \
    if nm -D --defined-only /staging/usr/lib/libav*.so.* /staging/usr/lib/libsw*.so.* | grep -q ' _Z'; then \
      echo 'FFmpeg exports C++ symbols beside ONNX Runtime' >&2; exit 1; \
    fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# native: FROM scratch, plus what one architecture alone needs
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM scratch AS native-base
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/mediactl/clustarr" \
      org.opencontainers.image.licenses="GPL-3.0-only" \
      org.opencontainers.image.title="clustarr-native"
COPY --from=staging /staging/ /
ENV FFGO_SHIM_DIR=/usr/lib \
    ORT_LIB_PATH=/usr/lib/libonnxruntime.so
VOLUME ["/data"]
USER 1000:1000

# libva logs every driver load at info level on stderr; errors only keeps
# FFmpeg's own error in a transcode's stderr tail. The driver path is where
# staging put iHD, under amd64's multiarch directory.
FROM native-base AS native-amd64
ENV LIBVA_MESSAGING_LEVEL=1 \
    LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/dri \
    LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD

# arm64 stages no libva and no driver (see staging), so it names none.
FROM native-base AS native-arm64

FROM native-${TARGETARCH} AS native

FROM native AS native-debug
COPY --from=busybox:1.37-musl /bin/ /bin/
COPY images/distroless/busybox-SOURCE /usr/share/licenses/busybox/SOURCE
```

```sh
# Stages into $1 exactly what the native image loads, for a FROM-scratch
# image (images/Dockerfile.native).
#
# lddtree follows each file's DT_NEEDED tree: the agent (a cgo build, so it
# brings libc, libm, libresolv, libstdc++ and libgcc_s), markers and
# transcode (purego binaries, so the dynamic linker and libc), the ffgo shim,
# ONNX Runtime and every FFmpeg library -- never an ffmpeg, ffprobe or par2
# executable, which nothing in the image runs (R2), and which the last step
# refuses. What no DT_NEEDED names, because it is dlopen'ed, is traced
# explicitly: glibc's NSS plugins here, and the caller's EXTRA_DLOPEN (the
# Intel runtime).
```

     the last block (`:74-81`) becomes

```sh
# Every binary runs FFmpeg (and, from §11.1 step 12, par2) as a library; an
# executable here would be dead weight at best, and at worst a path back to
# exec'ing it.
for f in ffmpeg ffprobe par2; do
	if [ -n "$(find "$dst" -name "$f" \( -type f -o -type l \) | head -n1)" ]; then
		echo "stage.sh: $f was staged; the native image carries no media executable" >&2
		exit 1
	fi
done
```

````markdown
# The native image

`images/Dockerfile.native` builds `ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr/native` FROM
scratch (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-manager-agent-split-design.md`
§10.1.3): the `agent`, `markers` and `transcode` binaries on FFmpeg 9's
libraries. It replaced the `transcoder` image (this file's
`Dockerfile.transcoder` until then) and the debian-based `media` image, which
carried `ffmpeg`, `ffprobe` and `par2` executables; nothing runs an external
media program any more (R2).

| Target | Platforms | Runs | Size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `native` | amd64, arm64 | every agent domain, the download engines, markers, the transcode pools (`cpu`, `cuda`, `intel` on amd64) and the AudioGraft Jobs | the transcoder's 118 MB gzipped on amd64 plus the agent, markers and ONNX Runtime |
| `native-debug` | as `native` | | +1 MB (static busybox) |

Both are per-architecture: `native` is `native-amd64` or `native-arm64` over a
shared `native-base`, and only amd64, which stages libva and Intel's iHD
driver, sets `LIBVA_*`. There is no ENTRYPOINT: every container names its
binary (`/usr/bin/agent`, `/usr/bin/markers`, `/usr/bin/transcode`).

There is no CUDA image ([ADR-0015](../../docs/adr/0015-no-cuda-image.md)).
An nvidia pool runs `native`: the NVIDIA container runtime injects the
driver's libraries (`libcuda`, `libnvidia-encode`, `libnvcuvid`), which
FFmpeg `dlopen`s, into a pod that sets `runtimeClassName: nvidia`, requests
`nvidia.com/gpu` and sets `NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=video,compute,utility`,
as the manager's pool template does. Do not add a CUDA target back without
reading the ADR.

What is in it, and why:

- `stage.sh` runs `lddtree --copy-to-tree` on the three binaries (the agent
  is a cgo build, R13, so it brings glibc and libstdc++), the ffgo shim,
  ONNX Runtime and every FFmpeg library. It fails the build if `ffmpeg`,
  `ffprobe` or `par2` is staged.
- `lddtree` cannot see what is `dlopen`ed, so that is named: glibc's NSS
  plugins and, on amd64, the VAAPI driver and the QSV runtimes.
- The CA bundle, `nsswitch.conf`, `passwd` and `group` for uid 1000, and
  `/data`, `/scratch` and `/tmp`.
- FFmpeg's libraries, the shim and ONNX Runtime live in `/usr/lib`, which the
  dynamic linker searches without an `ld.so.cache`; `FFGO_SHIM_DIR` and
  `ORT_LIB_PATH` point there.

```sh
make docker-build-native   # native and native-debug, with the pinned contexts (make contexts)
make docker-selfcheck      # hack/image-checks.sh, as CI and the release run it
```
````

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test.** Append to `test/guards/images_test.go`:

```go
// imageCheckPatterns are the case patterns hack/image-checks.sh defines, as
// anchored regexps ("version:*" matches "version:agent").
func imageCheckPatterns(t *testing.T, root string) []*regexp.Regexp {
	t.Helper()
	script := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "hack/image-checks.sh"))
	var out []*regexp.Regexp
	for _, m := range regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^\s+([a-z0-9:*|-]+)\)`).FindAllStringSubmatch(script, -1) {
		for _, alt := range strings.Split(m[1], "|") {
			if alt == "*" {
				continue // the unknown-check fallthrough, which refuses
			}
			out = append(out, regexp.MustCompile("^"+strings.ReplaceAll(regexp.QuoteMeta(alt), `\*`, ".+")+"$"))
		}
	}
	require.NotEmpty(t, out, "hack/image-checks.sh defines no checks")
	return out
}

// TestTheMakefileChecksImagesThroughOneScript: hack/image-checks.sh is the
// one definition of the image checks (spec §10.1.4), as hack/e2e.sh's
// `make e2e` is of the e2e go test line. The Makefile never runs an image
// itself, names only checks the script defines, and passes the pinned
// contexts to every build; hack/kind.sh loads the two images that exist.
func TestTheMakefileChecksImagesThroughOneScript(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	patterns := imageCheckPatterns(t, root)
	known := func(check string) bool {
		for _, p := range patterns {
			if p.MatchString(check) {
				return true
			}
		}
		return false
	}
	mk := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "Makefile"))
	var builds, checks int
	for _, line := range strings.Split(mk, "\n") {
		l := strings.TrimSpace(line)
		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(l, "docker build "):
			builds++
			assert.Contains(t, l, "$(LOCAL_CONTEXTS)", "every image build passes the pinned contexts: %s", l)
		case strings.HasPrefix(l, "docker run"), strings.Contains(l, "--self-check"):
			t.Errorf("the Makefile checks an image itself (%q): hack/image-checks.sh is the one definition", l)
		case strings.HasPrefix(l, "hack/image-checks.sh "):
			for _, c := range strings.Fields(l)[2:] {
				if strings.Contains(c, "$(") {
					continue
				}
				checks++
				assert.True(t, known(c), "the Makefile asks hack/image-checks.sh for %q, which it does not define", c)
			}
		}
	}
	m := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^NATIVE_CHECKS \?= (.+)$`).FindStringSubmatch(mk)
	require.NotNil(t, m, "the Makefile has no NATIVE_CHECKS")
	for _, c := range strings.Fields(m[1]) {
		if !strings.Contains(c, "$(") {
			assert.True(t, known(c), "NATIVE_CHECKS names %q, which hack/image-checks.sh does not define", c)
		}
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 5, builds, "docker-build (2), docker-build-native (2), docker-build-fixtures (1)")
	assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, checks, 5)
	kind := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "hack/kind.sh"))
	assert.NotContains(t, kind, "MEDIA_IMG")
	assert.NotContains(t, kind, "TRANSCODER_IMG")
	assert.Contains(t, kind, `"${IMG}" "${NATIVE_IMG}"`)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** `hack/image-checks.sh` (`chmod +x`):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# hack/image-checks.sh IMAGE CHECK... -- the one definition of the image
# checks (spec 2026-10-06 §10.1.4). The Makefile's docker-selfcheck, ci.yml
# and release.yml all call it; none restates a check.
#
#   version:<bin>                 /usr/bin/<bin> --version, read-only, no capabilities, uid 1000
#   self-check:transcode:<class>  transcode --self-check=<class>, as a pool pod runs it
#   self-check:agent              agent --self-check
#   self-check:markers            markers --self-check
#   self-check:par2-child         agent par2-repair --self-check
#   no-shell                      the image has no /bin/sh
#   notices                       (debug image) every licence notice exists and is non-empty
#   no-media-executables          (debug image) no ffmpeg, ffprobe or par2 file anywhere
set -euo pipefail
usage="usage: hack/image-checks.sh IMAGE CHECK..."
img=${1:?$usage}
shift
[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || { echo "${usage}" >&2; exit 2; }
# The par2 integration (§11.1 step 12) adds par2cmdline-turbo's and par2go's notices.
notices=(
  /usr/share/licenses/ffmpeg/LICENSE.txt
  /usr/share/licenses/ffmpeg/SOURCE
  /usr/share/licenses/clustarr/LICENSE
  /usr/share/licenses/ffgo/LICENSE
  /usr/share/licenses/ffgo/SOURCE
  /usr/share/licenses/onnxruntime/LICENSE
  /usr/share/doc/libc6/copyright
)
locked() { docker run --rm --read-only --cap-drop=ALL --user 1000:1000 "$@"; }
for check in "$@"; do
  echo "== ${img}: ${check}" >&2
  case "${check}" in
    version:*)
      locked --entrypoint "/usr/bin/${check#version:}" "${img}" --version ;;
    self-check:transcode:*)
      locked --entrypoint /usr/bin/transcode "${img}" --self-check="${check#self-check:transcode:}" >/dev/null ;;
    self-check:agent|self-check:markers)
      locked --entrypoint "/usr/bin/${check#self-check:}" "${img}" --self-check ;;
    self-check:par2-child)
      locked --entrypoint /usr/bin/agent "${img}" par2-repair --self-check ;;
    no-shell)
      if docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh "${img}" -c true >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "${img} has a shell" >&2; exit 1
      fi ;;
    notices)
      docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh "${img}" -c \
        'set -e; for f in "$@"; do test -s "$f" || { echo "missing notice $f" >&2; exit 1; }; done; cat /usr/share/licenses/*/SOURCE' \
        sh "${notices[@]}" ;;
    no-media-executables)
      found=$(docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh "${img}" -c 'find / -xdev \( -name ffmpeg -o -name ffprobe -o -name par2 \) -type f')
      [[ -z "${found}" ]] || { echo "${img} carries a media executable: ${found}" >&2; exit 1; } ;;
    *)
      echo "hack/image-checks.sh: unknown check ${check}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
echo "ok: ${img}" >&2
```

  `Makefile`: after `IMAGE_VERSION := …` add `FIXTURES_IMG ?= ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr/e2e-fixtures:dev`;
  after the `docker-build-native` target add (append `self-check:markers` after `self-check:agent`
  in `NATIVE_CHECKS` only when W6.1 printed `markers-self-check=yes`):

```make
# The classes the native image is self-checked for: it serves every pool,
# cpu, nvidia and intel (ADR 0015). NATIVE_CHECKS is the native image's list
# for hack/image-checks.sh; markers decode (spec §11.1 step 10) adds
# self-check:markers and the par2 integration (step 12) self-check:par2-child.
NATIVE_CLASSES ?= cpu cuda intel
NATIVE_CHECKS ?= $(foreach c,$(NATIVE_CLASSES),self-check:transcode:$(c)) self-check:agent version:agent version:markers version:transcode no-shell

.PHONY: docker-build-fixtures
docker-build-fixtures: contexts ## Build the e2e fixture image.
	docker build $(LOCAL_CONTEXTS) -f images/Dockerfile.e2e-fixtures -t $(FIXTURES_IMG) .

.PHONY: docker-selfcheck
```

  becomes `#   IMG / NATIVE_IMG   image tags for `load`  (defaults match the Makefile)`; `:39-40`
  become `NATIVE_IMG="${NATIVE_IMG:-ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr/native:dev}"`; the `Next:` text's
  `make docker-build          # build ${IMG}, ${MEDIA_IMG} and ${TRANSCODER_IMG}` and
  `hack/kind.sh load          # load them into the cluster` become
  `make docker-build          # build ${IMG} and ${NATIVE_IMG}` and
  `make kind-load             # load them into the cluster`; `cmd_load` becomes

```bash
cmd_load() {
  need kind
  need docker
  cluster_exists || die "kind cluster '${CLUSTER_NAME}' does not exist; run 'hack/kind.sh up'"
  local img node_id
  for img in "${IMG}" "${NATIVE_IMG}"; do
    if ! docker image inspect "${img}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      log "image ${img} not found locally, skipping (run 'make docker-build')"
      continue
    fi
    # Loading unpacks gigabytes into the node's containerd store, which shares
    # a disk with etcd (CLAUDE.md, "loading an image into the node stalls
    # etcd"): load only an image whose content changed.
    node_id=$(docker exec "${CLUSTER_NAME}-control-plane" crictl inspecti -o go-template --template '{{.status.id}}' "${img}" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [[ "${node_id}" == "$(docker image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "${img}")" ]]; then
      log "${img} unchanged on the node, skipping"
      continue
    fi
    log "loading ${img}"
    kind load docker-image --name "${CLUSTER_NAME}" "${img}"
  done
}
```
