  **3d. Values and schema.** `charts/clustarr/values.yaml`: replace the `Images` section (`:8-36`, through
  `imagePullSecrets: []` exclusive) with

```yaml
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Images
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two images (spec 2026-10-06 §10.1, R1):
#   clustarr -- distroless static: the manager and ui binaries.
#   native   -- FROM scratch: the agent, markers and transcode binaries on
#               FFmpeg 9's libraries and ONNX Runtime. Every agent, markers,
#               and everything the manager renders at runtime (the download
#               engines, the transcode pools, AudioGraft Jobs) run it, nvidia
#               pools included: the NVIDIA container runtime injects the
#               driver's libraries from the host, so there is no CUDA image
#               (docs/adr/0015-no-cuda-image.md).
# An empty tag falls back to .Chart.AppVersion.
image:
  registry: ghcr.io
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  clustarr:
    repository: mediactl/clustarr
    tag: ""
  native:
    repository: mediactl/clustarr/native
    tag: ""
```

  insert after the `cloudnative-pg:` block

```yaml
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Autoscaling (spec 2026-10-06 §9)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# true: the manager owns one HorizontalPodAutoscaler per queue-driven
# Deployment (agent-catalog, agent-events, agent-import, agent-caption,
# markers) and scales each on JetStream consumer lag -- to zero while its
# queues are empty (agent-events keeps one) and up to the number of nodes its
# pods can schedule on -- through the External Metrics API it serves itself
# (templates/autoscaling.yaml renders the APIService). The chart never renders
# an HPA: the manager's reconciler owns them.
# false: fixed replicas from agents.<domain>.replicas and markers.replicas,
# and no APIService. Use it where KEDA or prometheus-adapter already holds
# v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io: only one APIService may hold the group.
autoscaling:
  enabled: true
```

  and replace everything from the `# Services` banner through the end of the `segmentarrWorker:` block
  (up to the `ui:` block's comment) with

```yaml
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Workloads (spec 2026-10-06 §10.2.1)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The parts that are not knobs -- image, command, domain, volumes, update
# strategy, grace period -- live in the templates, because getting them wrong
# is a correctness bug rather than a preference. GOMEMLIMIT is a share of
# resources.limits.memory: 80%, except agent-import and agent-caption (60%)
# and markers (50%), whose FFmpeg, par2 and ONNX Runtime allocations live
# outside the Go heap.

# Every controller in one process, one replica under the lease
# manager.clustarr.io (no replica knob). It renders the download engines, the
# transcode pools and AudioGraft Jobs, and serves the External Metrics API.
manager:
  # Transcode admission per hardware class (--slots): class=count pairs.
  slots: cpu=2,nvidia=1,intel=1
  # GIDs of the host group owning /dev/dri/renderD* on the Intel GPU nodes
  # (--intel-render-groups), added to every Intel transcode pod as
  # supplementalGroups. Host-specific, so no default; leave empty with a
  # runtime that has device_ownership_from_security_context.
  intelRenderGroups: []
  # Override the node labels that mark NVIDIA and Intel GPU nodes
  # (--gpu-node-label-nvidia/-intel). Empty uses the binary's defaults,
  # nvidia.com/gpu.present and intel.feature.node.kubernetes.io/gpu.
  gpuNodeLabelNvidia: ""
  gpuNodeLabelIntel: ""
  # The Cardigann definitions the manager's bundle loader applies. See the
  # README's "Cardigann definitions".
  cardigann:
    # --cardigann-bundled: load the corpus compiled into the binary.
    bundled: true
    # A ConfigMap or claim of definition files, mounted read-only and passed
    # as --cardigann-definitions-dir, replacing the corpus. One, not both.
    definitions:
      configMap: ""
      existingClaim: ""
      subPath: ""
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 512Mi
    limits:
      cpu: "2"
      memory: 1536Mi
  nodeSelector: {}
  tolerations: []
  affinity: {}

# One Deployment per agent domain (agent --domain=<domain>). replicas applies
# only with autoscaling.enabled=false. consumerSlots overrides a consumer's
# per-pod handler count (CLUSTARR_CONSUMER_SLOTS), which is also the HPA's
# per-pod target, e.g. {catalogarr-artwork-render: 2}.
agents:
  # Searches, grabs and artwork renders. Autoscaled 0..1: its searches end in
  # the index agent's per-host limiter, which more replicas cannot feed.
  catalog:
    enabled: true
    replicas: 1
    consumerSlots: {}
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 256Mi
      limits:
        cpu: "1"
        memory: 1Gi
    nodeSelector: {}
    tolerations: []
    affinity: {}
  # The RSS matcher, history sink, redownloads and DLQ projector. Their
  # streams are memory-backed on single-node NATS, so it never scales below one.
  events:
    enabled: true
    replicas: 1
    consumerSlots: {}
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 256Mi
      limits:
        cpu: "1"
        memory: 1Gi
    nodeSelector: {}
    tolerations: []
    affinity: {}
  # The metadata gateway, TheIntroDB markers, segment results and artwork
  # fetches. Always one replica, Recreate: its provider rate limiters live in
  # process memory (ADR-0007), so a second replica doubles the request rate.
  metadata:
    enabled: true
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 50m
        memory: 96Mi
      limits:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 512Mi
    nodeSelector: {}
    tolerations: []
    affinity: {}
  # Library scans, file imports, import-list syncs, recycle sweeps and probes.
  # Mounts /data read-write.
  import:
    enabled: true
    replicas: 1
    consumerSlots: {}
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 256Mi
      limits:
        cpu: "2"
        memory: 1536Mi
    nodeSelector: {}
    tolerations: []
    affinity: {}
  # The release index, the search/download/query RPC, RSS polls and the
  # Torznab facade. Always one replica, Recreate: a SQLite index on a
  # ReadWriteOnce PVC, and under postgres.enabled still one process holding
  # the RPC responders, the facade and the per-host limiter.
  index:
    enabled: true
    facade:
      service:
        type: ClusterIP
        port: 8080
      # The Secret holding the facade's API keys; empty means
      # <release>-indexarr-facade, created by the agent with one random key.
      apiKeySecret: ""
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 256Mi
      limits:
        cpu: "1"
        memory: 1Gi
    nodeSelector: {}
    tolerations: []
    affinity: {}
  # Subtitle fetches. Autoscaled 0..1: fetches wait on the shared provider
  # token bucket. Mounts /data read-write for sidecars.
  caption:
    enabled: true
    replicas: 1
    consumerSlots: {}
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 192Mi
      limits:
        cpu: "1"
        memory: 1Gi
    nodeSelector: {}
    tolerations: []
    affinity: {}

# Skip-segment detection (cmd/markers). Reads /data read-only and holds no
# ServiceAccount token. Autoscaled 0..N on segmentarr-analyze; its per-pod
# analyses are consumerSlots.segmentarr-analyze (default 1).
markers:
  enabled: true
  replicas: 1
  consumerSlots: {}
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 250m
      memory: 512Mi
    limits:
      cpu: "2"
      memory: 2Gi
  nodeSelector: {}
  tolerations: []
  affinity: {}
```

  `git mv config/postgres/indexarr-patch.yaml config/postgres/agent-index-patch.yaml`, content:

```yaml
# Strategic-merge patch: points the index agent at the CloudNativePG
# Cluster's release index instead of the local SQLite volume
# config/manager/agent-index.yaml mounts by default (design spec 2026-09-24
# §A.3-A.4; ADR-0010).
#
# CLUSTARR_INDEX_DSN is added (CLUSTARR_INDEX_PATH stays: the agent logs and
# ignores it once a DSN is set) from Secret "clustarr-postgres-app", which
# CNPG's bootstrap.initdb creates for cluster.yaml's "clustarr-postgres"
# Cluster (key "uri"). $patch: delete removes the index volumeMount and the
# volume: there is no PVC to mount under Postgres. The strategy stays
# Recreate: the index agent is one process under both engines (its RPC
# responders, facade and per-host limiter; spec 2026-10-06 R4 amendment).
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: agent-index
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: agent-index
        env:
        - name: CLUSTARR_INDEX_DSN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: clustarr-postgres-app
              key: uri
        volumeMounts:
        # volumeMounts' merge key is mountPath, not name.
        - mountPath: /var/lib/clustarr/index
          $patch: delete
      volumes:
      - name: index
        $patch: delete
```

```go
// assertExternalMetricsAPI holds an installer's External Metrics API to
// spec §10.2.2: the APIService names the external-metrics Service on 443,
// sends no caBundle (the manager injects it under clustarr-autoscale, and an
// installer that sent one would fight it) and never skips TLS; the Service
// selects the manager pods and publishes not-ready addresses, so the
// aggregator reaches a manager whose caches are still syncing; the manager
// may read the front-proxy CA in kube-system; and the manager is told the
// Service and Secret names.
func assertExternalMetricsAPI(t *testing.T, objs []*unstructured.Unstructured, prefix string) {
	t.Helper()
	svcName := prefix + "external-metrics"
	var api, svc, reader, manager *unstructured.Unstructured
	for _, o := range objs {
		switch {
		case o.GetKind() == "APIService" && o.GetName() == "v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io":
			api = o
		case o.GetKind() == "Service" && o.GetName() == svcName:
			svc = o
		case o.GetKind() == "RoleBinding" && o.GetNamespace() == "kube-system":
			reader = o
		case o.GetKind() == "Deployment" && o.GetName() == prefix+"manager":
			manager = o
		}
	}
	require.NotNil(t, api, "no APIService v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io")
	spec, _, _ := unstructured.NestedMap(api.Object, "spec")
	assert.Equal(t, "external.metrics.k8s.io", spec["group"])
	assert.Equal(t, "v1beta1", spec["version"])
	assert.NotContains(t, spec, "caBundle", "the manager injects caBundle")
	assert.Equal(t, false, spec["insecureSkipTLSVerify"])
	assert.EqualValues(t, 100, spec["groupPriorityMinimum"])
	assert.EqualValues(t, 100, spec["versionPriority"])
	service, _, _ := unstructured.NestedMap(api.Object, "spec", "service")
	assert.Equal(t, svcName, service["name"])
	assert.Equal(t, "clustarr-system", service["namespace"], "the APIService names the release namespace")
	assert.EqualValues(t, 443, service["port"])

	require.NotNil(t, svc, "no Service %s", svcName)
	pnra, _, _ := unstructured.NestedBool(svc.Object, "spec", "publishNotReadyAddresses")
	assert.True(t, pnra, "publishNotReadyAddresses")
	sel, _, _ := unstructured.NestedStringMap(svc.Object, "spec", "selector")
	assert.Equal(t, "manager", sel["app.kubernetes.io/component"], "the Service selects the manager pods")
	ports, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(svc.Object, "spec", "ports")
	require.Len(t, ports, 1)
	p := ports[0].(map[string]any)
	assert.Equal(t, "https", p["name"])
	assert.EqualValues(t, 443, p["port"])
	assert.Equal(t, "extmetrics", p["targetPort"])

	require.NotNil(t, reader, "no RoleBinding in kube-system")
	ref, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(reader.Object, "roleRef", "name")
	assert.Equal(t, "extension-apiserver-authentication-reader", ref)
	subjects, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(reader.Object, "subjects")
	require.Len(t, subjects, 1)
	assert.Equal(t, prefix+"manager", subjects[0].(map[string]any)["name"])

	require.NotNil(t, manager, "no manager Deployment")
	containers, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(manager.Object, "spec", "template", "spec", "containers")
	c := containers[0].(map[string]any)
	extmetrics := false
	for _, cp := range c["ports"].([]any) {
		if m := cp.(map[string]any); m["name"] == "extmetrics" {
			extmetrics = true
			assert.EqualValues(t, 6443, m["containerPort"])
		}
	}
	assert.True(t, extmetrics, "the manager exposes extmetrics")
	env := map[string]string{}
	for _, e := range c["env"].([]any) {
		m := e.(map[string]any)
		if v, ok := m["value"].(string); ok {
			env[m["name"].(string)] = v
		}
	}
	assert.Equal(t, svcName, env["CLUSTARR_EXTERNAL_METRICS_SERVICE"])
	assert.Equal(t, prefix+"external-metrics-tls", env["CLUSTARR_EXTERNAL_METRICS_SECRET"])
}
```

```yaml
{{- if .Values.autoscaling.enabled }}
{{/*
The External Metrics API the manager serves itself (spec 2026-10-06 §9.4),
which its autoscale reconciler's HPAs read to scale the queue-driven agents
on JetStream consumer lag. The manager creates its CA and serving cert in
<fullname>-external-metrics-tls and writes only spec.caBundle (field manager
clustarr-autoscale); nothing here sends caBundle, so Helm and the manager
never fight over it. Only one APIService may hold
v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io: where KEDA or prometheus-adapter already
does, set autoscaling.enabled=false (Helm refuses to adopt it, loudly).
*/}}
apiVersion: apiregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: APIService
metadata:
  name: v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io
  labels:
    {{- include "clustarr.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/component: external-metrics
spec:
  group: external.metrics.k8s.io
  version: v1beta1
  service:
    namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
    name: {{ include "clustarr.fullname" . }}-external-metrics
    port: 443
  groupPriorityMinimum: 100
  versionPriority: 100
  insecureSkipTLSVerify: false
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ include "clustarr.fullname" . }}-external-metrics
  labels:
    {{- include "clustarr.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/component: external-metrics
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  # The aggregator must reach a manager whose caches are still syncing: the
  # server answers before they do, and nothing gates on its readiness (§9.4).
  publishNotReadyAddresses: true
  selector:
    {{- include "clustarr.selectorLabels" (dict "root" $ "component" "manager") | nindent 4 }}
  ports:
  - name: https
    port: 443
    targetPort: extmetrics
    protocol: TCP
---
{{/* The manager reads the front-proxy client CA from
     kube-system/extension-apiserver-authentication. No
     system:auth-delegator binding: the kube-apiserver authenticates and
     authorizes before it proxies, and the server reviews no tokens. */}}
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: {{ include "clustarr.fullname" . }}-manager-auth-reader
  namespace: kube-system
  labels:
    {{- include "clustarr.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/component: manager
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: extension-apiserver-authentication-reader
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: {{ include "clustarr.fullname" . }}-manager
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
{{- end }}
```

```yaml
# The External Metrics API the manager serves itself (spec 2026-10-06 §9.4,
# §10.2.6): the APIService, the Service it names and the kube-system
# RoleBinding that lets the manager read the front-proxy client CA. The
# manager writes only the APIService's spec.caBundle (field manager
# clustarr-autoscale); nothing here sends it. config/default includes this
# directory. Only one APIService may hold v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io: on
# a cluster where KEDA or prometheus-adapter already does, leave it out and
# pass --autoscale=false to the manager.

    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: clustarr
```

  `config/default/kustomization.yaml` (whole file):

```yaml
# The deployable Clustarr install:
#
#   kustomize build config/default | kubectl apply --server-side -f -
#
# Composes the CRDs, RBAC, the nine Deployments of config/manager (the
# manager, six agents, markers and the ui), the External Metrics APIService
# (config/autoscaling), the dev NATS StatefulSet and the two PVCs (§11) into
# the clustarr-system namespace.
#
# The namespace comes from a NamespaceTransformer with unsetOnly, not the
# plain `namespace:` field, which would also move config/autoscaling's
# kube-system RoleBinding.
#
# Optional, not included here; add them when the cluster has the operators:
#   ../prometheus  ServiceMonitors (needs the Prometheus Operator CRDs)
#   ../postgres    the release index on CloudNativePG (a Component)
#
# Production installs should prefer charts/clustarr, which swaps this plain
# NATS StatefulSet for the upstream nats chart (clustered R3, reloader,
# prometheus-nats-exporter).
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
- namespace.yaml
- pvc.yaml
- ../crd
- ../rbac
- ../manager
- ../autoscaling
- ../nats

transformers:
- |-
  apiVersion: builtin
  kind: NamespaceTransformer
  metadata:
    name: clustarr-namespace
    namespace: clustarr-system
  unsetOnly: true
```

  `charts/clustarr/README.md`: replace W6.2's interim `## Autoscaling` paragraph with

```markdown
## Autoscaling

`autoscaling.enabled=true` (the default) lets the manager scale the
queue-driven workloads itself (spec 2026-10-06 §9). It owns one
HorizontalPodAutoscaler per Deployment labelled `autoscale.clustarr.io/domain`
(`agent-catalog`, `agent-events`, `agent-import`, `agent-caption`, `markers`)
and scales each on JetStream consumer lag: to zero while its queues are empty
(`agent-events` to one, its streams cannot buffer through zero) and up to the
number of nodes its pods can schedule on. The lag comes from an External
Metrics API the manager serves itself: `templates/autoscaling.yaml` renders the
`v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io` APIService, its `<release>-external-metrics`
Service and a `kube-system` RoleBinding that lets the manager read the
front-proxy client CA. The manager creates its own CA and serving certificate
in `<release>-external-metrics-tls` and injects the APIService's `caBundle`.

The chart never renders an HPA, and the autoscaled Deployments carry no
`replicas`: the manager's reconciler owns both, and Helm's server-side apply
would fight it. On a cluster without the `HPAScaleToZero` feature (on by
default from Kubernetes 1.37) the manager keeps one replica of each and records
a `ScaleToZeroUnavailable` Event.

Only one APIService may hold `v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io`. Where KEDA or
prometheus-adapter already does, set `autoscaling.enabled=false`: the chart
then renders `agents.<domain>.replicas` and `markers.replicas`, no APIService,
and passes `--autoscale=false` to the manager. Helm refuses to adopt an
APIService it does not own, so the conflict is a loud install error.

`agents.<domain>.consumerSlots` and `markers.consumerSlots` set a consumer's
per-pod handler count (`CLUSTARR_CONSUMER_SLOTS`), which is also the HPA's
per-pod target, for example `--set markers.consumerSlots.segmentarr-analyze=3`.
If the manager is down, `kubectl delete ns` of its namespace can hang on the
unavailable APIService; `kubectl delete apiservice v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io`
releases it.
```

```go
package guards

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"os/exec"

	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

// TestTheDefaultValuesPassTheSchema: the chart lints strictly and renders
// with its own values, and with the top-level keys today's templates read
// but the skeleton could drop (imagePullSecrets, both name overrides), so a
// key the closed schema forgets fails here, not at a user's upgrade.
func TestTheDefaultValuesPassTheSchema(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	helm := installtest.FindTool(t, "helm")
	for name, args := range map[string][]string{
		"defaults": nil,
		"imagePullSecrets and name overrides": {"--set", "imagePullSecrets[0].name=regcred",
			"--set", "nameOverride=media", "--set", "fullnameOverride=media-release"},
		"autoscaling off": {"--set", "autoscaling.enabled=false"},
		"consumer slots":  {"--set", "markers.consumerSlots.segmentarr-analyze=3", "--set", "agents.import.consumerSlots.importarr-fileimport=2"},
	} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			installtest.Run(t, root, helm, append([]string{"lint", "--strict", "charts/clustarr"}, args...)...)
			installtest.Run(t, root, helm, append([]string{"template", "clustarr", "charts/clustarr"}, args...)...)
		})
	}
	var schema struct {
		AdditionalProperties *bool                      `json:"additionalProperties"`
		Properties           map[string]json.RawMessage `json:"properties"`
	}
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(readRepoFile(t, root, "charts/clustarr/values.schema.json"), &schema))
	require.NotNil(t, schema.AdditionalProperties, "the schema's top level must say additionalProperties")
	assert.False(t, *schema.AdditionalProperties, "the schema's top level is closed (OD37)")
	assert.Contains(t, schema.Properties, "global", "Helm injects global into a chart with dependencies")
	var values map[string]any
	require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(readRepoFile(t, root, "charts/clustarr/values.yaml"), &values))
	for k := range values {
		assert.Contains(t, schema.Properties, k, "values.yaml's %s is not in the schema", k)
	}
}

// TestRetiredValuesKeysAreRejected (§10.2.8, OD37): a 0.4.x values file
// fails at install, naming the key, instead of rendering with its blocks

	for _, set := range []string{
		"image.controller.tag=x", "image.media.tag=x", "image.transcoder.tag=x",
		"catalogarr.replicas=1", "catalogarrMetadata.replicas=1", "importarr.replicas=1", "importarrWorker.replicas=1",
		"indexarr.replicas=1", "grabarr.replicas=1", "squasharr.workerEngine=ffgo", "captionarr.replicas=1",
		"captionarrWorker.ackWaitSeconds=120", "segmentarrWorker.concurrency=1", "keda.enabled=true",
		"agents.metadata.replicas=2", "agents.index.replicas=2", "manager.replicas=2", "markers.concurrency=2",
	} {
		t.Run(set, func(t *testing.T) {
			cmd := exec.Command(helm, "template", "clustarr", "charts/clustarr", "--set", set)
			cmd.Dir = root
			out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
			require.Error(t, err, "--set %s must fail the schema", set)
			assert.Regexp(t, regexp.MustCompile(`additional properties '[^']+' not allowed`), string(out))
		})
	}
}

// slotSchema is the part of an autoscaled workload's schema that names its
// consumers: allOf[1].properties.consumerSlots.propertyNames.enum.
type slotSchema struct {
	AllOf []struct {
		Properties struct {
			ConsumerSlots struct {
				PropertyNames struct {
					Enum []string `json:"enum"`
				} `json:"propertyNames"`
			} `json:"consumerSlots"`
		} `json:"properties"`
	} `json:"allOf"`
}

// TestConsumerSlotsNameOnlyTheDomainsConsumers (§10.2.2): a workload's
// consumerSlots may name exactly its own domain's consumers, so a slot meant
// for another workload fails at install instead of rendering an override its
// binary ignores and its HPA misreads.
func TestConsumerSlotsNameOnlyTheDomainsConsumers(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	var schema struct {
		Properties struct {
			Agents struct {
				Properties map[string]slotSchema `json:"properties"`
			} `json:"agents"`
			Markers slotSchema `json:"markers"`
		} `json:"properties"`
	}
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(readRepoFile(t, root, "charts/clustarr/values.schema.json"), &schema))
	enumOf := func(s slotSchema) []string {
		for _, a := range s.AllOf {
			if e := a.Properties.ConsumerSlots.PropertyNames.Enum; len(e) > 0 {
				return e
			}
		}
		return nil
	}
	for _, d := range agentdomain.Domains() {
		if !d.Autoscaled || len(d.Consumers) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		s := schema.Properties.Agents.Properties[d.Name]
		if d.Name == agentdomain.Markers {
			s = schema.Properties.Markers
		}
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, d.Consumers, enumOf(s), "%s's consumerSlots names exactly agentdomain's consumers", d.Name)
	}
	cmd := exec.Command(installtest.FindTool(t, "helm"), "template", "clustarr", "charts/clustarr",
		"--set", "agents.catalog.consumerSlots.captionarr-fetch-high=2")
	cmd.Dir = root
	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
	require.Error(t, err, "a caption consumer in the catalog agent's slots must fail")
	assert.Contains(t, string(out), "captionarr-fetch-high")
}

// TestTheChartREADMENamesOnlyLiveValuesKeys: outside "Upgrading from 0.4.x",
// the README names no retired key, and every key it names under a live top
// key exists in values.yaml (<domain>-style placeholders match any key).
func TestTheChartREADMENamesOnlyLiveValuesKeys(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	readme := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "charts/clustarr/README.md"))
	upgrading := regexp.MustCompile(`(?ms)^## Upgrading from 0\.4\.x\n.*?(^## |\z)`)
	require.Regexp(t, upgrading, readme, "the README has an \"Upgrading from 0.4.x\" section")
	rest := upgrading.ReplaceAllString(readme, "$1")
	retired := regexp.MustCompile("`(catalogarr|catalogarrMetadata|importarr|importarrWorker|indexarr|grabarr|squasharr|captionarr|captionarrWorker|segmentarrWorker|keda|image\\.controller|image\\.media|image\\.transcoder)\\b[^`]*`")
	for _, m := range retired.FindAllString(rest, -1) {
		t.Errorf("charts/clustarr/README.md names retired key %s outside \"Upgrading from 0.4.x\"", m)
	}
	var values map[string]any
	require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(readRepoFile(t, root, "charts/clustarr/values.yaml"), &values))
	key := regexp.MustCompile("`((?:manager|agents|markers|autoscaling)(?:\\.[A-Za-z<>-]+)+)`")
	for _, m := range key.FindAllStringSubmatch(rest, -1) {
		node := any(values)
		for _, seg := range strings.Split(m[1], ".") {
			obj, ok := node.(map[string]any)
			if !ok {
				break
			}
			if strings.HasPrefix(seg, "<") {
				for _, v := range obj {
					node = v
					break
				}
				continue
			}
			next, ok := obj[seg]
			assert.True(t, ok, "charts/clustarr/README.md names %s, which values.yaml does not have", m[1])
			if !ok {
				break
			}
			node = next
		}
	}
}
```

```python
import json
p = "charts/clustarr/values.schema.json"
d = json.load(open(p))
props, defs = d["properties"], d["$defs"]
retired = ["catalogarr", "catalogarrMetadata", "importarr", "importarrWorker", "indexarr",
           "grabarr", "squasharr", "captionarr", "captionarrWorker", "segmentarrWorker", "keda"]
old = {k: props.pop(k) for k in retired if k in props}
defs.pop("serviceBlock", None)

def reword(node, pairs):
    s = json.dumps(node)
    for a, b in pairs:
        s = s.replace(a, b)
    return json.loads(s)

cardigann = reword(old["indexarr"]["properties"]["cardigann"], [("indexarr --", "manager --"), ("indexarr", "the manager")])
facade = old["indexarr"]["properties"]["facade"]
sq = reword(old["squasharr"]["properties"], [("squasharr --", "manager --")])
sched = {"nodeSelector": {"type": "object"}, "tolerations": {"type": "array"}, "affinity": {"type": "object"}}
resources = {"$ref": "#/$defs/resources"}

defs["agentBlock"] = {
    "type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
    "required": ["enabled", "replicas", "consumerSlots", "resources", "nodeSelector", "tolerations", "affinity"],
    "properties": {
        "enabled": {"type": "boolean"},
        "replicas": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0,
                     "description": "Used only with autoscaling.enabled=false: otherwise the manager's HPA owns the replica count and the Deployment carries none."},
        "consumerSlots": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1},
                          "description": "Per-pod handler slots by consumer (CLUSTARR_CONSUMER_SLOTS), also the HPA's per-pod target."},
        "resources": resources, **sched}}

def autoscaled(consumers):
    return {"allOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/agentBlock"},
                      {"properties": {"consumerSlots": {"propertyNames": {"enum": consumers}}}}]}

def fixed(extra):
    return {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
            "required": ["enabled", *extra.keys(), "resources", "nodeSelector", "tolerations", "affinity"],
            "properties": {"enabled": {"type": "boolean"}, **extra, "resources": resources, **sched}}

props["global"] = {"type": "object", "description": "Injected by Helm into a chart with dependencies; clustarr reads nothing from it."}
props["autoscaling"] = {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False, "required": ["enabled"], "properties": {
    "enabled": {"type": "boolean", "description": "The manager owns the queue-driven workloads' HPAs and serves the External Metrics API they read; false renders fixed replicas and no APIService (README, \"Autoscaling\")."}}}
props["manager"] = {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
    "required": ["slots", "intelRenderGroups", "gpuNodeLabelNvidia", "gpuNodeLabelIntel", "cardigann", "resources", "nodeSelector", "tolerations", "affinity"],
    "properties": {"slots": sq["slots"], "intelRenderGroups": sq["intelRenderGroups"],
                   "gpuNodeLabelNvidia": sq["gpuNodeLabelNvidia"], "gpuNodeLabelIntel": sq["gpuNodeLabelIntel"],
                   "cardigann": cardigann, "resources": resources, **sched}}
props["agents"] = {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
    "required": ["catalog", "events", "metadata", "import", "index", "caption"],
    "properties": {
        "catalog": autoscaled(["catalogarr-search-high", "catalogarr-search-normal", "catalogarr-grab", "catalogarr-artwork-render"]),
        "events": autoscaled(["catalogarr-rss-matcher", "catalogarr-redownload", "catalogarr-history", "clustarr-dlq-projector"]),
        "metadata": fixed({}),
        "import": autoscaled(["importarr-scan", "importarr-fileimport", "importarr-list", "importarr-recycle", "importarr-probe-high", "importarr-probe-low"]),
        "index": fixed({"facade": facade}),
        "caption": autoscaled(["captionarr-fetch-high", "captionarr-fetch-normal"]),
    }}
props["markers"] = autoscaled(["segmentarr-analyze"])
d["additionalProperties"] = False
d["required"] = ["image", "storage", "podSecurityContext", "securityContext", "autoscaling", "manager", "agents", "markers"]
d["description"] = (
    "Values for the clustarr umbrella chart (0.5.0: the manager, agent and ui topology). Checks shapes "
    "(types, enums, known number/string formats) so a bad values file fails at `helm install`/`helm template`/"
    "`helm lint` with a schema-path error naming the exact key. The top level is closed: a key chart 0.5.0 "
    "retired (catalogarr, importarr, indexarr, grabarr, squasharr, captionarr and their worker blocks, "
    "segmentarrWorker, keda, image.controller/media/transcoder) fails here; see the README's \"Upgrading from "
    "0.4.x\". Cross-field invariants are clustarr.validate's in templates/_helpers.tpl. nats and cloudnative-pg "
    "pass through to the subcharts, which ship no schema of their own, and are checked only shallowly.")
open(p, "w").write(json.dumps(d, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
```

```markdown
Every workload the chart renders gets `GOMEMLIMIT` set to a share of its own
`resources.limits.memory`, computed at render time (`clustarr.gomemlimit` in
`templates/_helpers.tpl`) as a literal byte count: 80%, except `agent-import`
and `agent-caption` (60%) and `markers` (50%), whose FFmpeg, par2 and ONNX
Runtime allocations live outside the Go heap. The Downward API's
`resourceFieldRef` can only report 100% of a container's own limit, so the
share is computed here, from the same quantity `values.yaml` sets. Change a
memory limit and its `GOMEMLIMIT` moves with it on the next `helm upgrade`;
`config/manager` carries the same figures as literals, and
`TestGOMEMLIMITIsItsShareOfTheLimit` holds the two installers together.
```

```go
//go:build e2e

package e2e

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"

	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/agentdomain"
	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/subtitles"
)

// kubectlOut runs kubectl against the e2e cluster and returns its stdout,
// failing the test on error.
func kubectlOut(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, args ...string) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "kubectl", append([]string{"--context", KubeContext, "-n", Namespace}, args...)...)
	out, err := cmd.Output()
	require.NoError(t, err, "kubectl %v", args)
	return out
}

// TestCaptionAgentScalesFromZero is spec §11.2's gate-6 scenario (§10.4).
// With config/e2e's min-replicas floor removed, agent-caption scales to zero
// on an empty queue, the manager's External Metrics API reports its lag as
// 0, a new SubtitleRequest's fetch task wakes it within two minutes and its
// sidecar appears, and it returns to zero. It runs last (zzz_scale sorts
// after zzz_observability) because it removes the always-a-pod guarantee the
// other scenarios rely on; the cleanup restores it.
func TestCaptionAgentScalesFromZero(t *testing.T) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Minute)
	defer cancel()
	const deployment = "agent-caption"
	kubectlOut(ctx, t, "annotate", "deployment", deployment, agentdomain.AnnotationMinReplicas+"-")
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		cctx, ccancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 6*time.Minute)
		defer ccancel()
		kubectlOut(cctx, t, "annotate", "--overwrite", "deployment", deployment, agentdomain.AnnotationMinReplicas+"=1")
		kubectlOut(cctx, t, "wait", "--for=condition=Available", "deployment/"+deployment, "--timeout=300s")
	})
	replicas := func(ctx context.Context) int32 {
		var d appsv1.Deployment
		if err := k8sClient.Get(ctx, client.ObjectKey{Namespace: Namespace, Name: deployment}, &d); err != nil {
			return -1
		}
		return d.Status.Replicas
	}

	// The 300 s scale-down window plus HPA syncs.
	waitFor(t, ctx, 7*time.Minute, deployment+" scaled to zero",
		func(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) { return replicas(ctx) == 0, nil })
	raw := kubectlOut(ctx, t, "get", "--raw",
		"/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/namespaces/"+Namespace+"/clustarr_consumer_lag?labelSelector=consumer%3Dcaptionarr-fetch-high")
	var list struct {
		Items []struct {
			Value string `json:"value"`
		} `json:"items"`
	}
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(raw, &list), "%s", raw)
	require.Len(t, list.Items, 1, "one series for captionarr-fetch-high")
	assert.Equal(t, "0", list.Items[0].Value, "an empty queue reads lag 0")

	// A new SubtitleRequest: the manager publishes its fetch tasks.
	mf, profile, reqKey := setUpSubtitleFixture(ctx, t, "e2e-scale0")
	waitFor(t, ctx, 2*time.Minute, deployment+" woke from zero",
		func(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) { return replicas(ctx) >= 1, nil })
	sidecar := hostPath(subtitles.SidecarName(mf.Spec.Path, "en", string(profile.Spec.HIExtension)))
	waitFor(t, ctx, subtitleFetchTimeout, "the en sidecar for "+mf.Name,
		func(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) { _, err := os.Stat(sidecar); return err == nil, nil },
		describeSubtitleRequest(reqKey))
	waitFor(t, ctx, 7*time.Minute, deployment+" back to zero",
		func(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) { return replicas(ctx) == 0, nil })
}
```

```go
// TestTheWorkflowsCheckImagesThroughOneScript: CI and the release check
// images only through hack/image-checks.sh, naming checks it defines, build
// only the images that exist, and CI refuses a go.mod that replaces a module
// with a local directory, naming the cause, instead of failing obscurely in
// go mod download.
func TestTheWorkflowsCheckImagesThroughOneScript(t *testing.T) {
	root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
	patterns := imageCheckPatterns(t, root)
	known := func(c string) bool {
		for _, p := range patterns {
			if p.MatchString(c) {
				return true
			}
		}
		return false
	}
	type step struct {
		Name string `json:"name"`
		Run  string `json:"run"`
	}
	type job struct {
		Strategy struct {
			Matrix struct {
				Include []map[string]any `json:"include"`
			} `json:"matrix"`
		} `json:"strategy"`
		Steps []step `json:"steps"`
	}
	for _, f := range []string{".github/workflows/ci.yml", ".github/workflows/release.yml"} {
		raw := readRepoFile(t, root, f)
		for _, gone := range []string{"kedacore", "Dockerfile.media", "Dockerfile.transcoder", "Dockerfile.controller", "--self-check="} {
			assert.NotContains(t, string(raw), gone, f)
		}
		var wf struct {
			Jobs map[string]job `json:"jobs"`
		}
		require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(raw, &wf), f)
		var checksRun bool
		for name, j := range wf.Jobs {
			for _, inc := range j.Strategy.Matrix.Include {
				checks, _ := inc["checks"].(string)
				for _, c := range strings.Fields(checks) {
					assert.True(t, known(c), "%s job %s's matrix names check %q, which hack/image-checks.sh does not define", f, name, c)
				}
			}
			for _, s := range j.Steps {
				if strings.Contains(s.Run, "hack/image-checks.sh") {
					checksRun = true
				}
				assert.NotContains(t, s.Run, "docker run", "%s job %s step %q checks an image itself", f, name, s.Name)
			}
		}
		assert.True(t, checksRun, "%s never runs hack/image-checks.sh", f)
	}
	assert.Contains(t, string(readRepoFile(t, root, ".github/workflows/ci.yml")), `grep -nE '^replace .* => \.{1,2}/' go.mod`)
}
```

```yaml
# Verifies every push to main and every pull request: lint, generated code in
# sync, and the full unit + envtest suite -- the same gate a change must pass
# locally (`make generate manifests build lint test`, plus `go vet -tags e2e`).
#
# make test runs with CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1, so a missing tool (FFmpeg's
# libraries and the shims from `make native-assets`, helm and kustomize for
# the installer guards, KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS) fails rather than skips. The
# native test assets are the image's own pins (hack/native-assets.sh reads
# images/Dockerfile.native), not static executables. The e2e suite is only
# compiled here; it needs a kind cluster. A go.mod that replaces a module
# with a local directory (the ffgo fork, par2go) cannot build here, and the
# generated job says so first.
```

```yaml
  images:
    name: image ${{ matrix.image }} (${{ matrix.arch }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { image: clustarr, file: images/Dockerfile.clustarr, target: clustarr, arch: amd64, runner: ubuntu-24.04,
              checks: "version:manager version:ui no-shell" }
          - { image: native, file: images/Dockerfile.native, target: native, arch: amd64, runner: ubuntu-24.04,
              checks: "self-check:transcode:cpu self-check:transcode:cuda self-check:transcode:intel self-check:agent version:agent version:markers version:transcode no-shell" }
          - { image: native, file: images/Dockerfile.native, target: native, arch: arm64, runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm,
              checks: "self-check:transcode:cpu self-check:agent version:agent version:markers version:transcode no-shell" }
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1

      - name: Build ${{ matrix.image }}
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: ${{ matrix.file }}
          target: ${{ matrix.target }}
          platforms: linux/${{ matrix.arch }}
          load: true
          tags: selfcheck/${{ matrix.image }}:ci
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=${{ matrix.image }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=${{ matrix.image }}-${{ matrix.arch }}

      # The one definition of the image checks (hack/image-checks.sh); GPU
      # encodes need hardware (--trial, run on hosts that have it).
      - name: Check ${{ matrix.image }}
        env:
          IMAGE: selfcheck/${{ matrix.image }}:ci
          CHECKS: ${{ matrix.checks }}
        # CHECKS is a space-separated list, split on purpose.
        run: hack/image-checks.sh "$IMAGE" $CHECKS
```

## Wave 6b: test media without the CLI (W6.18 to W6.24)

**Source:** main's `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-06-unify-media-upgrade-guide.md` (commits `4377f49f`, `013b0eb8`): **U2**, the owner's decision of 2026-10-06 that no test may run the `ffmpeg` or `ffprobe` CLI, with fixture clips made on ffgo or committed, and every R2 parity check reading goldens recorded once from the exec implementation before it is deleted. Spec sections the decision amends: §4.5.6 (the guard), §6.7 (probe parity), §7.2.6/§7.2.10 (decode parity), §7.3.2 (extraction parity), §10.1.6-§10.1.8 (assets, CI, e2e fixtures).

**Order.** After W6.17 green and before W7.1: W6.18, then W6.19-W6.22 in any order (each owns its directories), then W6.23 (it needs every exec implementation still present: Wave 7 deletes the first), then W6.24.

**What stays until Wave 10.** `make native-assets` keeps the `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` CLIs, because the exec implementations Waves 7-8 delete still run them (and W6.23's recorder calls those implementations, never the CLIs itself). W10.9 adds the guard, W10.10 takes the CLIs out of the assets and CI, W10.11 rebuilds the e2e fixtures without them.

**The conversion table** (W6.19-W6.22, and every U2 amendment later). `internal/testmedia` models the ffmpeg command line, so a conversion is mechanical and keeps every assertion:

| ffmpeg argument | `testmedia` |
|---|---|
| `-f lavfi -i <graph>` (video: `testsrc2=…`, `color=…`, a chain such as `…,setfield=tff`) | `Video{Source: "<graph>"}` |
| `-f lavfi -i <graph>` (audio: `sine=…`, `anullsrc=…`, `…,aformat=channel_layouts=5.1(side)`) | `Audio{Source: "<graph>"}` |
| `-i some.wav` that the test wrote in Go | `Audio{Samples: &testmedia.Samples{Rate: r, Mono: x}}` |
| `-c:v X`, `-c:a X`, `-c:s srt\|ass` | `Video.Encoder`, `Audio.Encoder`, `Subtitle.Codec` (`subrip`, `ass`) |
| `-pix_fmt P`, `-sample_fmt F`, `-ar R`, `-ac N`, `-b:a 320k` | `Video.PixFmt`, `Audio.SampleFmt`, `Audio.SampleRate`, `Audio.Layout`, `Audio.BitrateKbps` |
| `-bf`, `-g`, `-flags`, `-x264-params`, `-x265-params`, `-strict`, `-center_mixlev`, `-bits_per_raw_sample`, `-crf`, `-preset` | `Options` of that stream (`"bf": "3"`, `"x265-params": "…"`) |
| `-color_primaries`, `-color_trc`, `-colorspace`, `-color_range` | `Video.Color` |
| x265 `master-display`/`max-cll`, or HDR10 side data | `Video.HDR10` |
| `-frames:v N`, `-shortest`, `-t D` | `Video.Frames`, `Spec.Shortest`, `Spec.Duration` |
| `-itsoffset S` before an input | that stream's `Offset` |
| `-output_ts_offset S` | `Spec.StartOffset` |
| `-metadata k=v`, `-metadata:s:X:i k=v`, `-disposition:X:i d` | `Spec.Tags`, `Stream.Metadata`, `Stream.Disposition` |
| a subtitle input file (`-i x.srt`) | `Subtitle{Events: testmedia.ParseSRT(t, body)}` |
| `-attach f -metadata:s:t mimetype=m` | `Spec.Attachments` |
| an `;FFMETADATA1` chapters input | `Spec.Chapters` (with the file's `TIMEBASE`) |
| `-f <muxer>`, `-movflags …` | `Spec.Format`, `Spec.MuxerOptions` |
| cutting a file short (`head -c`, `truncate`) | `testmedia.Truncate(t, path, n)` |
| `ffprobe -show_format/-show_streams/-show_chapters … -of json` used to **inspect** a test's output | `testmedia.Inspect(t, path)` |
| `ffprobe -show_entries stream=profile,pix_fmt,color_*,sample_aspect_ratio,codec_tag_string,channel_layout,start_time`, `stream_side_data=side_data_type` | `Inspect`'s `StreamInfo.{Profile, PixFmt, Color, SampleAspectRatio, CodecTag, Layout, StartTime, SideData}` |
| `ffprobe -count_frames … nb_read_frames`, `-show_entries frame=pts`, `frame_side_data=side_data_type` | `len(testmedia.Frames(t, path, i))`, `FrameInfo.PTS`, `FrameInfo.SideData` |
| `ffprobe -show_entries packet=stream_index,pts_time,pos` | `testmedia.Packets(t, path)` |
| `ffmpeg -i x -af astats -f null -` (per-channel RMS) | `testmedia.ChannelRMS(t, path, i)` |
| `-filter_complex` over inputs the test wrote in Go (`adelay=ms`, `volume=v`, `amix`) | the samples computed in Go (prepend `ms` of zeros, scale, sum), then `Audio{Samples: …}` |
| `-i existing -map 0 -c copy -metadata[:s:X:i] k=v [-t D] out` (retag or cut a file) | `testmedia.Remux(t, existing, name, testmedia.Retag{Tags, StreamMetadata, Until})` |
| a lavfi stream muxed with streams `-c copy`'d from another test clip | one `Spec` that carries every stream itself |
| `-b:v R`, `-minrate`, `-maxrate`, `-bufsize` | the video stream's `Options` (`"b": R`, …) |
| `-vtag T` / `-tag:v T` | dropped: no converted assertion reads the codec tag (`fileimport/probe_envtest_test.go`'s `[XviD]` comes from `pkg/naming` mapping codec `mpeg4` to XviD); `StreamInfo.CodecTag` reads one back where a test asserts it |
| `exec.LookPath("ffmpeg")` and a "not FFmpeg 9" check that only gate clip making | `testmedia.Require(t)` |

A Dolby Vision RPU cannot be synthesised on ffgo either: those tests keep their named skip.

```go
package testmedia_test

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/mediactl/clustarr/internal/testmedia"
)

// everything is helpers_test.go's everythingClip, as a Spec: H.264 video,
// English AC-3 5.1 (default), French AAC stereo "Commentary" (comment),
// English SubRip (forced), a font, two chapters, container title "Clip".
func everything(seconds int) testmedia.Spec {
	half := int64(seconds) * 500
	return testmedia.Spec{
		Duration: time.Duration(seconds) * time.Second, Shortest: true, Tags: map[string]string{"title": "Clip", "CLUSTARR_PROFILE": "p@h"},
		Video: []testmedia.Video{{Source: "testsrc2=size=160x90:rate=24", Encoder: "libx264", Options: map[string]string{"preset": "ultrafast"}}},
		Audio: []testmedia.Audio{
			{Source: "sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000", Encoder: "ac3", Layout: "5.1(side)", Stream: testmedia.Stream{Language: "eng", Disposition: []string{"default"}}},
			{Source: "sine=frequency=880:sample_rate=48000", Encoder: "aac", Layout: "stereo", Stream: testmedia.Stream{Language: "fre", Title: "Commentary", Disposition: []string{"comment"}}},
		},
		Subtitles:   []testmedia.Subtitle{{Codec: "subrip", Events: []testmedia.Event{{Start: 500 * time.Millisecond, End: 1500 * time.Millisecond, Text: "Hello"}}, Stream: testmedia.Stream{Language: "eng", Disposition: []string{"forced"}}}},
		Attachments: []testmedia.Attachment{{Name: "font.ttf", MIMEType: "application/x-truetype-font", Data: []byte("not really a font")}},
		Chapters:    []testmedia.Chapter{{Start: 0, End: half, TimeBase: [2]int{1, 1000}, Title: "One"}, {Start: half, End: 2 * half, TimeBase: [2]int{1, 1000}, Title: "Two"}},
	}
}

func TestAClipCarriesWhatItsSpecSays(t *testing.T) {
	path := testmedia.Make(t, "everything.mkv", everything(2))
	info := testmedia.Inspect(t, path)
	assert.Equal(t, "matroska,webm", info.Format)
	assert.InDelta(t, 2.0, info.Duration.Seconds(), 0.1)
	assert.Equal(t, "Clip", info.Tags["title"])
	assert.Equal(t, "p@h", info.Tags["CLUSTARR_PROFILE"])
	require.Len(t, info.Streams, 5)
	assert.Equal(t, "h264", info.Streams[0].Codec)
	assert.Equal(t, []any{"ac3", "eng", 6, []string{"default"}}, []any{info.Streams[1].Codec, info.Streams[1].Language, info.Streams[1].Channels, info.Streams[1].Disposition})
	assert.Equal(t, []any{"aac", "fre", "Commentary", 2}, []any{info.Streams[2].Codec, info.Streams[2].Language, info.Streams[2].Title, info.Streams[2].Channels})
	assert.Contains(t, info.Streams[2].Disposition, "comment")
	assert.Equal(t, []any{"subtitle", "subrip", "eng"}, []any{info.Streams[3].Type, info.Streams[3].Codec, info.Streams[3].Language})
	assert.Contains(t, info.Streams[3].Disposition, "forced")
	assert.Equal(t, "attachment", info.Streams[4].Type)

	assert.Equal(t, "Two", info.Chapters[1].Title)
}

func TestHDR10AndTenBitHEVC(t *testing.T) {
	path := testmedia.Make(t, "hdr10.mkv", testmedia.Spec{Duration: time.Second, Video: []testmedia.Video{{
		Source: "testsrc2=size=160x90:rate=24", Encoder: "libx265", PixFmt: "yuv420p10le",
		Options: map[string]string{"x265-params": "log-level=error"},
		HDR10:   &testmedia.HDR10{MasteringDisplay: [10]uint32{13250, 34500, 7500, 3000, 34000, 16000, 15635, 16450, 10000000, 50}, MaxCLL: 1000, MaxFALL: 400},
	}}})

	assert.Contains(t, info.Streams[0].SideData, "Mastering display metadata")
	assert.Contains(t, testmedia.Frames(t, path, 0)[0].SideData, "Mastering display metadata")
}

// The inspectors the converted tests assert through, in place of ffprobe's
// stream, frame and packet entries, ffmpeg's astats, and `-c copy` retags.
func TestTheInspectorsReadWhatTheConvertedTestsAssert(t *testing.T) {
	path := testmedia.Make(t, "everything.mkv", everything(2))
	info := testmedia.Inspect(t, path)
	assert.NotEmpty(t, info.Streams[0].Profile)
	assert.NotEmpty(t, info.Streams[0].PixFmt)
	assert.Equal(t, "5.1(side)", info.Streams[1].Layout)
	frames := testmedia.Frames(t, path, 0)
	require.Len(t, frames, 48, "2 s at 24 fps")
	for i := 1; i < len(frames); i++ {
		assert.Greater(t, frames[i].PTS, frames[i-1].PTS)
	}
	per := map[int]int{}
	for _, p := range testmedia.Packets(t, path) {
		per[p.Stream]++
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 48, per[0])
	assert.NotZero(t, per[1])
	assert.Len(t, testmedia.ChannelRMS(t, path, 1), 6)
	re := testmedia.Remux(t, path, "retag.mkv", testmedia.Retag{Tags: map[string]string{"CLUSTARR_PROFILE": "q@r"}, StreamMetadata: map[int]map[string]string{2: {"language": "ger"}}})
	got := testmedia.Inspect(t, re)
	assert.Equal(t, "q@r", got.Tags["CLUSTARR_PROFILE"])
	assert.Equal(t, "Clip", got.Tags["title"], "a retag keeps the tags it does not name")
	assert.Equal(t, "ger", got.Streams[2].Language)
	assert.Len(t, got.Streams, len(info.Streams))
}

func TestTruncateAndTheSameSpecWritesTheSameBytes(t *testing.T) {
	a := testmedia.Make(t, "a.mkv", everything(1))
	b := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "b.mkv")
	require.NoError(t, testmedia.Write(b, everything(1)))
	ba, err := os.ReadFile(a)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	bb, err := os.ReadFile(b)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, sha256.Sum256(ba), sha256.Sum256(bb), "bit-exact: the goldens' clips are reproducible on one FFmpeg build")
	cut := testmedia.Truncate(t, a, 4096)
	st, err := os.Stat(cut)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, int64(4096), st.Size())
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** `require.go`:

```go
// Require skips t unless FFmpeg 9's libraries and a versioned libffshim
// load. With CLUSTARR_FFGO_REQUIRE=1 (CI) a missing library fails t, so a
// test that needs ffgo can never pass by skipping (upgrade guide U2.1).
func Require(t testing.TB) {
	t.Helper()
	miss := func(format string, args ...any) {
		if os.Getenv("CLUSTARR_FFGO_REQUIRE") == "1" {
			t.Fatalf("testmedia: "+format, args...)
		}
		t.Skipf("testmedia: "+format, args...)
	}
	if err := ffgo.Init(); err != nil {
		miss("no FFmpeg libraries: %v", err)
	}
	if _, avc, _ := ffgo.Version(); avc>>16 != 63 {
		miss("libavcodec %d is not FFmpeg 9's 63", avc>>16)
	}
	if ffgo.ShimAPIVersion() < 1 {
		miss("libffshim has no API version (want the clustarr/unify-media fork's shim, FFSHIM_API_VERSION >= 1)")
	}
	if err := avdevice.RegisterAll(); err != nil { // lavfi sources
		miss("libavdevice: %v", err)
	}
}
```

  `write.go`, the core (one function per concern; the shapes are the contract):

```go
// Write makes the clip s describes at path, as the equivalent ffmpeg
// command would: every source is a lavfi graph read through ffgo's
// demuxer (Samples go through a WAV and amovie), every stream is encoded
// with its encoder and Options, and packets are interleaved by
// presentation time. Muxer and encoders run bit-exact (fflags and flags
// +bitexact, one thread each), so one FFmpeg build writes the same bytes.
func Write(path string, s Spec) error {
	// A lavfi source opens only after avdevice.RegisterAll (W0.30), which
	// Require does for tests; hack/record-goldens and test/fixtures/mkclips
	// call Write without Require.
	if err := registerDevices(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("testmedia: libavdevice: %w", err)
	}
	m, err := ffgo.NewMuxer(path, s.format(path))
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("testmedia: %w", err)
	}
	defer m.Close()
	var srcs []*source // one per Video and Audio: a lavfi decoder, an encoder and its muxer stream
	for i := range s.Video {
		src, err := openVideo(m, s.Video[i], s.Duration)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		srcs = append(srcs, src)
	}
	for i := range s.Audio {
		src, err := openAudio(m, s.Audio[i], s.Duration)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		srcs = append(srcs, src)
	}
	subs := make([]*ffgo.MuxerStream, len(s.Subtitles))
	for i, sub := range s.Subtitles {
		if subs[i], err = m.AddSubtitleStream(&ffgo.SubtitleStreamConfig{Codec: sub.codec(), Header: []byte(sub.Header), Options: sub.Stream.options()}); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("testmedia: subtitle %d: %w", i, err)
		}
	}
	for _, a := range s.Attachments {
		if err := m.AddAttachment(ffgo.Attachment{Filename: a.Name, MimeType: a.MIMEType, Data: a.Data}); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("testmedia: attachment %s: %w", a.Name, err)
		}
	}
	if err := m.SetChapters(s.chapters()); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := m.SetMetadata(ffgo.Metadata(s.Tags)); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	opts := map[string]string{"fflags": "+bitexact"}
	maps.Copy(opts, s.MuxerOptions)
	if err := m.WriteHeaderWithOptions(opts); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for i, sub := range s.Subtitles {
		for n, ev := range sub.Events {
			if err := m.WriteSubtitle(subs[i], ffgo.SubtitleEvent{PTS: ev.Start.Microseconds(), Duration: (ev.End - ev.Start).Microseconds(), Data: sub.packet(n, ev)}); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
	}
	if err := interleave(m, srcs, s.Shortest, s.StartOffset); err != nil { // always encodes the source whose next frame is earliest
		return err
	}
	return m.WriteTrailer()
}
```

  `registerDevices` is a package-level `sync.Once` around `avdevice.RegisterAll()` that keeps
  its error (registering twice is harmless, so `Require` keeps its own call).
  `openVideo` opens `ffgo.NewDecoderWithOptions(v.Source + durationSuffix, &ffgo.DecoderOptions{Format: "lavfi"})`,
  adds `format=<PixFmt>` to the graph when `PixFmt` is set, builds `ffgo.NewVideoStreamEncoder` with
  `EncoderName: v.Encoder` (default `libx264`), the source's size and rate, `CodecOptions` =
  `{"threads": "1", "flags": "+bitexact"}` plus `v.Options`, `SideData` from `v.HDR10` (mastering
  display and content light, as W0.30's test builds them), and adds it with
  `m.AddEncoderStream(enc, ffgo.StreamOptions{… v.Stream, SideData: the same two blobs})`; each frame gets
  `SetColorSpec` from `v.Color` (BT.2020/PQ/BT.2020nc when `HDR10` is set and `Color` is zero). `openAudio`
  does the same with `ffgo.NewAudioEncoder(ffgo.AudioEncoderConfig2{EncoderName, SampleRate, Layout,
  BitRate, Options})`, appending `aformat=sample_fmts=<the encoder's format>:channel_layouts=<Layout>` to the
  graph; `Samples` writes a 16-bit WAV beside the clip and uses `amovie=<path>` as the source; `Offset` is
  added to every packet's timestamps (rescaled to the stream's time base), as `-itsoffset` does.
  `durationSuffix` appends `:d=<Duration>` only when the graph's first filter has no `d=`/`duration=`.
  `inspect.go` reads the file back with `ffgo.NewDecoder` (format name, duration, tags, each stream's type,
  codec name, language, title, disposition names, channels, sample rate, size and tags, and the chapters)
  and fails `t` on an error. `ParseSRT` parses SubRip cues; `Truncate` copies the first `keep` bytes. `Inspect` fills `CodecTag` from `avcodec.GetCodecParTag(s.CodecParameters())` and `SideData` from `ffgo.StreamSideData`; `Frames`, `Packets` and `ChannelRMS` read with the same decoder (`ReadPacket`; each decoded frame's `BestEffortTimestamp` (F5) and `Frame.SideData` for the HDR types; float PCM per channel). `RemuxFile` opens `src` with `ffgo.NewDecoder`, adds one `AddCopyStream` per stream with its metadata merged with `StreamMetadata[i]`, sets the source's format tags merged with `Tags`, copies packets until `Until`, and is bit-exact like `Write` (`fflags +bitexact`). All of it (`Packet.Pos`, `Frame.SideData`, `StreamSideData`, `GetCodecParTag`, `AddCopyStream`, `WritePacket`) is in the fork's base tag, ffgo `.11` and later: no fork addition.
  `doc.go`: "Package testmedia writes deterministic test clips on ffgo, the model of an ffmpeg command line,
  so no test runs the ffmpeg or ffprobe CLI (owner decision of 2026-10-06; upgrade guide U2). Tests,
  hack/record-goldens and test/fixtures/mkclips import it; no binary does (TestNoBinaryLinksTestmedia)."

- [ ] **Step 4: Run and pass.**

```bash
go build ./... && go vet ./internal/testmedia/
CLUSTARR_FFGO_REQUIRE=1 go test -count=1 -v ./internal/testmedia/
```
  Expected: every test `PASS`, none `SKIP` (the host has FFmpeg 9's libraries; under `$NATIVE`, the
  Waves 7-10 preamble's "The native test environment" after `make native-assets`, the pinned ones). If the byte-equality case fails, a component is not bit-exact: find it (the muxer's
  `bitexact`, an encoder's threads) and fix it here; do not drop the assertion.

```bash
git commit -m "test(testmedia): internal/testmedia writes test clips on ffgo -- lavfi sources, any encoder and its options, HDR10 side data, text subtitles, attachments, chapters and tags, bit-exact -- and reads them back, so no test needs the ffmpeg or ffprobe CLI (upgrade guide U2.1)" -- internal/testmedia
```

  - `probe/<name>.json`: `{"mediaInfo": <commonv1.MediaInfo>, "raw": <the whole mediainfo.Raw, go-ffprobe's types as JSON>, "audio": <mediainfo.AudioProbe>|null, "audioError": ""}`. The whole Raw, so W8.4 can compare the leaves it reads and run `transcode.FromProbe` and the standard's plan on the golden side too.
  - `extract/<name>.s<index>.srt`: the exec extractor's bytes for each text subtitle stream.
  - `decode/<name>.json`: `{"audio": [{"stream": 0, "from": 12.5, "dur": 10, "samples": n, "sha256": "…", "chromaprint": [ … ]}], "frames": [{"from": 15, "count": n, "sha256": ["…"]}], "frame": [{"at": 7.3, "sha256": "…"}]}` for W7.6's windows (audio at 0, 12.05, 12.5 for 10 s; frames at 15; a frame at 1, 7.3, 12.05, 20.5 and 29). `chromaprint` is `pkg/segments/chromaprint.Fingerprint` of the window, so a mismatch can still report the Hamming distance W7.6's `compareAudio` prints.
  - package `github.com/mediactl/clustarr/test/goldens`: `Manifest(t) []Entry` with `type Entry struct{ Name, Path string; Kinds []string; SHA256, Spec string }` (the MANIFEST, `Path` module-relative); `ClipPath(name string) string` (that entry's `Path`, made absolute from the module root); `GoldenPath(kind, name string) string` (`probe/<name>.json`, `decode/<name>.json`, and for `extract` the glob `extract/<name>.s*.srt`, since extraction goldens are one file per stream); `Clips(t, kind string) map[string]string` (name → path of a committed clip that has goldens of that kind, checked against its MANIFEST sha256), `Probe(t, name) ProbeGolden`, `Extract(t, name string, stream int) []byte`, `Decode(t, name) DecodeGolden`, and the types.

```go
// The goldens are what the parity tests compare with after the exec
// implementations are gone, so they must be complete and intact: every
// clip in the manifest exists with its recorded hash, and every kind it
// names has a golden (upgrade guide U2.3).
func TestTheGoldensAreCompleteAndIntact(t *testing.T) {
	m := goldens.Manifest(t)
	require.NotEmpty(t, m)
	var total int64
	for _, c := range m {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(goldens.ClipPath(c.Name))
		require.NoError(t, err, c.Name)
		assert.Equal(t, c.SHA256, fmt.Sprintf("%x", sha256.Sum256(b)), "%s changed after it was recorded", c.Name)
		assert.LessOrEqual(t, len(b), 1<<20, "%s is over 1 MiB", c.Name)
		total += int64(len(b))
		for _, k := range c.Kinds {
			m, err := filepath.Glob(goldens.GoldenPath(k, c.Name)) // extract is one file per stream
			require.NoError(t, err)
			assert.NotEmpty(t, m, "%s has no %s golden", c.Name, k)
		}
	}
	assert.LessOrEqual(t, total, int64(16<<20), "the committed clips stay under 16 MiB")
	for _, k := range []string{"probe", "extract", "decode"} {
		assert.NotEmpty(t, goldens.Clips(t, k), "no clip carries %s goldens", k)
	}
}
```

### Wave-specific rules

- **Order.** W7 → W8 → W9 → W10, each after the installers wave (§11.1 step 9).
  W8 and W9 additionally need `cmd/clustarr` deleted (W5.17): they put purego
  into packages `cmd/clustarr` linked. Inside a wave, tasks run in order unless
  a task says it may run in parallel.
- **The native test environment.** Every native test (FFmpeg, ffgo's shim, ORT,
  par2go) runs with the variables `make test` exports (§10.1.6); `t.Setenv` is
  too late, because ffgo maps FFmpeg at package init. Save once as
  `<scratchpad>/native-env.sh` (scratchpad: this session's scratchpad directory;
  not committed) and source it before every `go test` below that names it:

  ```bash
  export NATIVE_ASSETS="$(go env GOPATH)/bin/native-assets"
  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$NATIVE_ASSETS/lib" CLUSTARR_NATIVE_ASSETS="$NATIVE_ASSETS" \
         FFGO_SHIM_DIR="$NATIVE_ASSETS/lib" ORT_LIB_PATH="$NATIVE_ASSETS/lib/libonnxruntime.so" \
         PAR2GO_LIB="$NATIVE_ASSETS/lib/libpar2shim.so" PATH="$NATIVE_ASSETS/bin:$PATH" \
         CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1
  ```

  `$NATIVE` below means `. <scratchpad>/native-env.sh &&`. Run `make native-assets`
  once first. A native test that reports SKIP under `$NATIVE` is a failure of the
  step, never a pass (the CLAUDE.md silent-skip gotcha).
- **Envtest.** `$ENVTEST` means
  `KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS="$($(go env GOPATH)/bin/setup-envtest use 1.37.0 -i -p path)"`.
  Envtest packages these waves touch: `app/catalog/controller/mediafile`,
  `app/catalog/worker/segmentresults`, `app/import/worker/fileimport`,
  `app/import/worker/rescan`, `app/squash/worker`,
  `app/squash/controller/transcodejob`, `internal/cli/agent`.
- **Parity tests** carry `//go:build parity` and live under `test/`, which the
  exec guard does not scan (§4.5.6). Run them with `-tags parity` under
  `$NATIVE`, so the CLIs in `$NATIVE_ASSETS/bin` are BtbN's FFmpeg 9.0.2, the
  same build ffgo loads.
- **Formatting.** After every edit run
  `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/gofumpt -w <files>` and
  `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/goimports -local github.com/mediactl/clustarr -w <files>`.
  Every new `.go` file starts with `hack/boilerplate.go.txt` verbatim, a blank
  line, then `package`; the snippets below omit the header.
- **No go.mod edit, no `go get`, no `go mod tidy`** (step 0c owns the three edits).
- **No field manager, CRD field, stream, consumer or RBAC rule is added** in W7-W9
  (§8.6: par2 owns none; §7: decode and extraction write nothing). `make manifests`
  must leave `config/` and `charts/` unchanged; each wave gate checks.
- **AudioGraft drift.** The graft run (`cmd/transcode --graft-task`,
  `app/squash/worker/graft`, `pkg/transcode/engine/graft.go`) decodes on ffgo
  in-process already. W8.5 routes its FFmpeg log through `ffruntime` and loads
  FFmpeg through `ffruntime.Load` before a graft runs; nothing else in these waves
  touches it. main's `142d0d4b` (an arm64 image with no libva environment)
  is carried by the installers wave as `native-base` plus `native-amd64` and
  `native-arm64` (W6.5); W9.7 puts `ENV PAR2GO_LIB` on `native-base`.
- **Commits** are path-scoped (`git commit -m '…' -- <paths>`); `git add` new files
  first; a `git mv` stages both paths, so the pathspec names both. Never
  `git stash`, never push.

`pkg/ffruntime/do_test.go` (package `ffruntime`, internal, for the seams):

```go
package ffruntime

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// seams sets the grace and the wedge threshold for one test and resets the
// process-wide abandonment state around it. No test in this package is
// parallel: the state is the process's.
func seams(t *testing.T, g time.Duration, max int) {
	t.Helper()
	resetDo()
	oldGrace, oldMax := grace, maxAbandoned
	grace, maxAbandoned = g, max
	t.Cleanup(func() { grace, maxAbandoned = oldGrace, oldMax; resetDo() })
}

func TestDoReturnsTheBodysResult(t *testing.T) {
	seams(t, 50*time.Millisecond, MaxAbandoned)
	boom := errors.New("boom")
	assert.NoError(t, Do(context.Background(), func(context.Context) error { return nil }))
	assert.ErrorIs(t, Do(context.Background(), func(context.Context) error { return boom }), boom)
}

func TestDoNeverStartsAfterItsContextEnded(t *testing.T) {
	seams(t, 50*time.Millisecond, MaxAbandoned)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	cancel()
	ran := false
	err := Do(ctx, func(context.Context) error { ran = true; return nil })
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, context.Canceled)
	assert.False(t, ran)
}

// A body that honours its context inside the grace is not abandoned.
func TestABodyThatStopsInsideTheGraceIsNotAbandoned(t *testing.T) {
	seams(t, time.Second, MaxAbandoned)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	go func() { time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
	err := Do(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error { <-ctx.Done(); return ctx.Err() })
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, context.Canceled)
	assert.NotErrorIs(t, err, ErrAbandoned)
	assert.Zero(t, Abandoned())
}

// The old process-group kill's replacement: a call blocked past its context
// returns after the grace, and is counted until it returns (spec §7.4).
func TestACancelledCallReturnsWithinTheGraceAndIsCountedUntilItReturns(t *testing.T) {
	seams(t, 100*time.Millisecond, MaxAbandoned)
	release := make(chan struct{})
	start := time.Now()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Millisecond)
	defer cancel()
	err := Do(ctx, func(context.Context) error { <-release; return nil })
	assert.Less(t, time.Since(start), time.Second)
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrAbandoned)
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, context.DeadlineExceeded)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, Abandoned())
	close(release)
	assert.Eventually(t, func() bool { return Abandoned() == 0 }, time.Second, 5*time.Millisecond,
		"a call that returns after being abandoned is no longer counted")
}

func TestMaxAbandonedWedgesTheProcess(t *testing.T) {
	seams(t, 10*time.Millisecond, 2)
	release := make(chan struct{})
	defer close(release)
	for range 2 {
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Millisecond)
		require.ErrorIs(t, Do(ctx, func(context.Context) error { <-release; return nil }), ErrAbandoned)
		cancel()
	}
	select {
	case <-Wedged():
	case <-time.After(time.Second):
		t.Fatal("Wedged() did not close at MaxAbandoned outstanding calls")
	}
	assert.ErrorIs(t, Do(context.Background(), func(context.Context) error { return nil }), ErrWedged)
	assert.ErrorIs(t, Healthz(nil), ErrWedged)
}
```

`pkg/ffruntime/log_test.go` (package `ffruntime`):

```go
func newRouterForTest(t *testing.T, now func() time.Time) (*logRouter, *bytes.Buffer) {
	t.Helper()
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	r := newLogRouter(now)
	r.logger = slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(&buf, &slog.HandlerOptions{Level: slog.LevelDebug}))
	return r, &buf
}

// Errors reach slog at Warn as "ffmpeg", at most a burst of 20 and then
// 10 a second; warnings and below never do (spec §7.4).
func TestErrorsReachSlogRateLimited(t *testing.T) {
	now := time.Unix(0, 0)
	r, buf := newRouterForTest(t, func() time.Time { return now })
	r.dispatch(ffgo.LogWarning, "a warning\n")
	for range 100 {
		r.dispatch(ffgo.LogError, "an error\n")
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 20, strings.Count(buf.String(), "msg=ffmpeg"))
	assert.NotContains(t, buf.String(), "a warning")
	now = now.Add(time.Second)
	for range 100 {
		r.dispatch(ffgo.LogError, "an error\n")
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 30, strings.Count(buf.String(), "msg=ffmpeg"), "10 more after one second")
}

func TestCaptureSeesEveryLineUntilReleased(t *testing.T) {
	r, _ := newRouterForTest(t, time.Now)
	var got []string
	release := r.capture(func(_ ffgo.LogLevel, m string) { got = append(got, m) })
	r.dispatch(ffgo.LogWarning, "w")
	r.dispatch(ffgo.LogError, "e")
	release()
	r.dispatch(ffgo.LogError, "after")
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"w", "e"}, got)
}

func TestMuteSilencesSlogButNotCaptures(t *testing.T) {
	r, buf := newRouterForTest(t, time.Now)
	var got int
	defer r.capture(func(ffgo.LogLevel, string) { got++ })()
	unmute := r.mute()
	r.dispatch(ffgo.LogError, "muted")
	unmute()
	r.dispatch(ffgo.LogError, "heard")
	assert.Equal(t, 2, got)
	assert.NotContains(t, buf.String(), "muted")
	assert.Contains(t, buf.String(), "heard")
}
```

```go
// Report names the files the dynamic loader actually mapped, so a host's
// system FFmpeg can never stand in for the pinned build (spec §7.4).
func TestMappedFindsTheLoadedLibraries(t *testing.T) {
	maps := []byte(strings.Join([]string{
		"7f00-7f01 r--p 00000000 08:01 1 /opt/native/lib/libavutil.so.60.3.100",
		"7f01-7f02 r-xp 00001000 08:01 2 /opt/native/lib/libavcodec.so.63.1.100",
		"7f02-7f03 r--p 00000000 08:01 3 /opt/native lib/libavformat.so.63.1.101",
		"7f03-7f04 r--p 00000000 00:00 0 ",
		"7f04-7f05 r--p 00000000 08:01 4 /usr/lib/libffshim.so",
	}, "\n"))
	assert.Equal(t, "/opt/native/lib/libavutil.so.60.3.100", mapped(maps, "libavutil.so"))
	assert.Equal(t, "/opt/native/lib/libavcodec.so.63.1.100", mapped(maps, "libavcodec.so"))

	assert.Equal(t, "/usr/lib/libffshim.so", mapped(maps, "libffshim.so"))
	assert.Empty(t, mapped(maps, "libswscale.so"))
}
```

```go
// Package ffruntime is the one runtime gate every binary that links ffgo
// passes through (spec 2026-10-06 §7.4). Load maps FFmpeg 9 and the ffgo
// shim once and checks the shim's API; Require checks the demuxers,
// decoders, encoders and filters a caller needs; one process-wide log
// trampoline routes FFmpeg's log to slog (RouteLog), to a run's own sink
// (Capture) or nowhere (Mute); and Do bounds every in-process FFmpeg call by
// its context plus Grace, counting calls it had to abandon until they
// return, and reports the process wedged at MaxAbandoned outstanding calls.
//
// ffgo dlopens FFmpeg at package init (avutil/avutil.go's init), not at
// Load, so any binary linking this package has mapped FFmpeg before main.
// It imports the standard library and ffgo only (TestFFRuntimeImportsOnlyFFgo).
package ffruntime
```

`pkg/ffruntime/load.go`:

```go
package ffruntime

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo"
)

const (
	// AVCodecMajor is FFmpeg 9's libavcodec major.
	AVCodecMajor = 63
	// MinShimAPI is FFSHIM_API_VERSION of ffgo v0.0.0-clustarr.13: an older
	// shim reads FFmpeg 9's structs at FFmpeg 4-7's offsets (spec §7.1 fact 8).
	MinShimAPI = 1
	// Grace is how long Do waits for a call after its context ends: the old
	// subprocess WaitDelay.
	Grace = 5 * time.Second
	// MaxAbandoned outstanding abandoned calls wedge the process.
	MaxAbandoned = 4
)

// Report is what Load found; the library paths are the files the dynamic
// loader mapped (/proc/self/maps), not the names asked for.
type Report struct {
	FFmpegMajor int    `json:"ffmpegMajor"`
	ShimAPI     int    `json:"shimAPI"`
	AVUtil      string `json:"avutil,omitempty"`
	AVCodec     string `json:"avcodec,omitempty"`
	AVFormat    string `json:"avformat,omitempty"`
	ShimPath    string `json:"shimPath,omitempty"`
}

var (
	// ErrUnavailable wraps every reason FFmpeg cannot be used here.
	ErrUnavailable = errors.New("ffruntime: FFmpeg is unavailable")
	// ErrWedged refuses calls once MaxAbandoned are outstanding.
	ErrWedged = errors.New("ffruntime: FFmpeg calls are stuck; restart the process")
	// ErrAbandoned is a call that outlived its context plus Grace.
	ErrAbandoned = errors.New("ffruntime: an FFmpeg call outlived its context and was abandoned")
)

var ffmpegReleases = map[int]int{58: 4, 59: 5, 60: 6, 61: 7, 62: 8, 63: 9}

var (
	loadOnce   sync.Once
	loadReport Report
	loadErr    error
)

// Load loads FFmpeg and the shim once per process and keeps the first
// result: ffgo's own loader remembers a failure and cannot be retried.
func Load() (Report, error) {
	loadOnce.Do(func() { loadReport, loadErr = load(func() ([]byte, error) { return os.ReadFile("/proc/self/maps") }) })
	return loadReport, loadErr
}

func load(maps func() ([]byte, error)) (Report, error) {
	var r Report
	if err := ffgo.Init(); err != nil {
		return r, fmt.Errorf("%w: load the FFmpeg libraries (LD_LIBRARY_PATH): %w", ErrUnavailable, err)
	}
	_, avc, _ := ffgo.Version()
	major := int(avc >> 16)
	r.FFmpegMajor = ffmpegReleases[major]
	if major != AVCodecMajor {
		return r, fmt.Errorf("%w: libavcodec %d is not FFmpeg 9's (%d)", ErrUnavailable, major, AVCodecMajor)
	}
	d := ffgo.Diagnose()
	r.ShimPath = d.ShimPath
	if !d.ShimLoaded {
		return r, fmt.Errorf("%w: no ffgo shim built for FFmpeg 9 was loaded (FFGO_SHIM_DIR): %s", ErrUnavailable, d.ShimError)
	}
	r.ShimAPI = ffgo.ShimAPIVersion()
	if r.ShimAPI < MinShimAPI {
		return r, fmt.Errorf("%w: the ffgo shim %s has API %d; this build needs %d (rebuild libffshim.so from ffgo v0.0.0-clustarr.13)",
			ErrUnavailable, d.ShimPath, r.ShimAPI, MinShimAPI)
	}
	if b, err := maps(); err == nil {
		r.AVUtil, r.AVCodec, r.AVFormat = mapped(b, "libavutil.so"), mapped(b, "libavcodec.so"), mapped(b, "libavformat.so")
		if p := mapped(b, "libffshim.so"); p != "" {
			r.ShimPath = p
		}
	}
	// F13 makes the level effective under a callback: lines above it never
	// reach the trampoline, so a debug line costs no purego callback.
	if err := ffgo.SetLogLevel(ffgo.LogWarning); err != nil {
		return r, fmt.Errorf("%w: set FFmpeg's log level: %w", ErrUnavailable, err)
	}
	return r, nil
}

// mapped is the path of the first mapping whose file name begins with lib,
// so "libavcodec.so" matches libavcodec.so.63.1.100.
func mapped(maps []byte, lib string) string {
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(maps), "\n") {
		f := strings.Fields(line)
		if len(f) < 6 {
			continue
		}
		if p := strings.Join(f[5:], " "); strings.HasPrefix(filepath.Base(p), lib) {
			return p
		}
	}
	return ""
}
```

`pkg/ffruntime/require.go`:

```go
package ffruntime

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/avcodec"
	"github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/avfilter"
	"github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/avformat"
)

// Needs names what a caller asks of FFmpeg, by FFmpeg's names.
type Needs struct{ Demuxers, Decoders, Encoders, Filters []string }

// Require loads FFmpeg (Load) and fails naming every missing piece of n.
func Require(n Needs) error {
	if _, err := Load(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	var missing []string
	for _, d := range n.Demuxers {
		if avformat.FindInputFormat(d) == nil {
			missing = append(missing, "demuxer "+d)
		}
	}
	for _, d := range n.Decoders {
		if avcodec.FindDecoderByName(d) == nil {
			missing = append(missing, "decoder "+d)
		}
	}
	for _, e := range n.Encoders {
		if avcodec.FindEncoderByName(e) == nil {
			missing = append(missing, "encoder "+e)
		}
	}
	for _, f := range n.Filters {
		if avfilter.GetByName(f) == nil {
			missing = append(missing, "filter "+f)
		}
	}
	if len(missing) > 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: this FFmpeg lacks %s", ErrUnavailable, strings.Join(missing, ", "))
	}
	return nil
}
```

`pkg/ffruntime/log.go`:

```go
package ffruntime

import (
	"log/slog"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo"
)

// logRouter is the one FFmpeg log callback a process installs (FFmpeg's
// log callback is process-wide; spec §7.4). Lines at LogError or worse go to
// slog at Warn as "ffmpeg", rate-limited unless muted; every line goes to
// each Capture sink.
type logRouter struct {
	mu        sync.Mutex
	installed bool
	logger    *slog.Logger
	muted     int
	sinks     map[int]func(ffgo.LogLevel, string)
	next      int
	bucket    tokenBucket
}

func newLogRouter(now func() time.Time) *logRouter {
	return &logRouter{sinks: map[int]func(ffgo.LogLevel, string){}, bucket: tokenBucket{rate: 10, burst: 20, tokens: 20, now: now}}
}

var router = newLogRouter(time.Now)

// RouteLog sends FFmpeg's errors to l from now on.
func RouteLog(l *slog.Logger) {
	router.mu.Lock()
	router.logger = l
	router.mu.Unlock()
	router.install()
}

// Capture hands every FFmpeg line to sink until release is called.
func Capture(sink func(ffgo.LogLevel, string)) (release func()) {
	router.install()
	return router.capture(sink)
}

// Mute stops FFmpeg's errors reaching slog until release is called; Capture
// sinks still see them.
func Mute() (release func()) {
	router.install()
	return router.mute()
}

func (r *logRouter) install() {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	if r.installed {
		return
	}
	if err := ffgo.SetLogCallback(r.dispatch); err == nil {
		r.installed = true
	}
}

func (r *logRouter) capture(sink func(ffgo.LogLevel, string)) func() {
	r.mu.Lock()
	id := r.next
	r.next++
	r.sinks[id] = sink
	r.mu.Unlock()
	var once sync.Once
	return func() { once.Do(func() { r.mu.Lock(); delete(r.sinks, id); r.mu.Unlock() }) }
}

func (r *logRouter) mute() func() {
	r.mu.Lock()
	r.muted++
	r.mu.Unlock()
	var once sync.Once
	return func() { once.Do(func() { r.mu.Lock(); r.muted--; r.mu.Unlock() }) }
}

func (r *logRouter) dispatch(level ffgo.LogLevel, msg string) {
	r.mu.Lock()
	sinks := make([]func(ffgo.LogLevel, string), 0, len(r.sinks))
	for _, s := range r.sinks {
		sinks = append(sinks, s)
	}
	logger := r.logger
	toSlog := logger != nil && r.muted == 0 && level <= ffgo.LogError && r.bucket.allow()
	r.mu.Unlock()
	for _, s := range sinks {
		s(level, msg)
	}
	if toSlog {
		logger.Warn("ffmpeg", "level", level.String(), "message", strings.TrimRight(msg, "\n"))
	}
}

// tokenBucket is a burst-then-rate limiter; the caller holds the router's lock.
type tokenBucket struct {
	rate, burst float64
	tokens      float64
	last        time.Time
	now         func() time.Time
}

func (b *tokenBucket) allow() bool {
	t := b.now()
	if !b.last.IsZero() {
		b.tokens = min(b.burst, b.tokens+t.Sub(b.last).Seconds()*b.rate)
	}
	b.last = t
	if b.tokens < 1 {
		return false
	}
	b.tokens--
	return true
}
```
